children.text: Brahma-saṃhitā - Śrī-Jīva-gosvāmi-kṛta-dig-darśanī-ṭīkā-sahitā
children.translated_text: <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> — with the <s>Dig-darśanī</s> commentary composed by <s>Śrī Jīva Gosvāmin</s>

children.text:
īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saccidānanda-vigrahaḥ |
anādir ādir govindaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam ||1|| // BrS_5.1 //
children.translated_text: The Supreme Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose form is <s>saccidānanda</s> (being, consciousness, and bliss). Without beginning, yet the beginning of all, <s>Govinda</s>, the cause of all causes. ||1|| // BrS 5.1 //

children.text: śrī-śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ namaḥ |
children.translated_text: Obeisance to <s>Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: sanātana-samo yasya jyāyān śrīmān sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose elder is the illustrious <s>Sanātana</s>, equal to none—

children.text: śrī-vallabho'nujaḥ so'sau śrī-rūpo jīva-sad-gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, the younger brother of <s>Śrī Vallabha</s> (Anupama), is the true refuge of the <s>jīvas</s> (living beings).

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa-rūpa-mahimā mama citte mahīyatām |
children.translated_text: May the glory of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s form be magnified in my heart,

children.text: yasya prasādād vyākartum icchāmi brahma-saṃhitām ||
children.translated_text: by whose grace I desire to explain the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>.

children.text: duryojanāpi yuktārthā suvicārād ṛṣi-smṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Though difficult to construe, the saying of the sages has a fitting meaning when well examined;

children.text: vicāre tu mamātra syād ṛṣīṇāṃ sa ṛṣir gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in such examination, may the sages' sage be my guide.

children.text: yadyapy adhyāya-śata-yuk saṃhitā sā tathāpy asau |
children.translated_text: Although that <s>saṃhitā</s> (compilation) has a hundred chapters, nevertheless—

children.text: adhyāyaḥ sūtra-rūpatvāt tasyāḥ sarvāṅgatāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that chapter [the fifth], being in the form of <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms), has attained the status of comprising the whole.

children.text: śrīmad-bhāgavatādyeṣu dṛṣṭaḥ yan mṛṣṭa-buddhibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: That which has been perceived in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> and other scriptures by those of refined intellect—

children.text: tad evātra parāmṛṣṭaṃ tato hṛṣṭaṃ mano mama ||
children.translated_text: that very thing is touched upon here; therefore my mind is delighted.

children.text: yad yac chrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe vistārād vinirūpitam |
children.translated_text: Whatever was elaborately established in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Sandarbha</s>—

children.text: atra tat punar āmṛśya vyākhyātuṃ spṛśyate mayā ||
children.translated_text: here, reflecting upon that again, I attempt to explain it.

children.text:
atha śrīmad-bhāgavate yad uktaṃ ete cāṃśa-kalāḥ puṃsaḥ kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān
svayam [BhP 1.3.28] iti tad eva prathamam āha īśvara iti | atra kṛṣṇa ity eva
viśeṣya tan-nāmaiva | kṛṣṇāvatārotsavety ādau
śrī-śukādi-mahājana-prasiddhyā | kṛṣṇāya vāsudevāya devakī-nandanāya
ity ādau sāmopaniṣadi ca | prathama-pratītatvena
tan-nāma-vargāvirbhāva-kṛtā gargeṇa prathamam uddiṣṭatvena tathā yaṃ
mantram adhikṛtya so'yam ārambhaḥ tatrāgrataḥ paricitatvena mūla-rūpatvāt |
tad uktaṃ padma-purāṇe prabhāsa-khaṇḍe nārada-kuśadhvaja-saṃvāde
śrī-bhagavad-uktau - nāmnāṃ mukhyatamaṃ nāma kṛṣṇākhyaṃ me
parantapa iti |
children.translated_text: Now, regarding what was said in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>—'These are the portions and sub-portions of the <s>Puruṣa</s>, but <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the Lord Himself' [BhP 1.3.28]—that very thing is stated first with '<s>Īśvara</s>' etc. Here, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' alone is the subject; that very name itself [is primary], because of the renown among great authorities like <s>Śrī Śuka</s> in [the compound] 'the festival of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s descent,' etc.; in 'To <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to the son of <s>Devakī</s>,' etc., and in the <s>Sāma Upaniṣad</s>; because of its being first apprehended, because of the appearance among the group of His names, because of its being first designated by <s>Garga</s>, and because of its being the root form, well-known from the outset in that mantra concerning which this work begins. Thus it is said in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Prabhāsa-khaṇḍa</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>, in the speech of the Blessed Lord: 'The foremost of all names is the name called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O tormentor of foes.'

children.text: ataiva brahmāṇḍa-purāṇe śrī-kṛṣṇāṣṭottara-śata-nāma-stotre -
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> 108-name hymn—

children.text: sahasra-nāmnāṃ puṇyānāṃ trir-āvṛttyā tu yat phalam |
children.translated_text: The fruit obtained by thrice repeating the thousand holy names—

children.text: ekāvṛttyā tu kṛṣṇasya nāmaikaṃ tat prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: that is bestowed by a single utterance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s name.

children.text:
ity atra śrī-kṛṣṇasyety evoktaṃ yat tv agre govinda-nāmnā stoṣyate tat khalu
kṛṣṇatve'pi tasya gavendratva-vaiśiṣṭya-darśanārtham eva |
children.translated_text: In this passage, 'of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>' is indeed stated; that He will be praised ahead by the name <s>Govinda</s> is only for the purpose of showing the distinction of His being the lord of cows, even while being <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text:
tad evaṃ rūḍhitvena prādhānyāt tasya iśvara ity ādīni viśeṣaṇāni | atha
guṇa-dvārāpi tad dṛśyate | yathāha gargaḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus, because of its being the established conventional term and its primacy, '<s>Īśvara</s>' and the rest are qualifying attributes of Him [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]. Now, this is also seen through the analysis of qualities. As <s>Garga</s> said—

children.text: āsan varṇās trayo hy asya gṛhṇato 'nuyugaṃ tanūḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Your son has had three colors—white, red, and yellow—

children.text: śuklo raktas tathā pīta idānīṃ kṛṣṇatāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: corresponding to the different ages in which He assumed bodies; now He has assumed the dark complexion (<s>kṛṣṇatā</s>).'

children.text: bahūni santi nāmāni rūpāṇi ca sutasya te |
children.translated_text: 'Your son has many names and forms,

children.text: guṇa-karmānurūpāṇi tānya ahaṃ veda no janāḥ || [BhP 10.8.13-14]
children.translated_text: corresponding to His qualities and deeds; I know them, but people do not.' [BhP 10.8.13-14]

children.text:
anayor arthaḥ | asya kṛṣṇatvena dṛśyamānasya prati-yugaṃ tanūr nānāvatārān
gṛhṇataḥ prakāśyataḥ śuklādayas trayo āsan prakāśam avāpuḥ | sa ca sa ca
śuklādir avatāra idānīṃ sākṣād asyāvatāra-samaye kṛṣṇāṅgataḥ etasminn
evāntarbhūtaḥ | ataiva kṛṣṇe kartṛtvāt sarvotkarṣakatvāt kṛṣṇa iti mukhyaṃ
nāma | tasmād asyaiva tāni rūpāṇīty āha bahūnīti | tad evaṃ guṇa-dvārā
tan-nāmni prādhyānya-sūcakasya kṛṣṇasya tan-nāmnaḥ prādhānye labdhe -
children.translated_text: The meaning of these two verses: Of this one who is seen as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in each age, as He assumes bodies—that is, manifests various incarnations—the three colors beginning with white were manifest, came to light. And those white and other incarnations have now, at the very time of this incarnation, entered into <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s own body, being included within this very one. Therefore, because of being the agent in the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and because of being the most excellent of all, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' is the primary name. Therefore, those very forms belong to Him alone—thus He says 'many,' etc. Thus, when the primacy of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s name, which indicates His primacy through qualities, has been established—

children.text: kṛṣir bhū-vācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛtivācakaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣi</s>' is a word denoting existence (<s>bhū</s>), and '<s>ṇa</s>' denotes bliss (<s>nirvṛti</s>);

children.text: tayor aikyaṃ paraṃ brahma kṛṣṇa ity abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: the union of these two is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
iti yoga-vṛttitve tasya tādṛśatvaṃ labhyate | na cedaṃ padyam anya-param |
tad-upāsanā-tantra-gautamīya-tantre aṣṭādaśākṣara-vyākhyāyāṃ tad etat
tulyaṃ padyaṃ dṛśyate -
children.translated_text: By the etymological derivation (<s>yoga-vṛtti</s>), His such nature is obtained. Nor is this verse directed elsewhere. In the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s> dedicated to His worship, in the explanation of the eighteen-syllable mantra, an equivalent verse is seen—

children.text:
kṛṣi-śabdaś ca sattārtho ṇaś cānanda-svarūpakaḥ |
sukha-rūpo bhaved ātmā bhāvānanda-mayatvataḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣi</s>' means 'existence' and '<s>ṇa</s>' is of the form of bliss; the Self would be of the nature of bliss, because of being constituted of the bliss of being.

children.text:
tasmād ayam arthaḥ - bhavanty asmāt sarve'rthā iti bhūḥ dhātv-artha ucyate
bhāva-śadavat sa cātra karṣter evārthas tasyaiva prāptatvāt | gautamīye
bhū-śabdasya sattā-vācakatve'pi tad-dhātv-artha-sattaivocyate | ghaṭatvaṃ
sattā-vācakam ity ukte ghaṭa-sattaiva gamyate na tu paṭa-sattā na vā
sāmānya-satteti |
children.translated_text: Therefore this is the meaning: 'all things come into being from this'—thus '<s>bhū</s>' is said to have the verbal root meaning, like the word '<s>bhāva</s>'; and here the meaning of the root '<s>karṣ</s>' (to attract) alone is obtained, since it has been arrived at. In the <s>Gautamīya</s>, even when the word '<s>bhū</s>' has the meaning of existence, it is the existence of that very root that is spoken of. Just as when the expression 'the existence of a pot' is stated, only the existence of the pot is understood, not the existence of cloth, nor existence in general.

children.text:
atha nivṛttir ānandas tayor aikyaṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyena vyaktaṃ yat paraṃ
brahma sarvato'pi sarvasyāpi bṛṃhaṇaṃ vastu tat bṛhattamaṃ kṛṣṇa ity
abhidhīyate kintu kṛṣer ākarṣa-mātrārthatvena ṇa-śabdasya ca
pratipādyenānandena saha sāmānādhikaraṇyāsambhavād dhetu-mator
abhedopacāraḥ kāryaḥ | tac cākarṣa-prācuryārtham āyur ghṛtam itivat |
brahma-śabdasya tat-tad-arthatvaṃ ca bṛhattvād bṛṃhaṇatvāc ca tad brahma
paramaṃ vidur [ViP 1.12.57] iti viṣṇu-purāṇāt |
children.translated_text: Now, <s>nirvṛti</s> is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss); the union of the two is clearly expressed through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). That which is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>—the greatest of all, the nourisher of everything—that greatest entity is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. However, since '<s>kṛṣi</s>' means only 'attraction' and co-referentiality with the bliss denoted by the suffix '<s>ṇa</s>' is impossible, a figurative identification of cause and effect should be made. And this is for the sake of expressing the abundance of attraction, like '<s>ghee</s> is life.' The word <s>Brahman</s> having various meanings is shown from the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>: 'They know that Supreme <s>Brahman</s> because of its being great and its causing growth' [ViP 1.12.57].

children.text: evam evoktaṃ bṛhad-gautamīye -
children.translated_text: Thus indeed it is stated in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s>—

children.text:
kṛṣi-śabdaś ca sattārtho ṇaś cānanda-svarūpakaḥ |
sattā-svānandayor yogāt cit paraṃ brahma cocyate || iti |
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣi</s>' means 'existence' and '<s>ṇa</s>' is of the form of bliss; from the union of existence and self-bliss, the supreme transcendental <s>Brahman</s> is spoken of.

children.text:
advaya-vādibhir api sattānandayor aikyaṃ tathā mantavyam | śābdikair
bhinnābhidheyatvena pratīteḥ | sattā-śabdena cātra sarveṣāṃ satāṃ
pravṛtti-hetur yat paramaṃ sa tad evocyate | sad eva saumyedam agra āsīd
[Chā 6.2.1] iti śruteḥ | abhinnābhidheyatve'pi vṛkṣas tarur ityvad
viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣyatvāyogād ekasya vaiyarthyāc ca | gautamīyaṃ padyaṃ caiva
vyākhyeyam | pūrvārdhe sarvākarṣaṇa-śakti-viśiṣṭa ānandaḥ kṛṣṇa ity
arthaḥ | uttarārdhe yasmād evaṃ sarvākarṣaka-sukha-rūpo'sau tasmād ātmā
jīvaś ca tatra sukha-rūpo bhavet | tatra hetu-bhāvaḥ premā
tanmayānandatvād iti |
children.translated_text: Even by the <s>Advaitavādins</s> (non-dualists), the identity of existence and bliss should be so understood—because the linguists apprehend them as having different denotations. By the word 'existence' (<s>sattā</s>), what is meant here is that supreme cause of the activity of all existing things. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Being alone, O dear one, this was in the beginning' [Chāndogya 6.2.1]. Even with non-distinct denotation, like '<s>vṛkṣa</s>' and '<s>taru</s>' [both meaning 'tree'], because the relation of qualifier and qualified would be impossible, and because one term would be redundant. The <s>Gautamīya</s> verse should also be explained thus: in the first half, the meaning is '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is bliss endowed with the power of attracting all'; in the second half, because He is thus of the form of all-attracting bliss, the <s>ātman</s> (Self) and <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) also become of the form of bliss therein. The cause of this is <s>prema</s> (divine love), because of being constituted of bliss in absorption with Him.

children.text:
tad evaṃ svarūpa-guṇābhyāṃ parama-bṛhattamaḥ sarvākarṣaka ānandaḥ
kṛṣṇa-śabda-vācya iti jñeyam | sa ca śabdaḥ śrī-devakīnandana eva rūḍhaḥ |
asyaiva sarvānandakatvaṃ vāsudevopaniṣadi dṛṣṭam - devakī-nandano
nikhilam ānandayat iti | āhuś ca nāma-kaumudī-kārāḥ - kṛṣṇa-śabdasya
tamāla-śyāmala-tviṣi śrī-yaśodā-stanandhaye para-brahmaṇi rūḍhiḥ iti | tataś
cāsau śabdo nānyatra saṅkramaṇīyaḥ | yathāha bhaṭṭaḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus it should be known that the one denoted by the word <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is the greatest in essential nature and qualities, the all-attracting, is bliss itself. And that word is conventionally established (<s>rūḍha</s>) as referring to <s>Śrī Devakīnandana</s> (the son of <s>Devakī</s>) alone. His capacity to bring bliss to all is seen in the <s>Vāsudeva Upaniṣad</s>: '<s>Devakī</s>'s son delights all.' And the authors of the <s>Nāma-kaumudī</s> say: 'The word <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has its conventional meaning in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, who has the dark complexion of a <s>tamāla</s> tree, the nursing infant of <s>Śrī Yaśodā</s>.' Therefore that word is not to be transferred elsewhere. As <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> has said—

children.text: labdhātmikā satī rūḍhir bhaved yogāpahāriṇī |
children.translated_text: A conventional meaning (<s>rūḍhi</s>) that has attained its identity overrides the etymological meaning (<s>yoga</s>);

children.text: kalpanīyā tu labhante nātmānaṃ yoga-bādhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: meanings that have to be imagined do not attain their identity, due to the obstruction by etymological meaning.

children.text:
iti para-brahmatvaṃ ca śrīmad-bhāgavate gūḍhaṃ paraṃ brahma
manuṣya-liṅgam [BhP 7.15.58] iti, yan-mitraṃ paramānandaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahma
sanātanam iti [BhP 10.14.32] | śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe - yatrāvatīrṇaṃ kṛṣṇākhyaṃ
paraṃ brahma narākṛti [ViP 4.11.2] iti | śrī-gītāsu ca brahmaṇo hi
pratiṣṭhāham [Gītā 14.27] iti | śrī-gopāla-tāpanīṣu ca yo'sau paraṃ brahma
gopālaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: And His being the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> [is shown] in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>: 'the hidden Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form' [BhP 7.15.58]; 'whose friend is the supreme bliss, the full, eternal <s>Brahman</s>' [BhP 10.14.32]. In the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>: 'where descended that which is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form' [ViP 4.11.2]. And in the <s>Śrī Gītā</s>: 'I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>' [Gītā 14.27]. And in the <s>Śrī Gopāla-tāpanī</s> [Upaniṣad]: 'He who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Gopāla</s>.'

children.text:
atha mūlam anusarāmaḥ | yasmād eva tādṛk kṛṣṇa-śabda-vācyas tasmād
īśvaraḥ sarva-vaśāyitā | tad idam upalakṣitaṃ bṛhad-gautamīye
kṛṣṇa-śabdasyaivārthāntareṇa |
children.translated_text: Now let us follow the root text. Since the one denoted by such a word <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is so, He is '<s>Īśvara</s>' (the supreme controller), the subjugator of all. This is indicated in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s> by yet another meaning of the word <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—

children.text:
athavā karṣayet sarvaṃ jagat sthāvara-jaṅgamam |
kāla-rūpeṇa bhagavān tenāyaṃ kṛṣṇa ucyate || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Or else, He draws to Himself everything in the world, moving and non-moving, in the form of Time—the Blessed Lord—therefore He is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text:
kalayati niyamayati sarvam iti kāla-śabdārthaḥ | tathā ca tṛtīye tam
uddiśoddhavasya pūrṇa eva nirṇayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The meaning of the word <s>kāla</s> (time): He measures, that is, regulates everything. And thus, in the Third Canto [of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>], with reference to Him, is <s>Uddhava</s>'s complete conclusion—

children.text:
svayaṃ tv asāmyātiśayas tryadhīśaḥ
svārājya-lakṣmy-āpta-samasta-kāmaḥ |
baliṃ haradbhiś cira-loka-pālaiḥ
kirīṭa-koṭy-eḍita-pāda-pīṭhaḥ || [BhP 3.2.21] iti |
children.translated_text: whose footstool is honored by the crests of the crowns of the eternal world-guardians who bring Him tribute' [BhP 3.2.21].
'He Himself, unequalled and unsurpassed, the lord of the three worlds, having attained all desires through the splendor of His sovereign majesty,

children.text:
śrī-gītāsu viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat [Gītā 10.42] iti |
śrī-gopāla-tāpanyām-eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣṇa īḍyaḥ [GTU 1.19] iti | yasmād
eva tādṛg-īśvaraḥ, tasmāt paramaḥ | sarvotkṛṣṭā mā lakṣmī-rūpāḥ śaktayo
yasmin | tad uktaṃ śrī-bhāgavate --reme ramābhir nija-kāma-samplutaḥ
[BhP 10.59.43] iti | nāyaṃ śriyo'ṅga u nitānta-rateḥ prasādaḥ [BhP 10.47.60]
ityādi | tatrātiśuśubhe tābhir bhagavān devakī-sutaḥ [BhP 10.33.6] iti | tābhir
vidhūta-śokābhir bhagavān acyuto vṛtaḥ | vyarocatādhikam [BhP 10.32.20] iti
children.translated_text: surrounded by them whose grief was dispelled, the Lord <s>Acyuta</s> shone even more [BhP 10.32.20].

children.text:
ca | atraivāgre vakṣyate - śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ [BrahmaS
5.56] iti | tāpanyāṃ ca -kṛṣṇo vai paramaṃ daivatam [GTU 1.3] iti | yasmād eva
tādṛk paramas tasmād ādiś ca | tad uktaṃ śrī-daśame -
children.translated_text: And here ahead it will be stated: 'The beloved consorts are the <s>Śrīs</s> (goddesses of fortune), and the supreme Person is their beloved' [<s>BrahmaS</s> 5.56]. And in the <s>Tāpanī</s>: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed the supreme deity' [GTU 1.3]. Since He is such a supreme one, He is also the original (<s>ādi</s>). As stated in the Śrī Tenth [Canto]:

In the Śrī <s>Gītā</s>: 'I stand pervading this entire universe with a single portion [of Myself]' [<s>Gītā</s> 10.42]. In the Śrī <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s>: 'The one controller, all-pervading, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worthy of worship' [GTU 1.19]. Since He is such a Lord, therefore He is supreme. [He is one] in whom reside the highest powers in the form of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (<s>śaktis</s>). As stated in the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s>: 'He sported with the <s>Ramās</s> (goddesses of fortune), immersed in His own desire' [BhP 10.59.43]. 'This is not the grace of <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune), O friend, from her constant devotion' [BhP 10.47.60] and so forth. 'There, the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), the son of <s>Devakī</s>, was exceedingly resplendent among them' [BhP 10.33.6]. Among them,

children.text: śrutvājitaṃ jarāsandhaṃ nṛpater dhyāyato hariḥ |
āhopāyaṃ tam evādya uddhavo yam uvāca ha || [BhP 10.72.15] iti |
children.translated_text: spoke the very means that <s>Uddhava</s> had previously spoken. [BhP 10.72.15]
Hearing that <s>Jarāsandha</s> was undefeated, while the king was pondering, <s>Hari</s>

children.text:
ṭīkā ca svāmi-pādānām - ādyo hariḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa ity eṣā | ekādaśe tu tasya
śreṣṭhatvam ādyatvaṃ ca yugapad āha | puruṣam ṛṣabham ādyaṃ
kṛṣṇa-saṃjñaṃ nato'smi iti |
children.translated_text: And the commentary of the venerable <s>Svāmī-pāda</s> [<s>Śrīdhara Svāmī</s>]: 'The original (<s>ādya</s>) <s>Hari</s> is Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — this is the meaning. And in the Eleventh [Canto], His supremacy and originality are simultaneously stated: 'I bow to the supreme, original Person named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text:
na caitad āditvaṃ tad-avatārāpekṣaṃ kintu anādi na vidyate ādir yasya
tādṛśaḥ | tāpanyāṃ ca -- eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣṇa īḍyaḥ ity uktvāha nityo
nityānām iti ca yasmād eva tādṛśatayā ādis tasmāt sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam |
tathā ca daśame taṃ prati devakī-vākyam -
children.translated_text: And this originality (<s>āditva</s>) is not relative to His incarnations, but rather [means] one who has no beginning (<s>anādi</s>). And in the <s>Tāpanī</s>: having said 'The one controller, all-pervading, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worthy of worship,' it states 'the eternal among eternals.' Since He is of such nature as the original, therefore He is the cause of all causes. And so in the Tenth [Canto], the words of <s>Devakī</s> to Him:

children.text: yasyāṃśāṃśāṃśa-bhāgena viśvotpatti-layodayāḥ |
bhavanti kila viśvātmaṃs taṃ tvādyāhaṃ gatiṃ gatā || [BhP 10.85.31] iti |
children.translated_text: take place — O Soul of the universe, I have taken refuge in You, the original. [BhP 10.85.31]
By a fraction of a fraction of a fraction of whose portion, the creation, dissolution, and sustenance of the universe

children.text:
ṭīkā ca - yasyāṃśaḥ puruṣas tasyāṃśo māyā tasyā aṃśā guṇās teṣāṃ
bhāgena paramāṇu-mātra-leśena viśvotpatty-ādayo bhavanti | taṃ tvā tvāṃ
gatiṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāsmi ity eṣā | tathā ca brahma-stutau - nārāyaṇo'ṅga
nara-bhū-jalāyanāt [BhP 10.14.3] iti |
children.translated_text: And the commentary: 'Whose portion (<s>aṃśa</s>) is the <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose portion is <s>Māyā</s>, whose portions are the <s>guṇas</s> — by a fraction, by the merest atomic particle of these, the creation of the universe, etc., take place. To You (tvā), I have gone to You as refuge (<s>gati</s>)' — this is the meaning. And in <s>Brahmā</s>'s prayer: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, O friend, [so called] from the waters born of the cosmic person' [BhP 10.14.3].

children.text: narāj jātāni tattvāni nārāṇīti vidur budhāḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise know that the elements born from <s>Nara</s> are called <s>Nārāṇi</s>;

children.text: tasya tāny ayanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His being their resting place (<s>ayana</s>) is primary; hence He is called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text:
ity anena lakṣito yo nārāyaṇaḥ sa tavāṅgaṃ tvaṃ punar aṅgīty arthaḥ |
śrī-gītāsu viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat iti | tad evaṃ
kṛṣṇa-śabdasya yaugikārtho'pi sādhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who is indicated by this [verse] is Your limb (<s>aṅga</s>); but You are the principal body (<s>aṅgī</s>) — this is the meaning. In the Śrī <s>Gītā</s>: 'I stand pervading this entire universe with a single portion.' Thus the etymological meaning of the word <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is also established.

children.text:
ye ca tac-chabdena kṛṣiṇābhyāṃ paramānanda-mātraṃ vācayanti te'pi
īśvarādi-viśeṣaṇais tatra svābhāvikī śaktiṃ manyeran | tasmin na
dvitīyatvena sarva-kāraṇatvena ca vastv-antara-śaktiṃ manyeran | tasmin na
dvitīyatvena sarva-kāraṇatvena ca vastv-antara-śakty-āropāyogāt | tathā ca
śrutiḥ - ānando brahma iti | ko hy evānyāt kaḥ prāṇyād yad eṣa ākāśa
ānando na syāt | ānandād dhīmāni bhūtāni jāyante | [TaittU 2.7.1]
children.translated_text: And those who, by the word consisting of <s>kṛṣ</s> and <s>ṇa</s>, express 'supreme bliss alone' — they too, by the qualifiers such as 'Lord' (<s>Īśvara</s>), would accept the inherent power (<s>svābhāvikī śakti</s>) therein. Because it is impossible to superimpose the power of another entity upon that [<s>Brahman</s>] which is non-dual and the cause of all. And so the <s>śruti</s>: 'Bliss is <s>Brahman</s>' [<s>TaittU</s>]. 'Who indeed could breathe, who could live, if this bliss were not in space? From bliss indeed are these beings born.' [<s>TaittU</s> 2.7.1]

children.text:
na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate
na tat-samaś cābhyadhikaś ca dṛśyate |
parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate
svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca || [ŚvetU 6.8] iti |
children.translated_text: inherent, comprising knowledge, strength, and action. [<s>ŚvetU</s> 6.8]
No work or instrument of His is found, nor is anyone seen equal to or greater than Him. His supreme power is heard of as manifold,

children.text:
nanu sva-mate yoga-vṛttau ca sarvākarṣakaṃ parama-bṛhattamānandaḥ kṛṣṇa
ity abhidhānāt avigraha eva sa ity avagamyate ānandasya vigrahānavagamāt |
satyam | kintv ayaṃ paramo'pūrvaḥ pūrva-siddhānanda-vigrahaḥ iti |
sac-cid-ānanda-lakṣaṇo yo vigrahas tad-rūpa evety arthaḥ | tathā ca
śrī-daśame brahmaṇaḥ stave tvayy eva nitya-sukha-bodha-tanāv iti |
tāpanī-hayaśīrṣayor api - sac-cid-ānanada-rūpāya kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭa-kāriṇe iti |
brahmāṇḍe ca śrī-kṛṣṇāṣṭottara-śata-nāma-stotre nanda-vraja-janānandī
sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Objection: In your own view, since in the <s>yoga-vṛtti</s> (yogic state), <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is described as 'the supreme, greatest bliss that attracts all,' it is understood that He is formless, since bliss is not understood to have a form. True. But this supreme, unprecedented [Being] has a form that is pre-established bliss (<s>pūrva-siddha-ānanda-vigraha</s>). The form characterized by existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda</s>) is of that very nature — this is the meaning. And so in the Śrī Tenth [Canto], in <s>Brahmā</s>'s prayer: 'In You, the embodiment of eternal bliss and knowledge.' And in the <s>Tāpanī</s> and <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> [<s>Pañcarātra</s>] as well: 'To <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose form is existence-consciousness-bliss, who acts without effort.' And in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, in the hymn of 108 names of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'The bliss of the people of <s>Nanda</s>'s <s>Vraja</s>, whose form is existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha</s>).'

children.text:
etad uktaṃ bhavati | sattvaṃ khalv avyabhicāritvam ucyate tad-rūpatvaṃ ca tasya
śrī-daśame brahmādi-vākye -
children.translated_text: This is what is stated: <s>Sattva</s> (truth/goodness) is said to be 'unfailing' — it is His being of that very nature. And in the Śrī Tenth [Canto], in the statement of <s>Brahmā</s> and others:

children.text: satye pratiṣṭhitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ satyam atra pratiṣṭhitam |
satyāt satyaṃ ca govindas tasmāt satyo hi nāmataḥ || [Mbh 5.68.12] iti |
children.translated_text: From truth comes truth — <s>Govinda</s>; therefore He is called 'true' by name. [Mbh 5.68.12]
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is established in truth, and truth is established in Him.

children.text: śrī-devakī-vākye ca --
children.translated_text: And in the words of Śrī <s>Devakī</s>:

children.text: naṣṭe loke dvi-parārdhāvasāne
children.translated_text: When the world is destroyed at the end of two <s>parārdhas</s> (half of Brahmā's lifespan),

children.text: mahā-bhūteṣv ādi-bhūtaṃ gateṣu |
children.translated_text: when the great elements have merged into the primordial element,

children.text: vyakte 'vyaktaṃ kāla-vegena yāte
children.translated_text: when the manifest has gone into the unmanifest by the force of time,

children.text: bhavān ekaḥ śiṣyate 'śeṣa-saṃjñaḥ || [BhP 10.3.25]
children.translated_text: You alone remain, known as 'the remainder' (<s>Śeṣa</s>). [BhP 10.3.25]

children.text:
martyo mṛtyu-vyāla-bhītaḥ palāyan
lokān sarvān nirbhayaṃ nādyagacchat |
tat-pādābjaṃ prāpya yadṛcchayādya
svasthaḥ śete mṛtyur asmād apaiti || [BhP 10.3.24] ity ādi |
children.translated_text: he sleeps peacefully; death flees from him. [BhP 10.3.24] And so forth.
The mortal, terrified of the serpent of death, fleeing, could not find fearlessness in any world. Having attained His lotus feet by chance,

children.text:
eko'si prathamam [BhP 10.14.18] ity ādi śrī-brahmaṇo vākye tad amitaṃ
brahmādvayaṃ śiṣyate iti | śrī-gītāsu brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham iti |
children.translated_text: In the statement of Śrī <s>Brahmā</s> beginning with 'You are one, the first' [BhP 10.14.18]: 'That immeasurable, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> alone remains.' In the Śrī <s>Gītā</s>: 'I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text:
yasmāt kṣaram atīto'ham akṣarād api cottamaḥ |
ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Veda</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person).' [<s>Gītā</s> 15.18]

children.text: tāpanyām -
children.translated_text: In the <s>Tāpanī</s>:

children.text:
janma-jarābhyāṃ bhinnaḥ sthānur ayam acchedyo'yaṃ yo'sau saurye tiṣṭhati |
yo'sau goṣu tiṣṭhati, yo'sau gāḥ pālayati, yo'sau gopeṣu tiṣṭhati govindān
mṛtyur bibheti || [GTU 2.23] ity ādi ca | tatra pūrvatra saurya iti | saurī
yamunā, tad adūra-deśe vṛndāvane ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Free from birth and old age, this one is permanent, indestructible — He who stands in <s>Saurya</s> (on the banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>), who stands among the cows, who protects the cows, who stands among the cowherds — from <s>Govinda</s>, death fears.' [GTU 2.23] And so forth. There, in the former [passage], '<s>Saurya</s>' means: <s>Saurī</s> is the <s>Yamunā</s>; [<s>Saurya</s> means] in the area near it, i.e., in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atha cid-rūpatvaṃ sva-prakāśatvena para-prakāśatvam | tac coktaṃ śrī-daśame
brahmaṇā ekas tvam ātmā ity ādau svayaṃ jyotīr iti | tāpanyāṃ -
children.translated_text: Now, His nature as consciousness (<s>cid-rūpatva</s>) means self-luminosity and the illumination of others. And this is stated in the Śrī Tenth [Canto] by <s>Brahmā</s>, beginning with 'You are the one Self,' [continuing with] 'self-luminous.' In the <s>Tāpanī</s>:

children.text:
yo brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ
yo vidyāstasmai gopāyati sma kṛṣṇaḥ |
taṃ ha daivamātmabuddhiprakāśaṃ
mumukṣurvai śaraṇamanuvrajeta || [GTU 1.26] iti |
children.translated_text: The one seeking liberation should take refuge in that divine Being, the illuminator of self-knowledge. [GTU 1.26]
He who formerly created <s>Brahmā</s>, who protects the <s>Vedas</s> for him — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text:
na cakṣuṣā paśyati rūpam asya
yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas
tasyaiṣa ātmā vṛṇute tanuṃ svām || ity śruty-antaravat |
children.translated_text: 'The eye does not see His form; He is attainable only by him whom this [Self] chooses — to such a one this Self reveals His own form.' As in another <s>śruti</s>.

children.text:
yathānanda-svarūpatvaṃ sarvāṃśena nirupādhi-parama-premāspadatvam | tac
ca śrī-daśame brahma-stavānte - brahman parodbhave kṛṣṇe [BhP 10.14.49]
ity-ādi-praśnottarayor vyaktam | tathā cānubhūtam ānakadundubhinā --
children.translated_text: Just as His nature is bliss (<s>ānanda-svarūpatva</s>), [it means] being the object of unconditional supreme love (<s>prema</s>) in all aspects. And this is evident in the Śrī Tenth [Canto], in the questions and answers at the end of <s>Brahmā</s>'s prayer, beginning with 'O <s>Brahman</s>, in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who is the supreme source' [BhP 10.14.49]. And it was directly experienced by <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>):

children.text: vidito 'si bhavān sākṣāt puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
kevalānubhavānanda- svarūpaḥ sarva-buddhi-dṛk || [BhP 10.3.13] iti |
children.translated_text: whose very form is the bliss of pure experience, the witness of all intelligence.' [BhP 10.3.13]
'You are known directly as the Person beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature),

children.text: ānandaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ iti śruty-antaravat |
children.translated_text: 'Bliss is the form of <s>Brahman</s>' — as in another <s>śruti</s>.

children.text:
tad evaṃ tasya sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha-rūpatve siddhe, vigraha evātmā
tathātmaiva vigraha iti siddham | tato jīvavad dehitvaṃ tasya nety api
siddhāntitam | yathoktaṃ śrī-śukena -
children.translated_text: Thus, when it is established that His nature is a form of existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha</s>), the form itself is the Self, and the Self itself is the form — this is established. Therefore, unlike the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), His embodiment is not [a material covering] — this too is conclusively determined. As stated by Śrī <s>Śuka</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇam enam avehi tvam ātmānam akhilātmanām |
jagad-dhitāya so'py atra dehīvābhāti māyayā || [BhP 10.14.55] iti |
children.translated_text: For the welfare of the world, He too appears here as if embodied, by [His] grace.' [BhP 10.14.55]
'Know this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to be the Self of all selves.

children.text:
tathāpi tasya dehival-līlā-kṛpā-paravaśatayaivety arthaḥ | māyā dambhe
kṛpāyāṃ ca iti viśva-prakāśaḥ | tad evam asya tathā
tathā-lakṣaṇa-śrī-kṛṣṇa-rūptave siddhe cobhaya-līlābhiniviṣṭatvena kvacid
vṛṣṇīndratvaṃ kvacid govindatvaṃ ca dṛśyate | tathāha dvādaśe śrī-sūtaḥ --
children.translated_text: Yet His play as if embodied is solely due to being under the sway of compassionate pastimes (<s>līlā</s>) — this is the meaning. '<s>Māyā</s> [means] pretense and compassion' — thus the <s>Viśva-prakāśa</s> dictionary. Thus, when His identity as Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of such-and-such characteristics is established, and being immersed in both [types of] pastimes, sometimes His identity as the chief of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> is seen, and sometimes His identity as <s>Govinda</s>. So states Śrī <s>Sūta</s> in the Twelfth [Canto]:

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇa-sakha-vṛṣṇy-ṛṣabhāvani-dhrug-
rājanya-vaṃśa-dahanānapavargya-vīrya |
govinda gopa-vanitā-vraja-bhṛtya-gīta-
tīrtha-śravaḥ śravaṇa-maṅgala pāhi bhṛtyān || [BhP 12.11.25] iti |
children.translated_text: O <s>Govinda</s>, whose holy fame is sung by the cowherd women of <s>Vraja</s>, whose name is purifying to hear — protect Your servants!' [BhP 12.11.25]
'O Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), foremost of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, O You who destroyed the irreligious kings of the earth, whose valor leads to liberation,

children.text:
tad evam api svābhīṣṭa-rūpa-līlā-parikara-viśiṣṭatayā govindatvam eva
svārādhyatvena yojayati govinda iti | yathā atraivāgre stoṣyate
cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa iti | abhiṣekānte govinda iti
cābhyadhāt [BhP 10.27.23] ity uktvā tat prakaraṇārambhe śrī-śuka-prārthanā
prīyān na indro gavām [BhP 10.26.25] iti gavāṃ sarvāśrayatvād
gavendratvenaiva sarvendratva-siddheḥ | na cedaṃ nyūnaṃ mantavyam | tathā
hi go-sūktam -
children.translated_text: Even so, by the distinction of his own desired form, pastimes, and associates, he establishes his nature as <s>Govinda</s> as the object of his own worship, [indicated by the word] '<s>Govinda</s>.' As will be praised later here itself: 'In the abodes made of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems), with <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling trees)...' Having said 'At the conclusion of the anointing, he addressed him as <s>Govinda</s>' [BhP 10.27.23], at the beginning of that section, <s>Śrī Śuka</s>'s prayer: 'May the <s>Indra</s> (lord) of the cows be pleased' [BhP 10.26.25] — since by being the shelter of all cows, lordship over all is established through lordship over cows alone. This should not be considered inferior. For thus the <s>Go-sūkta</s> (Hymn of the Cow) says:

children.text:
gobhyo yajñāḥ pravartante gobhyo devāḥ samutthitāḥ |
gobhir vedāḥ samudgīrṇāḥ ṣaḍ-aṅga-padaka-kramāḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: From cows, sacrifices proceed; from cows, the gods arise; from cows, the <s>Vedas</s> were proclaimed, along with their six limbs in proper order.

children.text:
astu tāvat parama-golokāvatīrṇānāṃ tāsāṃ gavām indratvam iti tāpanīṣu ca
brahmaṇā tadīyam eva svenārādhanaṃ prakāśitam -- govindaṃ
sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaṃ vṛndāvana-sura-bhūruha-talāsīnaṃ satataṃ
samarud-gaṇo'haṃ toṣayāmi | [GTU 1.37] iti |
children.translated_text: together with the host of <s>Maruts</s>, I satisfy [him].' [GTU 1.37]

So be it — the lordship over those cows who have descended from the supreme <s>Goloka</s>. And in the <s>Tāpanīya Upaniṣads</s>, by <s>Brahmā</s> himself, his own worship was revealed: '<s>Govinda</s>, whose form is <s>sac-cid-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), seated beneath the divine wish-fulfilling trees of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, always

children.text:
tathaiva daśame -- tad bhūri bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyām
[BhP 10.14.34] ity ādi, śrī-nanda-nandanatvenaiva ca taṃ labdhuṃ prārthanā |
naumīḍya te'bhra-vapuṣe taḍid-ambarāya ity ādi paśupāṅgajāya [BhP 10.14.1]
iti |
tad evaṃ govinda-śabdasya nānā-pāramaiśvarya-mayy anyārthatāpi tena
nābhimatā | tathā coktaṃ - īśvaratve
parameśvaratvānuvāda-pūrvaka-tātparyāvasānatayā gautamīya-tantre
śrīmad-daśākṣara-mantrārtha-kathane -
children.translated_text: Similarly in the Tenth [Canto]: 'That great fortune, any birth in this forest' [BhP 10.14.34] and so on, and the prayer to attain him precisely as the son of <s>Śrī Nanda</s>. 'I bow to the praiseworthy one whose body is like a cloud, whose garment is like lightning' and so on, 'to the son of the cowherd' [BhP 10.14.1]. Thus, even though the word '<s>Govinda</s>' has various other meanings related to supreme lordship, these are not intended by him. And thus it is said — in [the discussion of] lordship, with the conclusion being established through the restatement of supreme lordship — in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>, in the explanation of the meaning of the sacred ten-syllable <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: gopīti prakṛtiṃ vidyāj janas tattva-samūhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: By '<s>gopī</s>' one should understand <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature); 'people' refers to the aggregate of principles (<s>tattvas</s>);

children.text: anayor āśrayo vyāptyā kāraṇatvena ceśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: the shelter of these two, by pervading and being the cause, is <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord);

children.text: sāndrānandaṃ paraṃ jyotir vallabhatvena kathyate ||
children.translated_text: the concentrated bliss, the supreme light, is spoken of as the Beloved (<s>Vallabha</s>).

children.text: athavā gopī prakṛtir janas tad-aṃśa-maṇḍalam |
children.translated_text: Or, '<s>gopī</s>' is <s>prakṛti</s> (nature); 'people' is the circle of his portions;

children.text: anayor vallabhaḥ proktaḥ svāmī kṛṣṇākhya īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the beloved of these two is said to be the master, the Lord named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: kārya-kāraṇayor īśaḥ śrutibhis tena gīyate ||
children.translated_text: He is sung by the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) as the Lord of both effect and cause.

children.text: aneka-janma-siddhānāṃ gopīnāṃ patir eva vā |
children.translated_text: Or, he is indeed the lord of the <s>gopīs</s> who have attained perfection through many births;

children.text: nanda-nandana ity uktas trailokyānanda-vardhanaḥ || iti.
children.translated_text: he is called the son of <s>Nanda</s>, the increaser of the bliss of the three worlds.

children.text:
prakṛtim iti māyākhyāṃ jagat-kāraṇa-śaktim ity arthaḥ tattva-samūhako
mahad-ādi-rūpaḥ | anayor āśrayaḥ sāndrānandaṃ paraṃ jyotir īśvarao
vallabha-śabdena kathyate | īśvaratve hetur vyāptyā kāraṇatvena ceti |
prakṛtir iti svarūpa-bhūtā māyātītā vaikuṇṭhādau prakāśamānā
mahā-lakṣmy-ākhyā śaktir ity arthaḥ | aṃśa-maṇḍalaṃ saṅkarṣaṇādi-rūpam |
aneka-janma-siddhānām ity atra | bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna
[Gītā 4.5] iti śrī-bhagavad-gītā-vacanām anādi-janma-paramparāyām eva
tātparyam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Prakṛti</s>' means the power called <s>māyā</s>, the causal energy of the universe; the 'aggregate of principles' refers to <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) and so forth. The shelter of these two — the concentrated bliss, the supreme light, the Lord — is spoken of by the word '<s>Vallabha</s>' (beloved). The reason for lordship is pervading and being the cause. '<s>Prakṛti</s>' here means the energy that is part of his essential nature, transcending <s>māyā</s>, manifesting in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and elsewhere, called <s>Mahā-Lakṣmī</s>. The 'circle of portions' refers to <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and so forth. Regarding 'those who have attained perfection through many births' — the statement of the <s>Śrī Bhagavad-gītā</s>, 'Many births of mine have passed, and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>' [Gītā 4.5], has its purport in the beginningless succession of births.

children.text:
tad evam atrāpi nanda-nandanatvam evābhimataṃ śrī-gargeṇa ca yathoktam |
prāg ayaṃ vāsudevasya kvacij jātas tavātmajaḥ [BhP 10.8.14] iti | ātmajatvaṃ
hi tasya śrī-vasudevasyāpi manasy āvirbhūtatvam evābhimatam |
āviveśāṃśa-bhāgena mana ānakadundubheḥ [BhP 10.2.16] iti | śrī-devakyām
api dadhāra sarvātmakam ātma-bhūtaṃ kāṣṭhā yathānanda-karaṃ manastaḥ
[BhP 10.2.18] ity ādeḥ | śrī-vrajeśvarayo'pi tathāsīd eva phalena
phala-kāraṇam anumīyate | śrī-bhagavat-prādurbhāvasya
pūrvāvyavahita-kālaṃ vyāpya tathā tathā sarvatra darśanāt | kintv ātmani
tasyāvirbhāve saty apy ātmajatvāya pitṛ-bhāva-maya-śuddha-mahā-premaiva
prayojakam | brahmaṇaḥ sakāśād varāha-devasyāvirbhāve'pi parasparaṃ tathā
bhāva-darśanābhāvāt | tathā nṛsiṃha-devaḥ stambhayor api | na ca vaktavyam
udara-praveśe sati putratvaṃ syāt | parīkṣid-rakṣaṇārthaṃ tan-mātur
udara-praviṣṭe ca tayos tādṛśa-vyavahārābhāvāt | tasmāt
vātsalyābhidha-premaiva putratve kāraṇam | tādṛśa-śuddha-premā tu
śrī-vrajeśvarayor eva śrī-vasudeva-devakyos tu paramaiśvarya-jñānaṃ
pratibandhakaṃ iti sādhūktaṃ prāg ayaṃ vasudevasya iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, here too, his nature as the son of <s>Nanda</s> is what is intended, as stated by <s>Śrī Garga</s> as well: 'Previously, this son of yours was born somewhere as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>' [BhP 10.8.14]. For his sonship — even regarding <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> — is understood as a manifestation in the mind. 'He entered with a portion of his portion into the mind of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (Vasudeva)' [BhP 10.2.16]. In <s>Śrī Devakī</s> also: 'She held the all-pervading one, self-born, bliss-giving, within her mind, like a wooden sheath' [BhP 10.2.18] and so on. For the lord and lady of <s>Vraja</s> too, it was similarly so — the cause is inferred from the effect, since it is seen everywhere pervading the time immediately preceding the Lord's manifestation. But even though he manifests within the self, the impelling cause for his sonship is pure great love imbued with parental affection (<s>vātsalya</s>) alone — since even though <s>Varāha-deva</s> appeared from <s>Brahmā</s>, there is no evidence of such mutual parental feeling between them; similarly with <s>Nṛsiṃha-deva</s> and the pillar. And it should not be said that entering the womb would make one a son, since even though [the Lord] entered the womb of <s>Parīkṣit</s>'s mother for the purpose of protecting him, there was no such relationship between them. Therefore, love called <s>vātsalya</s> (parental affection) alone is the cause of sonship. Such pure love belonged to the lord and lady of <s>Vraja</s> alone; for <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>, knowledge of supreme lordship was an obstacle. Thus it is well said: 'Previously this [was the son] of <s>Vasudeva</s>.'

children.text:
atha śrī-śukadevena tathaiva nirṇītaṃ nāyaṃ sukhāpo bhagavān dehināṃ
gopikā-sutaḥ [BhP 10.9.21] iti | āgama-vidbhir api sakala-loka-maṅgalo
nanda-gopa-tanayo devatā iti | ataḥ śrīmad-daśākṣara-viniyoge'pi tan-maya
eva dṛśyate iti | atha viśeṣaḥ śrī-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇyāṃ nandas tv ātmaja
utpannaḥ [BhP 10.5.1] ity ādau draṣṭavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śrī Śukadeva</s> similarly determined: 'This Lord, the son of a <s>gopī</s>, is not easily attained by embodied beings' [BhP 10.9.21]. Even by those who know the <s>āgamas</s>: 'The auspiciousness of all worlds, the son of <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd, is the deity.' Therefore, even in the application of the sacred ten-syllable [mantra], it is seen to be pervaded by him. The specific details should be seen in the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s>, beginning with 'A son was born to <s>Nanda</s>' [BhP 10.5.1].

children.text:
sahasra-patra-kamalaṃ gokulākhyaṃ mahat padam |
tat-karṇikāraṃ tad-dhāma tad-anantāṃśa-sambhavam ||2|| // BrS_5.2 //
children.translated_text: The thousand-petaled lotus named <s>Gokula</s> is the great abode; its pericarp is that dwelling, born from a portion of <s>Ananta</s>. ||2||

children.text:
atha tasya tad-rūpatā-sādhakaṃ nityaṃ dhāma pratipādayati sahasra-patraṃ
kamalam ity ādinā | sahasrāṇi patrāṇi yatra tat kamalam | bhūmiś
cintāmaṇi-gaṇamayīti vakṣyamāṇānusāreṇa cintāmaṇi-mayaṃ padmaṃ
tad-rūpaṃ mahat sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ padaṃ sthānam | mahataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya
mahā-bhagavato vā padaṃ mahā-vaikuṇṭhādi-rūpaṃ ity arthaḥ | rūḍhir
yogam apaharatīti nyāyena tasyaiva pratīteḥ | etad abhipretyoktaṃ śrī-daśame
bhagavān gokuleśvaraḥ iti śīlārthe tv atra varac-pratyayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, establishing his eternal abode which manifests his form, [the author says] beginning with 'the thousand-petaled lotus.' That lotus in which there are thousands of petals. In accordance with what will be stated — that the ground is made of hosts of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems) — the lotus made of <s>cintāmaṇi</s>; that form, the great, most excellent abode. The abode of the great one, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, or of the Supreme Lord, in the form of <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha</s> and so on — this is the meaning. By the principle 'conventional meaning overrides etymological meaning,' this alone is understood. With this intention it is said in the Tenth [Canto]: 'The Lord, the ruler of <s>Gokula</s>.' Here the suffix '-vara' is used in the sense of temperament.

children.text:
ataiva tad-anukūlatvenottara-grantho'pi vyākhyeyaḥ | tad eva cāmnātaṃ
gokulaṃ vana-vaikuṇṭham iti | tasya śrī-kṛṣṇasya dhāma
śrī-nanda-yaśodādibhiḥ saha vāsa-yogyaṃ mahāntaḥ-puraṃ taiḥ
sahavāsitātvagre samuddekṣyate | tasya svarūpam āha tad iti | anantasya
śrī-baladevasyāṃśena jyotir-vibhāga-viśeṣeṇa sambhavaḥ sadāvirbhāvo yasya
tat tathā tantreṇaitad api bodhyate | ananto'ṃśo yasya tasya śrī-baladevasyāpi
sambhavo nivāso yatra tad iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the subsequent text too should be interpreted in accordance with that. And that very [<s>Gokula</s>] is traditionally declared to be '<s>Gokula</s>, the forest-<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.' His, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s, abode — the great inner palace fit for dwelling together with <s>Śrī Nanda</s>, <s>Yaśodā</s>, and others — their co-residence will be shown further on. He describes its essential nature with the word 'tat' (that): that which has its perpetual manifestation through a special division of light, by a portion of <s>Ananta</s>, that is, <s>Śrī Baladeva</s>. This is also to be understood through the <s>Tantra</s>. That in which there is the abode or manifestation of <s>Śrī Baladeva</s>, of whom <s>Ananta</s> is a portion.

children.text: karṇikāraṃ mahad yantraṃ ṣaṭ-koṇaṃ vajra-kīlakam |
ṣaḍ-aṅga-ṣaṭ-padī-sthānaṃ prakṛtyā puruṣeṇa ca || // BrS_5.3 //
children.translated_text: the seat of the six-limbed six-lined [mantra], presided over by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Supreme Person). ||3||
The pericarp is the great <s>yantra</s> (mystic diagram), hexagonal, with a diamond-pointed pivot,

children.text:
premānanda-mahānanda-rasenāvasthitaṃ hi yat |
jyotī-rūpeṇa manunā kāma-bījena saṅgatam ||3|| // BrS_5.4 //
children.translated_text: That which is established by the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of <s>premānanda</s> (bliss of divine love) and <s>mahānanda</s> (great bliss), joined with the <s>mantra</s> in the form of light, with the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (seed syllable of desire). ||4||

children.text:
sarva-gaṇa-sevitasya śrīmad-aṣṭadaśākṣara-mantra-rājasya bahu-pīṭhasya
mukhya-pīṭham idam ity āha karṇikāram iti dvayena | mahad-yantram iti |
yat prakṛtir eva sarvatra mantratvena pūjārthaṃ likhyate ity arthaḥ | yantram
eva darśayati ṣaṭ-koṇā abhyantare yasya tat | vajra-kīlakaṃ karṇikāre
bīja-rūpa-hīra-kakolaka-śobhitam || yantre ca-kāropalakṣitā | caturthy-antā
catur-akṣarī kīla-rūpā jñeyā | ṣaṭ-koṇatve prayojanam āha ṣaḍ-aṅgāni
yasyāḥ sā ṣaṭ-padī śrīmad-aṣṭādaśākṣarī tasyāḥ sthānam | prakṛtir
mantrasya svarūpaṃ svayam eva śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ, kāraṇa-rūpatvāt | tac coktam
ṛṣy-ādi-smaraṇe - kṛṣṇaḥ prakṛtir iti |
children.translated_text: This is the principal seat of the king of <s>mantras</s>, the sacred eighteen-syllable [mantra], which is served by all attendants and has many seats — this he states with the two [verses beginning] 'the pericarp.' 'The great <s>yantra</s>' — that which, being the very nature [of the mantra], is everywhere inscribed as a <s>mantra</s> for the purpose of worship. He describes the <s>yantra</s> itself: that within which there are six angles. 'Diamond-pointed pivot' — adorned at the pericarp with a diamond nail in the form of the seed-syllable. In the <s>yantra</s>, it is indicated by the syllable 'ca'; the four-syllable [formula] ending in the dative case should be known as the pivot-form. He states the purpose of the hexagonal form: that which has six limbs — the six-lined [formation], the sacred eighteen-syllable [mantra] — this is its seat. The <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) of the <s>mantra</s>, its essential form, is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, because he is the causal form. And thus it is said in the recollection of the seer and other elements: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>prakṛti</s>.'

children.text:
puruṣaś ca sa eva tad-adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-rūpaḥ | tābhyām avasthitam
adhiṣṭhitam | sa hi mantre caturdhā pratīyate | mantrasya kāraṇa-rūpatvena,
adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-rūpatvena, varṇa-samudāya-rūpatvena, ārādhya-rūpatvena
ca | tatra kāraṇa-rūpatvena adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-rūpatvenātrocyate |
ārādhya-rūpatvena prāg uktaḥ | īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇa iti |
varṇa-rūpatvenāgre uddhariṣyate kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya iti | yathoktaṃ
hāyaśīrṣa-pañcarātre -
vācyatvaṃ vācakatvaṃ devatā-mantrayor iha |
abhedenocyate brahma tattva-vidbhir vicārataḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: And the <s>Puruṣa</s> is he himself, in the form of the presiding deity. By these two [<s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>], it is established and presided over. For he is understood in the <s>mantra</s> in four ways: as the causal form of the <s>mantra</s>, as the presiding deity form, as the form of the collection of syllables, and as the form of the object of worship. Here, he is spoken of as the causal form and as the presiding deity form. As the form of the object of worship, he has been stated earlier: '<s>Īśvaraḥ paramaḥ Kṛṣṇaḥ</s>' (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the Supreme Lord). As the form of syllables, it will be stated later: '<s>kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya</s>' (desire [directed] toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). As stated in the <s>Hāyaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>: 'The signified and the signifier, the deity and the <s>mantra</s> — here, <s>Brahman</s> is spoken of as non-different by the knowers of truth, upon deliberation.'

children.text: gopāla-tāpanī-śrutiṣu -
children.translated_text: In the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī Śrutis</s> (Upaniṣads) —

children.text:
vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo
janye janye pañca-rūpo babhūva |
kṛṣṇas tathaiko'pi jagad-dhitārthaṃ
śabdenāsau pañca-pado vibhāti || iti |
children.translated_text: Just as the one wind, having entered the world, became fivefold in each being, so too <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though one, for the welfare of the world, shines in five aspects through sound [mantra].

children.text:
kvacid durgāyā adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ śakti-śaktimator abheda-vivakṣayā yathā ca
bṛhad-gautamīye -
children.translated_text: Somewhere the presiding role of <s>Durgā</s> is [spoken of] through the intention of non-difference between the energy (<s>śakti</s>) and the possessor of energy (<s>śaktimān</s>), as in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s>—

children.text: rādhā durgā śivā durgā lakṣmī durgā prakīrtitā |
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> is <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Śivā</s> is <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s> is proclaimed as <s>Durgā</s>;

children.text: gopāla-viṣṇu-pūjāyām ādy-antā na tu madhyamā ||
children.translated_text: in the worship of <s>Gopāla-Viṣṇu</s>, the first and last [<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>] are applicable, but not the middle one [<s>Śivā</s>].

children.text:
ataivoktaṃ gautamīya-kalpe --
yaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saiva durgā syād yā durgā kṛṣṇa eva saḥ |
anayor antarādarśī saṃsārān no vimucyate || ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Thus it is stated in the <s>Gautamīya-kalpa</s>: 'He who is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed <s>Durgā</s>; she who is <s>Durgā</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself. One who sees a difference between these two is not freed from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth),' etc.

children.text:
ataḥ svayam eva śrī-kṛṣṇas tatra svarūpa-śakti-rūpeṇa durgā nāmeti | tasmān
neyaṃ māyāṃśa-bhūtā durgātigamyate | niruktiś cātra kṛcchreṇa
durgārādhanādi bahu-prayāsena gamyate jñāyate iti | tathā ca
nārada-pañcarātre śruti-vidyā-saṃvāde -
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself, in the form of His essential energy (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>), is called <s>Durgā</s>. Therefore, she is not to be understood as the <s>Durgā</s> who is a portion of <s>Māyā</s>. And the etymology here: she is 'known' (<s>gamyate</s>) 'with difficulty' (<s>kṛcchreṇa</s>) through worship of <s>Durgā</s> and much effort. And thus in the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Vidyā</s>—

children.text: jānāty ekā parā-kāntaṃ saiva durgā tad-ātmikā |
children.translated_text: One supreme beloved alone knows the transcendent Lord; she herself is <s>Durgā</s>, of His very nature,

children.text: yā parā paramā śaktir mahā-viṣṇu-svarūpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: she who is the supreme transcendent <s>śakti</s> (energy), of the form of <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yasyā vijñāna-mātreṇa parāṇāṃ paramātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: By the mere knowledge of whom, attainment of the Supreme Self

children.text: muhūrtād eva devasya prāptir bhavati nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: of all transcendent beings comes in a moment, and not otherwise.

children.text: ekeyaṃ prema-sarvasva-svabhāvā śrī-kuleśvarī |
children.translated_text: She alone, whose nature is the totality of <s>prema</s> (divine love), the sovereign of the <s>Śrī</s> family—

children.text: anayā sulabho jñeya ādi devo'khileśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: by her the primeval Lord, the controller of all, is known to be easily attainable.

children.text: bhaktir bhajana-sampattir bhajate prakṛtiḥ priyam |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) is the treasure of worship (<s>bhajana</s>); <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) worships the beloved.

children.text: jñāyate'tyanta duḥkhena seyaṃ prakṛtir ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She, this <s>Prakṛti</s> of the Self, is known through the most extreme suffering.

children.text:
durgeti gīyate sadbhir akhaṇḍa-rasa-vallabhā |
asyā āvarikā śaktir mahā-māyākhileśvarī |
yayā mugdhaṃ jagat sarvaṃ sarva-dehābhimānataḥ || iti ca |
children.translated_text: She is sung by the wise as <s>Durgā</s>, the beloved of undivided <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture). Her covering energy is <s>Mahā-Māyā</s>, the sovereign of all, by whom the entire world is deluded through identification with all bodies.

children.text: tathā ca sammohana-tantre jayāṃ prati śrī-durgā-vacanaṃ -
children.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Sammohana Tantra</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Durgā</s> to <s>Jayā</s>—

children.text:
yan nāmnā nāmnī durgāhaṃ guṇair guṇavatī hy aham |
yad-vaibhavā mahā-lakṣmī rādhā nityāparā dvayā || iti |
children.translated_text: 'By whose name I am named <s>Durgā</s>, by whose qualities I am endowed with qualities, by whose majesty <s>Mahā-Lakṣmī</s> exists—<s>Rādhā</s> is the eternal supreme one; the other two are subordinate.'

children.text: kiṃ ca prema-rūpā ye ānanda-mahānanda-rasās tat paripāka-bhedās
tad-ātmakena tathā jyotī-rūpeṇa sva-prakāśakena manunā mantra-rūpeṇa
children.translated_text: by that very nature, and by the self-luminous radiance in the form of a <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: kāma-bījena saṅgatam iti mūlāntargatatve'pi kāma-bījasya pṛthag-uktiḥ
children.translated_text: conjoined with the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (seed syllable of desire)—thus, even though the <s>kāma-bīja</s> is included within the root [mantra], its separate mention

children.text: kutracana svātantryāpekṣayā ||3||
children.translated_text: is with a view to its independent function in certain contexts. ||3||
Moreover, the essences of <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>mahānanda</s> (great bliss), and <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture) in the form of <s>prema</s> (love), which are differentiations of that maturation—

children.text: tat-kiñjalkaṃ tad-aṃśānāṃ tat-patrāṇi śriyām api ||4|| // BrS_5.5 //
children.translated_text: The filaments of that [lotus] are the abodes of His portions (<s>aṃśas</s>), and its petals are the [abodes] of the <s>Śrīs</s> (divine consorts) as well. ||4|| // BrS 5.5 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ tad-dhāmoktvā tad-āvaraṇāny āha tad ity ardhena | tasya
karṇikā-rūpa-dhāmnaḥ kiñjalkāḥ śikharāvali-valita-prācīra-paṅktya ity
arthaḥ | tac ca tad-aṃśānāṃ tasminn aṃśodāyo vidyate yeṣāṃ
parama-prema-bhājāṃ sajātīyānāṃ dhāmety arthaḥ | gokulākhyam ity uktir
eva | teṣāṃ sajātīyatvaṃ coktaṃ śrī-bādarāyaṇinā -
children.translated_text: Thus, having described that abode, He now describes its coverings with 'tat' etc. in half a verse. The filaments of that lotus-shaped abode are the rows of battlements surrounded by chains of pinnacles—this is the meaning. And that is the abode of His portions—that is, the abode of those who are of the same nature, supreme recipients of love, called <s>Gokula</s>—this is the meaning. Their being of the same nature is stated by <s>Śrī Bādarāyaṇi</s> (<s>Śukadeva</s>)—

children.text: evaṃ kakudminaṃ hatvā stūyamānaḥ dvijātibhiḥ |
viveśa goṣṭhaṃ sa-balo gopīnāṃ nayanotsavaḥ || [BhP 10.36.15] iti |
children.translated_text: He entered the cowshed with <s>Bala</s> [<s>Balarāma</s>], a feast for the eyes of the <s>gopīs</s>.' [BhP 10.36.15]
'Having thus killed <s>Kakudmin</s> [the bull-demon], praised by the twice-born,

children.text:
kaṃsa-vadhānte śrī-vraja-rājaṃ prati svayaṃ bhagavatā - jñātīn vo draṣṭum
eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham [BhP 10.45.23] iti | ataiva kamalasya patrāṇi
śriyāṃ tat-preyasīnāṃ gopī-rūpāṇāṃ śrī-rādhādīnām upavana-rūpāṇi
dhāmānīty arthaḥ | gopī-rūpatvaṃ cāsāṃ mantrasya tan-nāmnāliṅgitatvāt
rādhāditvaṃ ca -
children.translated_text: After the killing of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the Lord Himself said to <s>Śrī Vraja-rāja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>): 'We shall come to see our kinsmen, having ensured the happiness of our friends' [BhP 10.45.23]. Therefore the petals of the lotus are the grove-like abodes belonging to the <s>Śrīs</s>—that is, His beloveds in the form of <s>gopīs</s>, <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and others—this is the meaning. That they are in the form of <s>gopīs</s> is because the mantra is embraced by their names; and that <s>Rādhā</s> is foremost [is shown]—

children.text:
devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā |
sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ sammohinī parā || iti bṛhad-gautamīyāt |
children.translated_text: 'The Goddess who is of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s nature is called <s>Rādhikā</s>, the supreme deity, comprising all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, all beauty, the supreme enchantress'—from the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s>.

children.text:
vārāṇasyāṃ viśālākṣī vimalā puruṣottame |
rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane || iti matsya-purāṇāt |
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> she is <s>Viśālākṣī</s>, in <s>Puruṣottama</s> she is <s>Vimalā</s>, in <s>Dvāravatī</s> she is <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, and in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> she is <s>Rādhā</s>'—from the <s>Matsya Purāṇa</s>.

children.text:
rādhayā mādhavo devo mādhavenaiva rādhikā | vibhrājante janeṣv ā iti
ṛk-pariśiṣṭa-śrutau ca |
children.translated_text: '<s>Rādhā</s> shines through <s>Mādhava</s>, and <s>Rādhikā</s> through <s>Mādhava</s> alone; they shine resplendent among the people'—and in the supplementary <s>Ṛk śruti</s> as well.

children.text:
atra viśeṣa-jijñāsāyāṃ kṛṣṇārcana-dīpikā draṣṭavyā | tatra patrāṇām
ucchrita-prāntānāṃ vartmāṇy agrima-sandhiṣu tu goṣṭhāni jñeyāni |
akhaṇḍa-kamalasya gokulatvāt tathaiva gokula-samāveśāc ca goṣṭhaṃ tathaiva
yat tu sthānāntare vacanam asti -
children.translated_text: For specific inquiry here, the <s>Kṛṣṇārcana-dīpikā</s> should be consulted. There, the paths of the petals with their raised edges should be understood as the cowherd settlements at the forward junctions. Since the undivided lotus is <s>Gokula</s>, and since there is inclusion within <s>Gokula</s>, the cowshed (<s>goṣṭha</s>) is likewise. But regarding the statement about another location—

children.text: sahasrāraṃ padmaṃ dala-tatiṣu devībhir abhitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'A thousand-petalled lotus, on whose petal-rows, on all sides, by goddesses

children.text: parīto go-saṅghair api nikhila-kiñjalka-militaiḥ |
children.translated_text: surrounded, and also by herds of cows merged with all the filaments;

children.text: varāṭe yasyāsti svayam akhila-śaktyā prakaṭita-
children.translated_text: on whose circumference, Himself manifested with all <s>śakti</s> (energy)—

children.text: prabhāvaḥ satyaḥ śrī-parama-puruṣas taṃ kila bhaje || iti padma-bīja-koṣe ity
children.translated_text: that powerful, real, Supreme Person (<s>Parama-puruṣa</s>)—Him indeed I worship.' From the <s>Padma-bīja-koṣa</s>—

children.text:
arthaḥ |
tatra go-saṅkhyair iti tu pāṭhaḥ samañjasaḥ | go-saṅkhyāś ca gopāḥ iti | gope
gopāla-gosaṅkhya-godhug-ābhīra-vallabhā ity amaraḥ | akhila-śaktyā
prakaṭitaḥ prabhāvaḥ yena saḥ parama-puruṣaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa ity arthaḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: manifested whose power'—that Supreme Person is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>—this is the meaning. ||4||

this is the meaning. There, 'go-saṅkhyaiḥ' (by those who count cows, i.e., cowherds) is the proper reading. 'Go-saṅkhyāḥ' means '<s>gopas</s>' (cowherds). As stated in the <s>Amara-koṣa</s>: '<s>gopa</s>, <s>gopāla</s>, <s>gosaṅkhya</s>, <s>godhuk</s>, <s>ābhīra</s>, <s>vallabha</s>' are synonyms. 'With all energy

children.text: catur-asraṃ tat-paritaḥ śvetadvīpākhyam adbhutam |
catur-asraṃ catur-mūrteś catur-dhāma catuṣ-kṛtam || // BrS_5.6 //
children.translated_text: fourfold due to the four forms (<s>catur-mūrti</s>), four abodes, made into four. // BrS 5.6 //
Surrounding that, the wonderful [realm] called <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, quadrangular,

children.text: caturbhiḥ puruṣārthaiś ca caturbhir hetubhir vṛtam |
śūlair daśabhir ānaddham ūrdhvādho dig-vidikṣv api || // BrS_5.7 //
children.translated_text: bound by ten tridents above, below, and in the cardinal and intermediate directions. // BrS 5.7 //
Surrounded by the four goals of life (<s>puruṣārthas</s>) and four means,

children.text: aṣṭabhir nidhibhir juṣṭam aṣṭabhiḥ siddhibhis tathā
manu-rūpaiś ca daśabhir dik-pālaiḥ parito vṛtam || // BrS_5.8 //
children.translated_text: surrounded on all sides by the guardians of the directions in the forms of ten <s>Manus</s>. // BrS 5.8 //
Attended by eight treasures (<s>nidhis</s>) and eight supernatural powers (<s>siddhis</s>) likewise,

children.text:
śyāmair gauraiś ca raktaiś ca śuklaiś ca pārṣadarṣabhaiḥ
śobhitaṃ śaktibhis tābhir adbhutābhiḥ samantataḥ ||5|| // BrS_5.9 //
children.translated_text: Adorned by the chief attendants of dark, golden, red, and white colors, and by those wonderful <s>śaktis</s> (energies) all around. ||5|| // BrS 5.9 //

children.text:
atha gokulāvaraṇāny āha caturasram iti caturbhiḥ | tasya gokulasya bahiḥ
sarvataś caturasraṃ catuṣkoṇātmakaṃ sthānaṃ śvetadvīpākhyam | tad etad
upalakṣaṇaṃ golokākhyaṃ cety arthaḥ | yadyapi gokule śvetadvīpatvam asty
eva tad-avāntara-bhūmimayatvāt | tathāpi viśeṣa-nāmnoktatvāt tenaiva tat
pratīyate iti tathoktam | kintu caturasre'py antar-maṇḍalaṃ
śrī-vṛndāvanākhyaṃ jñeyam | tathā ca svāyambhuvāgame - dhyāyet
tatra-viśuddhātmā idaṃ sarvaṃ krameṇa ca ity ādikam uktvā tan-madhye
vṛndāvanaṃ kusumitaṃ nānā-vṛkṣa-vihaṅgamaṃ saṃsmaret ity uktam | tathā
ca bṛhad-vāmane śrutīnāṃ prārthanā pūrvakāṇi padyāni
children.translated_text: Now He describes the coverings of <s>Gokula</s> with 'quadrangular' etc. in four verses. Outside of that <s>Gokula</s>, on all sides, the quadrangular, four-cornered region is called <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>. This is a designation for the realm called <s>Goloka</s> as well—this is the meaning. Although <s>Gokula</s> itself has the nature of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, being constituted of its sub-regions, nevertheless, because it is mentioned by its specific name, it is understood as such. But within the quadrangular area, the inner circle should be known as <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>. And thus in the <s>Svāyambhuva Āgama</s>, having stated 'one of purified mind should meditate there on all this in sequence,' it says 'in the midst of that, one should remember the flowering <s>Vṛndāvana</s> with its various trees and birds.' And thus in the <s>Bṛhad-Vāmana</s> Purāṇa, the verses preceded by the prayer of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedic hymns personified)—

children.text: ānanda-mātram iti yad vadanti hi purāvidaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That which the ancients declare to be pure bliss alone—

children.text: tad-rūpe darśayāsmākaṃ yadi deyo varo hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: show us that form, if indeed a boon is to be granted to us.'

children.text: śrutvaitad darśayāmāsa svaṃ lokaṃ prakṛteḥ param |
children.translated_text: 'Hearing this, He showed His own world, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature),

children.text: kevalānubhavānanda-mātram akṣaram avyayam ||
children.translated_text: consisting of mere experience of bliss, imperishable, undecaying.'

children.text:
yatra vṛndāvanaṃ nāma vanaṃ kāma-dughair drumaiḥ |
manorama-nikuñjāḍhyaṃ sarvartu-sukha-saṃyutam || ity ādi tac ca caturasram |
children.translated_text: 'Where there is the forest called <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, with wish-fulfilling trees, rich in delightful bowers, endowed with the happiness of all seasons'—etc. And that is quadrangular.

children.text:
catur-mūrteś catur-vyūhasya vāsudevādi-catuṣṭayasya | catuṣkṛtaṃ caturdhā
vibhaktam catur-dhāma | kintu deva-līlatvāt tad-upari-vyoma-yāna-sthā eva
jñeyā hetubhiḥ | tat-puruṣārtha-sādhanaiḥ | manu-rūpaiḥ
sva-sva-mantrātmakaiḥ | dik-pālaiḥ indrādibhiḥ | śyāmādayaḥ catvāro vedāḥ
tair ity arthaḥ | kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra chandobhiḥ stūyamānaṃ suvismitāḥ iti
daśamāt | śaktibhiḥ vimalādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Of the four forms': of the fourfold <s>vyūha</s> (emanation)—<s>Vāsudeva</s> and the other four. 'Made into four': divided fourfold into four abodes. However, because of being divine play (<s>deva-līlā</s>), they should be understood as stationed above in the celestial vehicle. 'By means': by the instruments for achieving those <s>puruṣārthas</s>. 'In the forms of <s>Manus</s>': those whose very nature consists of their respective mantras. 'Guardians of the directions': <s>Indra</s> and others. 'The dark ones, etc.' are the four <s>Vedas</s>—by them, this is the meaning. 'And <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> there, being praised by the Vedic meters, greatly astonished'—from the Tenth Canto. '<s>Śaktis</s>': <s>Vimalā</s> and others.

children.text: tad evaṃ goloka-nāmā ayaṃ lokaḥ śrī-bhāgavate sādhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, this world called <s>Goloka</s> is established in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>:

children.text: nandas tv atīndriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā loka-pāla-mahodayam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s>, having seen the supernatural, magnificent opulence of the world-guardians,

children.text: kṛṣṇe ca sannatiṃ teṣāṃ jñātibhyo vismito 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and their submission to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, astonished, told his kinsmen.'

children.text: te cautsukya-dhiyo rājan matvā gopās tam īśvaram |
children.translated_text: 'Those cowherds, with eager minds, O King, considering Him the Lord,

children.text: api naḥ svagatiṃ sūkṣmām upādhāsyad adhīśvaram ||
children.translated_text: [wondered:] will He bestow upon us our own subtle destination, the supreme controller?'

children.text: iti svānāṃ sa bhagavān vijñāyākhila-dṛk svayam |
children.translated_text: 'The Lord Himself, the all-seeing one, understanding the wish of His own people,

children.text: saṅkalpa-siddhaye teṣāṃ kṛpayaitad acintayat ||
children.translated_text: for the fulfillment of their desire, compassionately thought thus:'

children.text: jano vai loka etasminn avidyā-kāma-karmabhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'People in this world, by ignorance, desire, and action,

children.text: uccāvacāsu gatiṣu na veda svāṃ gatiṃ bhraman ||
children.translated_text: wandering in high and low states, do not know their own destination.'

children.text: iti sañcintya bhagavān mahā-kāruṇiko hariḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having thus reflected, the Lord <s>Hari</s>, the supremely compassionate one,

children.text: darśayāmāsa lokaṃ svaṃ gopānāṃ tamasaḥ param ||
children.translated_text: showed His own world to the cowherds, the world beyond darkness.'

children.text: satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ yat brahma jyotiḥ sanātanam |
children.translated_text: 'Truth, knowledge, infinite—that <s>Brahman</s>, the eternal light,

children.text: yad dhi paśyanti munayo guṇāpāye samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which the sages, concentrated, behold when the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature) have ceased.'

children.text: te tu brahma-hradaṃ nītā magnāḥ kṛṣṇena coddhṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'They, led to the lake of <s>Brahman</s>, submerged and raised up by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: dadṛśur brahmaṇo lokaṃ yatrākrūro 'dhyagāt purā ||
children.translated_text: saw the world of <s>Brahman</s> where <s>Akrūra</s> had gone before.'

children.text: nandādayas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramānanda-nirvṛtāḥ |
kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra cchandobhiḥ stūyamānaṃ suvismitāḥ || [BhP 10.28.10-17] iti |
children.translated_text: and [they saw] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> there being praised by the <s>Vedas</s> in metrical hymns, and they were greatly astonished.' [BhP 10.28.10-17] Thus.
'<s>Nanda</s> and the others, having seen that, filled with supreme bliss,'

children.text:
atīndriyam adṛṣṭa-pūrvam | sva-gatiṃ sva-dhāma | sūkṣmāṃ durjñeyām |
upādhāsyan upadhāsyati | asmān prāpayiṣyatīty arthaḥ | iti saṅkalpitavanta
iti śeṣaḥ | jano'sau vraja-vāsī mama svajanaḥ | sālokya-sārṣṭi- [BhP 3.29.12]
ity ādi padye janā itivad ubhayatrāpy anya-janatvam aprastutatam iti |
vraja-janasya tu tadīya-svajanatamatvaṃ tena svayam eva vibhāvitam -
children.translated_text: 'Beyond the senses'—never seen before. 'Their own destination'—their own abode. 'Subtle'—difficult to comprehend. 'Will convey'—will cause to attain; the meaning is: 'He will bring us there.' The completion is: thus they resolved. 'That community'—the residents of <s>Vraja</s>, my own people. In the verse beginning 'the equality of residence, opulence' [BhP 3.29.12] etc., the word 'people' in both cases refers to others, which is not the topic here. But the supreme intimacy of the <s>Vraja</s> community as His own people has been demonstrated by Him personally—

children.text: tasmān mac-charaṇaṃ goṣṭhaṃ man-nāthaṃ mat-parigraham |
gopāye svātma-yogena so'yaṃ me vrata āhitaḥ || [BhP 10.25.18] ity anena |
children.translated_text: I protect it by the power of my own Self—this is my established vow.' [BhP 10.25.18] By this [statement].
'Therefore my shelter is <s>Goṣṭha</s> (the cowherd settlement), whose protector I am, whose possessions are mine;

children.text:
sa etasmin prāpañcike loke avidyābhir yā uccāvacā deva-tiryag-ādi-rūpā
gatayas tāsu svāṃ gatiṃ bhraman tan-miśratayābhivyakteḥ tan-nirviśeṣatayā
jānan, tām eva svāṃ gatiṃ bhaved ity arthaḥ madīya-laukika-līlāveśena
jñānāṃśa-tirodhānād iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: He, in this phenomenal world, through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), wanders in the various high and low destinies in the forms of gods, animals, and so forth; knowing His own destination as undifferentiated from those [destinies] due to its manifestation being mixed with them—the meaning is: that very destination would be His own. The purport is: due to the concealment of the aspect of knowledge through absorption in His worldly <s>līlā</s> (pastimes).

children.text: iti nandādayo gopāḥ kṛṣṇa-rāma-kathāṃ mudā |
children.translated_text: 'Thus <s>Nanda</s> and the other cowherds, joyfully

children.text: kurvanto ramamāṇāś ca nāvindan bhava-vedanām || [BhP 10.11.28]
children.translated_text: narrating the deeds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>, and delighting [therein], did not experience the suffering of worldly existence.' [BhP 10.11.28]

children.text:
iti śrī-daśamokter avidyā-kāma-karmaṇāṃ tatrāsāmarthyāt | gopīnāṃ svāṃ
lokaṃ golokam iti | arthāt tān praty eva sandarśayāmāsa | tamasaḥ prakṛteḥ
param svarūpa-śaktyābhivyaktatvāt | ataiva saccidānanda-rūpa evāsau loka ity
āha satyam iti |
children.translated_text: Thus, from the statement in the Tenth [Canto], due to the incapacity of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>karma</s> (action) there. 'Their own world' for the <s>gopīs</s> means <s>Goloka</s>. By implication, He showed it to them alone. 'Beyond darkness'—beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature), because it is manifested by His own essential potency (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>). For this very reason, that realm is of the nature of <s>saccidānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss)—this He states with 'satyam' (true/real).

children.text:
atha śrī-vṛndāvane tādṛśa-darśanaṃ katama-deśa-sthitānāṃ teṣām ity ata
āha te tv iti | brahma-hradaṃ akrūra-tīrthaṃ kṛṣṇena nītā punaś ca tenaiva
magnāḥ majjitāḥ punaś ca tasmāt tenaivoddhṛtāḥ | uddhṛtya punaḥ
sva-sthāna-prāpitāḥ santo, brahmaṇaḥ parama-bṛhattamasya tasyaiva lokaṃ
golokākhyaṃ dadṛśuḥ | mūrdhabhiḥ satya-lokas tu brahma-lokaḥ sanātanaṃ
[BhP 2.5.38] iti dvitīye | vaikuṇṭhāntarasyāpi tat tayākhyāteḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, regarding such a vision in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>—in which location were they situated?—to this He says 'te tu' (but they). [They were] taken by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to <s>Brahma-hrada</s> (<s>Akrūra-tīrtha</s>), and again immersed—that is, submerged—by Him, and again lifted out by Him from that [pool]. Having lifted them out and restored them to their own place, they beheld the world of <s>Brahman</s>—the supreme, greatest of all—called <s>Goloka</s>. 'At the crown, <s>Satya-loka</s> is indeed <s>Brahma-loka</s>, the eternal' [BhP 2.5.38]—from the Second [Canto]. Because even the inner <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is designated by that name.

children.text:
ko'sau brahma-hradaḥ ? tatrāha yatreti | purety etat-prasaṅgād bhāvi-kāla ity
arthaḥ | purā purāṇe nikaṭe prabandhātīta-bhāviṣu iti koṣa-kārāḥ | seyaṃ
ca paripāṭī tat tīrthaṃ mahimānaṃ lakṣyam eva vidhātum iti bhāvaḥ | tatra
svāṃ gatim iti tadīyatā-nirdeśo gopānāṃ svaṃ lokam iti ṣaṣṭhī-sva-śabdayor
nirdeśaḥ | kṛṣṇam iti sākṣān-nirdeśaś ca vaikuṇṭhāntaraṃ vyavacchidya
śrī-golokam eva sthāpitavān iti |
children.translated_text: What is this <s>Brahma-hrada</s>? To that he says 'yatra' (where). 'Formerly'—because of this context, it means a future time; the lexicographers state: 'purā [means] in ancient [times], near [at hand], in the continuous past, and in the future.' And this sequence is intended to indicate the greatness of that <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford)—this is the purport. There, 'their own destination'—the indication of belonging to Him; 'the cowherds' own world'—the indication through the genitive case and the word 'sva' (own); and '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'—the direct indication—having excluded the inner <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, he has established <s>Śrī Goloka</s> alone.

children.text: tathā ca harivaṃśe śakra-vacanam -
children.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, the statement of <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>)—

children.text: svargād ūrdhvaṃ brahma-loko brahmarṣi-gaṇa-sevitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Above <s>Svarga</s> (heaven) is <s>Brahma-loka</s>, attended by hosts of brahmanical sages;

children.text: tatra soma-gatiś caiva jyotiṣāṃ ca mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: there is the course of <s>Soma</s> (the Moon), and of the luminaries, the great souls.

children.text: tasyopari gavāṃ lokaḥ sādhyās taṃ pālayanti hi |
children.translated_text: Above that is the world of cows (<s>Goloka</s>); the <s>Sādhyas</s> indeed protect it.

children.text: sa hi sarva-gataḥ kṛṣṇa mahākāśa-gato mahān ||
children.translated_text: It is all-pervading, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, situated in the great ether, vast.

children.text: upary upari tatrāpi gatis tava tapomayī |
children.translated_text: Higher and higher still above that is Your destination, made of <s>tapas</s> (austerity),

children.text: yāṃ na vidmo vayaṃ sarve pṛcchanto'pi pitāmaham |
children.translated_text: which we all do not know, even when asking the Grandfather (<s>Brahmā</s>).

children.text: gatiḥ śama-damāḍhyānāṃ svargaḥ sukṛta-karmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: The destination of those endowed with tranquility and self-restraint is heaven; [that is the reward] of those of meritorious deeds.

children.text: brāhmye tapasi yuktānāṃ brahma-lokaḥ parā gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: For those engaged in sacred austerity relating to <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahma-loka</s> is the supreme destination.

children.text: gavām eva tu yo loko durāroho hi sā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the world of cows alone—that destination is indeed difficult to attain.

children.text: sa tu lokas tvayā kṛṣṇa sīdamānaḥ kṛtātmanā |
dhṛto dhṛtimatā vīra nighantopdadravān gavām || [HV 2.19.29-35] iti |
children.translated_text: sustained by You, the steadfast hero, destroying the calamities of the cows.' [HV 2.19.29-35] Thus.
But that world, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, which was sinking, was upheld by You, the self-realized one,

children.text:
tatrāpāta-pratītārthāntare svargād ūrdhvaṃ brahmaṇo loka ity ayuktaṃ syāt
loka-trayam atikramyokteḥ | tatra soma-gatiś caivety api na sambhavati
candrasyānyeṣām api jyotiṣāṃ dhruva-lokādhastād eva gateḥ | tatra sādhyās
taṃ pālayantīty api nopapadyate | deva-yoni-rūpāṇāṃ teṣāṃ svarga-lokasyāpi
pālanam asambhavyam | kim uta tad-upari golokasya | tathā tasya lokasya
surabhi-lokatve sati sarva-gata ity anupapannaṃ syāt |
śrī-bhagavad-vigraha-lokayor acintya-śaktitvena vibhutvaṃ ghaṭate na punar
asyeti | ataiva sarvātītatvāt tatrāpi tava gatir ity api śabdo vismaye prayuktaḥ |
yāṃ na vidmo vayaṃ sarve ity-ādikaṃ coktam |
children.translated_text: There, if one takes the superficially apparent meaning, it would be inappropriate to say '<s>Brahma-loka</s> is above <s>Svarga</s>,' because the statement transcends the three worlds. 'There is the course of <s>Soma</s>'—this too is impossible, since the Moon and other luminaries have their courses only below <s>Dhruva-loka</s> (the Pole Star realm). 'The <s>Sādhyas</s> protect it'—this too is untenable, for it is impossible that those [<s>Sādhyas</s>], who are a class of demigods, could protect even <s>Svarga-loka</s>, let alone <s>Goloka</s> above it. Moreover, if that world were the [material] world of <s>Surabhi</s> cows, it would be untenable to call it 'all-pervading.' The quality of all-pervasiveness is possible for <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s>'s form and abode through inconceivable potency (<s>acintya-śakti</s>), but not for this [material cow-world]. For this very reason—because it transcends everything—the word 'api' (even) in 'Your destination even there above' is used in the sense of wonder. And the statement 'which we all do not know' etc. has been said [to confirm this].

children.text:
tasmāt prākṛta-golokād anya evāsau goloka iti siddham | tathā ca
mokṣa-dharme nārāyaṇīyopākhyāne śrī-bhagavad-vākyaṃ -
children.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>Goloka</s> is established as distinct from the material <s>Goloka</s>. And thus, in the <s>Mokṣa-dharma</s>, in the <s>Nārāyaṇīya</s> sub-narrative, the statement of <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s>—

children.text: evaṃ bahu-vidhai rūpaiś carāmīha vasundharām |
brahma-lokaṃ ca kaunteya golokaṃ ca sanātanam || [Mbh 12.330.68] iti |
children.translated_text: and in <s>Brahma-loka</s>, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, and in eternal <s>Goloka</s>.' [Mbh 12.330.68] Thus.
'Thus in many forms I move about on this earth,

children.text: tasmād ayam arthaḥ svarga-śabdena --
