children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning is: by the word '<s>svarga</s>' (heaven)—

children.text: bhūr-lokaḥ kalpitaḥ padbhyāṃ bhuvar-loko 'sya nābhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhūr-loka</s> is fashioned from His feet, <s>Bhuvar-loka</s> from His navel,

children.text: hṛdā svar-loka urasā mahar-loko mahātmanaḥ || [BhP 2.5.42]
children.translated_text: <s>Svar-loka</s> from His heart, and <s>Mahar-loka</s> from the chest of the Great Soul.' [BhP 2.5.42]

children.text:
iti dvitīyānusāreṇa svar-lokam ārabhya satya-loka-paryantaṃ loka-pañcakam
ucyate | tasmād ūrdhvam upari brahma-loko brahmātmako loko brahma-lokaḥ
sac-cid-ānanda-rūpatvāt | brahmaṇo bhagavato loka iti vā | mūrdhabhiḥ
satya-lokas tu brahma-lokaḥ sanātanaḥ [BhP 2.5.38] iti dvitīyāt | tathā ca ṭīkā
-brahma-loko vaikuṇṭhākhyaḥ | sanātano nityaḥ | na tu sṛjyaḥ
prapañcāntarvartī | ity eṣā | śrutiś ca eṣa brahma-lokaḥ | eṣa ātma-lokaḥ |
iti |
children.translated_text: Following this [statement] from the Second [Canto], the five worlds from <s>Svar-loka</s> up to <s>Satya-loka</s> are referred to. Above that—'<s>Brahma-loka</s>'—means the world whose nature is <s>Brahman</s>, because it is of the nature of <s>saccidānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss); or, the world of <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Supreme Lord), who is <s>Brahman</s>. 'At the crown, <s>Satya-loka</s> is indeed <s>Brahma-loka</s>, the eternal' [BhP 2.5.38]—from the Second [Canto]. And the commentary [states]: '<s>Brahma-loka</s> is called <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>. Eternal—meaning permanent; not a created [world] situated within the material realm.' This is that [commentary]. And the <s>śruti</s> [states]: 'This is <s>Brahma-loka</s>; this is <s>Ātma-loka</s> (the world of the Self).'

children.text:
sa ca brahmarṣi-gaṇa-sevitaḥ | brahmāṇi mūrtimanto vedāḥ | ṛṣayaś ca
śrī-nāradādayaḥ | gaṇāś ca śrī-garuḍa-viṣvaksenādayaḥ | taiḥ sevitaḥ | evaṃ
nityāśritān uktvā tad-gamanādhikāriṇa āha | tatra brahma-loke umayā saha
vartata iti somaḥ śrī-śivas tasya gatiḥ |
children.translated_text: And it is 'attended by hosts of brahmanical sages': '<s>brahmāṇi</s>' means the <s>Vedas</s> in personified form; '<s>ṛṣis</s>' (sages) are <s>Śrī Nārada</s> and others; '<s>gaṇas</s>' (hosts) are <s>Śrī Garuḍa</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, and others—'attended' by them. Having thus described its eternal residents, he speaks of those qualified to go there. 'There, in <s>Brahma-loka</s>, <s>Soma</s> abides with <s>Umā</s>'—<s>Soma</s> means <s>Śrī Śiva</s>; his 'course' [means his destination there].

children.text: sva-dharma-niṣṭhaḥ śata-janmabhiḥ pumān
children.translated_text: 'A person steadfast in his own <s>dharma</s>, after a hundred births,

children.text: viriñcatām eti tataḥ paraṃ hi mām |
children.translated_text: attains the status of <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>); thereafter, [he attains] the Supreme, who is Myself.

children.text: avyākṛtaṃ bhāgavato 'tha vaiṣṇavaṃ
children.translated_text: The unmanifest realm of <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>

children.text: padaṃ yathāhaṃ vibudhāḥ kalātyaye || [BhP 4.24.29] iti caturthe
children.translated_text: abode—just as I [attain it], O wise ones, at the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle).' [BhP 4.24.29] Thus, in the Fourth [Canto],

children.text: śrī-rudra-gītam |
children.translated_text: the hymn of <s>Śrī Rudra</s> (<s>Rudra-gīta</s>).

children.text:
someti supāṃ sulug ity ādinā ṣaṣṭhyā luk chāndasaḥ | tata uttaratrāpi gatir
ity asyānvayaḥ | jyotir brahma tad-aikātmya-bhāvānāṃ muktānām ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Soma'—the elision of the genitive case ending is Vedic usage, by the rule 'supāṃ sulug' etc. Thereafter, 'course' is to be connected with what follows above as well. 'Of the luminaries'—means of the liberated souls who have attained identity with <s>Brahman</s>, the Light—this is the meaning.

children.text:
nanu tādṛśām api sarveṣāṃ kintu mahātmanāṃ mahāśayānāṃ
mokṣānādaratayā bhajatāṃ śrī-sanakādi-tulyānām ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, [one might ask:] even among all such [liberated souls], but [this refers to] the great souls—those of noble disposition who, out of indifference to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), engage in devotion, equal to <s>Śrī Sanaka</s> and the other [Kumāras]—this is the meaning.

children.text: muktānām api siddhānāṃ nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇaḥ
sudurlabhaḥ praśāntātmā koṭiṣv api mahā-mune || [BhP 6.14.5] iti ṣaṣṭhāt |
children.translated_text: is extremely rare—a person of tranquil soul—even among tens of millions, O great sage.' [BhP 6.14.5] From the Sixth [Canto].
'Even among the liberated and perfected beings, one who is devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>

children.text: yoginām api sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā |
children.translated_text: 'And among all <s>yogins</s>, one who worships Me with inner self absorbed in Me,

children.text: śraddhāvān bhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ || [Gītā 6.47] iti
children.translated_text: with faith—he is considered by Me to be the most united [in <s>yoga</s>].' [Gītā 6.47] Thus,

children.text: gītābhyaś ca |
children.translated_text: from the <s>Gītā</s> as well.

children.text:
teṣv eva mahattva-paryavasanāt | tasya ca brahma-lokasyopari
sarvordhva-pradeśe gavāṃ lokaḥ śrī-goloka ity arthaḥ | taṃ ca golokaṃ
sādhyāḥ prāpañcika-devānāṃ prasādhanīyā mūla-rūpā
nitya-tadīya-deva-gaṇāḥ pālayanti dik-pālatayā vartante te ha nākaṃ
mahimānaḥ sacantaḥ yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ [Rk 10.90.16] iti śruteḥ |
children.translated_text: Because [the discussion] culminates in their greatness. And above that <s>Brahma-loka</s>, in the supreme region above all, is the 'world of cows'—meaning <s>Śrī Goloka</s>. And that <s>Goloka</s>—the '<s>Sādhyas</s>' are the original forms of the phenomenal <s>devas</s>, who are to be propitiated; they are the eternal divine attendants belonging to Him, who protect it—they serve as guardians of the directions. 'Those who are great in glory attain the highest heaven, where dwell the ancient <s>Sādhyas</s>, the gods' [Ṛk 10.90.16]—from the <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: tatra pūrve ye ca sādhyā viśve devāḥ sanātanāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'There, the ancient <s>Sādhyas</s> and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the eternal ones,

children.text: te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacantaḥ śubha-darśanāḥ || iti
children.translated_text: those who are great in glory, attaining the highest heaven, are beautiful to behold.' Thus,

children.text: mahā-vaikuṇṭha-varṇane pādmottara-khaṇḍāc ca |
children.translated_text: from the <s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the description of <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha</s>.

children.text:
yad vā tad bhūri-bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyāṃ yad gokule'pi
[BhP 10.14.34] iti śrī-brahma-stavānusāreṇa tad-vidha-parama-bhaktānām api
sādhyās tādṛśa-siddhi-prāptaye prāsādhanīyāḥ śrī-gopī-prabhṛtayas taṃ
pālayanti |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, following the hymn of <s>Śrī Brahmā</s>—'What greatly fortunate birth is this, in any forest whatsoever, in <s>Gokula</s>' [BhP 10.14.34]—the <s>Sādhyas</s>, who are to be propitiated even by such supreme devotees for the attainment of such perfection, are <s>Śrī Gopīs</s> and others; they protect it.

children.text:
tad evaṃ sarvopari-gatatve'pi | hi prasiddhau | sa śrī-golokaḥ sarva-gataḥ
śrī-nārāyaṇa iva prāpañcikāprāpañcika-vastu-vyāpakaḥ | kaiścit
krama-mukti-vyavasthayā tathā prāpyamāno'py asau
dvitīya-skandha-varṇita-kamalāsana-dṛṣṭa-vaikuṇṭhavat śrī-vraja-vāsinbhir
atrāpi yasmād dṛṣṭa iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, even though it is situated above everything—'hi' is used in the sense of [well-known] certainty—that <s>Śrī Goloka</s> is 'all-pervading,' pervading all phenomenal and non-phenomenal entities, just like <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>. Although attainable by some through the gradual process of <s>krama-mukti</s> (progressive liberation), it was seen even here [on earth] by the residents of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>—just as the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> seen by <s>Brahmā</s> seated on the lotus, as described in the Second Canto—this is the purport.

children.text: ataiva mahān bhagavad-rūpa eva | mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānam [KaṭhU 2.22]
children.translated_text: For this very reason, [it is called] 'great'—being of the very form of <s>Bhagavān</s>. 'The great, all-pervading Self' [<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.22]

children.text:
iti śruteḥ | tatra hetuḥ | mahākāśaḥ parama-vyomākhyaḥ
brahma-viśeṣaṇa-lābhād ākāśas tal-liṅgād [Vs 1.1.22] iti nyāya-prasiddheś
ca | tad-gata-brahmākārodayāntaram eva vaikuṇṭha-prāpteḥ yathājāmilasya |
tad evam upary upari sarvopary api virājamāne tatra śrī-goloke'pi tava gatiḥ |
śrī-govinda-rūpeṇa krīḍā vartata ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus from the <s>śruti</s>. The reason: the great space (<s>mahākāśa</s>), called the supreme sky (<s>parama-vyoma</s>), since it qualifies <s>Brahman</s> — according to the well-known principle 'Space, because of the characteristic mark of that [<s>Brahman</s>]' [<s>Vedānta-sūtra</s> 1.1.22]. The attainment of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is within the interval until the arising of the form of <s>Brahman</s> therein — as in the case of <s>Ajāmila</s>. Thus, above and above all, even in that Śrī <s>Goloka</s> which shines supreme, Your destination (<s>gati</s>) [is there]. The meaning is: play in the form of Śrī <s>Govinda</s> takes place.

children.text:
ataiva sā ca gatiḥ sādhāraṇī na bhavati kintu tapomayī |
tapo'trānavacchinnaiśvaryaṃ sahasra-nāma-bhāṣye'pi paramaṃ yo mahat tapaḥ
ity atra tatra vyākhyātam | sa tapo'tapyata iti parameśvara-viṣayaka-śruteḥ |
aiśvaryaṃ prākāśayad iti tatrārthaḥ | ataiva brahmādi-durvitarkyatvam apy
āha yām iti | adhunā tasya śrī-goloka ity ākhyā bījam abhivyañjayati gatir
iti | brāhmye brahma-loka-prāpake tapasi viṣṇu-viṣayaka-manaḥ-praṇidhāne
yuktānāṃ yata-cittānāṃ tat-prema-bhaktānām ity arthaḥ | yasya jñāna-mayaṃ
tapaḥ iti śruteḥ | brahma-loko vaikuṇṭha-lokaḥ | parā prakṛtyatītā | gavāṃ
vraja-vāsi-mātrāṇāṃ mocayan vraja-gavāṃ dina-tāpam [BhP 10.35.25]
ity-uktānusāreṇa atraiva nighnatopadravān gavām ity uktyā ca
goloka-vāsi-mātrāṇāṃ svatas tad-bhāva-bhāvitānāṃ ca sādhana-vaśād ity
arthaḥ | atas tad-bhāvasya durlabhatvād durārohā | tad evaṃ golokaṃ
varṇayitvā tasya gokulena sahābhedam āha sa tv iti |
sa eva tu sa loko dhṛto rakṣitaḥ śrī-govardhanoddharaṇeneti | evam eva
mokṣa-dharma-śrī-nārāyaṇīyopākhyāne śrī-bhagavad-vākyam -
children.translated_text: Therefore, that destination is not ordinary but is of the nature of <s>tapas</s> (austerity/power). Here, <s>tapas</s> means unobstructed sovereignty; in the commentary on the Thousand Names too, in the passage 'the supreme great austerity,' this is explained. From the <s>śruti</s> regarding the Supreme Lord: 'He performed austerity.' The meaning there is: He manifested [His] sovereignty. Therefore, He also states the incomprehensibility [of this] even to <s>Brahmā</s> etc. with 'yām.' Now the name 'Śrī <s>Goloka</s>' of that [abode] — its seed is being revealed by the word '<s>gati</s>.' For those who are disciplined, restrained in mind, in the austerity pertaining to <s>Brahman</s>, which leads to the attainment of <s>Brahma-loka</s> — which is meditation focused on <s>Viṣṇu</s> — [for those who are] devotees of love (<s>prema-bhaktas</s>) toward Him — this is the meaning. From the <s>śruti</s>: 'Whose austerity is made of knowledge.' <s>Brahma-loka</s> means <s>Vaikuṇṭha-loka</s>. Transcendental (<s>parā</s>), beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>. Of all cows — meaning all residents of <s>Vraja</s> — as stated 'relieving the heat of the day for the cows of <s>Vraja</s>' [BhP 10.35.25], and by the statement 'destroying the calamities of the cows here' — meaning all residents of <s>Goloka</s>, who are naturally imbued with that mood, or who are [so] by the force of spiritual practice (<s>sādhana</s>). Therefore, because that mood is difficult to attain, it is 'hard to ascend' (<s>durārohā</s>). Thus, having described <s>Goloka</s>, he states its non-difference from <s>Gokula</s> with 'sa tu' — that same world is upheld and protected by the lifting of Śrī <s>Govardhana</s>. Similarly, in the <s>Mokṣa-dharma</s>, in the Śrī <s>Nārāyaṇīya</s> episode, the statement of the Blessed Lord:

children.text: evaṃ bahu-vidhai rūpaiś carāmīha vasundharām |
brahma-lokaṃ ca kaunteya golokaṃ ca sanātanam || [Mbh 12.330.68] iti |
children.translated_text: in <s>Brahma-loka</s>, and in the eternal <s>Goloka</s>, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>.' [Mbh 12.330.68]
'Thus, in many forms I move about on this earth,

children.text: tathā ca mṛtyu-sañjaya-tantre --
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Mṛtyu-sañjaya Tantra</s>:

children.text:
ekadā sāntarīkṣāc ca vaikuṇṭhaṃ svecchayā bhuvi |
gokulatvena saṃsthāpya gopīmaya-mahotsavā |
bhakti-rūpāṃ satāṃ bhaktim utpāditavatī bhṛśam || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Once, from the celestial space, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> was established on earth by His own will as <s>Gokula</s>. With a great festival of <s>gopīs</s>, it generated intense <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) in the form of devotion among the saintly.'

children.text: evaṃ nārada-pañcarātre vijayākhyāne -
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>, in the section called <s>Vijaya</s>:

children.text:
tat sarvopari goloke śrī-govindaḥ sadā svayam |
viharet paramānandī gopī-gokula-nāyakaḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: 'In that supreme <s>Goloka</s>, Śrī <s>Govinda</s> Himself always sports, the supremely blissful one, the lord of the <s>gopīs</s> and <s>Gokula</s>.'

children.text: tathā ṛkṣu cāyam eva pradiṣṭaḥ -
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Ṛg Veda</s> too, this very [abode] is indicated:

children.text:
tāṃ vāṃ vāstūny uśmasi gamadhyai
yatra gāvo bhūri-śṛṅgā ayāsaḥ |
atrāha tad urugāyasya vṛṣṇaḥ
paramaṃ padam avabhāti bhūri || iti |
vyākhyātaṃ ca - tāṃ tāni vāṃ yuvayoḥ kṛṣṇa-rāmayor vāstūni līlā-sthānāni
gamadhyai prāptuṃ uśmasi kāmayāmahe | tāni kiṃ viśiṣṭāni ? yatra yeṣu
bhūri-śṛṅgā mahā-śṛṅgyo gāvo bahu-śubha-lakṣaṇā iti vā | ayāsaḥ śubhāḥ |
ayaḥ śubhāvaho vidhir ity amaraḥ | devāsa itivat jasantaṃ padam | atra
bhūmau tal-loke vede ca prasiddhaṃ śrī-golokākhyaṃ urugāyasya svayaṃ
bhagavato tac-caraṇāravindasya paramaṃ prapañcātītaṃ padaṃ sthānaṃ bhūri
bahudhā avabhātīty āha veda iti |
children.translated_text: 'We desire to go to those abodes of You two (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>), where the cows with great horns are [and] auspicious. There indeed shines forth in many ways the supreme abode of the widely praised <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).' And the commentary: 'tāṃ tāni' — those; 'vāṃ' — of you two, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rāma</s>; 'vāstūni' — pastime-places; 'gamadhyai' — to reach; 'uśmasi' — we desire. What are they characterized by? 'yatra' — where; 'bhūri-śṛṅgāḥ' — great-horned; 'gāvaḥ' — cows; many auspicious marks — or thus. 'ayāsaḥ' — auspicious. 'Ayaḥ' means 'that which brings good fortune' — thus the <s>Amara</s> dictionary. Like 'devāsaḥ,' the word ending is '-as.' Here — on earth, in that world, and in the <s>Veda</s> — the well-known supreme abode called Śrī <s>Goloka</s>, of the 'urugāya' (widely praised), of the Blessed Lord Himself, of His lotus feet — the supreme, transcendental abode shines forth in many ways — this the <s>Veda</s> states.

children.text:
yajuḥsu - mādhyandinīyā stūyate dhāmāny uśmasi ity ādau | viṣṇoḥ
paramaṃ padam avabhātīti bhūrīti cātra prakārāntaraṃ paṭhanti śeṣaṃ
samānam ||5||
children.translated_text: is the same. ||5||

In the <s>Yajur Veda</s> — the <s>Mādhyandina</s> recension — in the passage beginning 'We praise, we desire the abodes' — they read a different version: 'The supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> shines forth' and 'extensively.' The rest

children.text:
evaṃ jyotir-mayo devaḥ sad-ānandaṃ parāt paraḥ |
ātmārāmasya tasyāsti prakṛtyā na samāgamaḥ ||6|| // BrS_5.10 //
children.translated_text: Thus the God who is made of light, whose bliss is eternal, who is higher than the highest — the self-delighting one (<s>ātmārāma</s>) has no contact with <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature). ||6|| // BrS 5.10 //

children.text:
atha mūla-vyākhyām anusarāmaḥ | virāṭ-tad-antaryāminor abheda-vivakṣayā
puruṣa-sūktādāv eka-puruṣatvaṃ yathā nirūpitaṃ, tathā
goloka-tad-adhiṣṭhātror apy āha evam iti | devo golokas
tad-adhiṣṭhātṛ-śrī-govinda-rūpaḥ | sadānandam iti tat-svarūpam ity arthaḥ |
napuṃsakatvaṃ vijñānam ānandaṃ brahma iti śruteḥ | ātmārāmasya
anya-nirapekṣasya prakṛtyā māyayā na samāgamaḥ | yathoktaṃ dvitīye - na
yatra māyā kim utāpare harer anuvratā yatra surāsurārcitāḥ [BhP 2.9.10] ||6||
children.translated_text: Now we follow the root commentary. Just as the unity of the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic form) and its inner controller is described in the <s>Puruṣa-sūkta</s> etc. with the intention of their non-difference, so also regarding <s>Goloka</s> and its presiding deity, he says 'evam' (thus). 'Deva' (God) means <s>Goloka</s> in the form of its presiding deity, Śrī <s>Govinda</s>. 'Sat-ānanda' (eternal bliss) — that is His essential nature — this is the meaning. The neuter gender is from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Knowledge and bliss are <s>Brahman</s>.' 'Of the self-delighting one (<s>ātmārāma</s>)' — of the one who is self-sufficient — 'with <s>Prakṛti</s>' — with <s>Māyā</s> — 'there is no contact.' As stated in the Second [Canto]: 'Where there is no <s>Māyā</s>, much less anything else of <s>Hari</s> — where dwell the pure devotees worshipped by gods and demons' [BhP 2.9.10]. ||6||

children.text: māyayāramamāṇasya na viyogas tayā saha |
ātmanā ramayā reme tyakta-kālaṃ sisṛkṣayā | // BrS_5.11 //
children.translated_text: by His own self, with <s>Ramā</s> (the goddess of fortune), He delighted, having released time for the purpose of creation. // BrS 5.11 //
Of Him who sports with <s>Māyā</s>, there is no separation from her;

children.text: niyatiḥ sā ramā devi tat-priyā tad-vaśaṃ tadā ||7|| // BrS_5.12ab //
children.translated_text: That <s>Niyati</s> (the regulating power) is that <s>Ramā</s>, the goddess, His beloved, subject to His will then. ||7|| // BrS 5.12ab //

children.text:
atha prapañcātmanas tad-aṃśasya puruṣasya tu na tādṛśatvam ity āha
māyayeti | prākṛta-pralaye'pi tasmiṃs tasyālayāt yasyāṃśāṃśāṃśa-bhāgenety
ādeḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the cosmic aspect, who is His portion — [He] is not of the same nature — this he states with '<s>māyayā</s>' (with <s>Māyā</s>). Even at the time of the cosmic dissolution, since that [<s>Puruṣa</s>] rests in Him — as indicated by 'by a fraction of a fraction of a fraction of whose portion' etc.

children.text:
nanu tarhi jīvavat-tal-liptatvena aniīśvaratvaṃ syāt ? tatrāha ātmaneti | sa tu
ātmanā antarvṛtyā tu ramayā svarūpa-śaktyaiva reme ratiṃ prāpnoti | bahir
eva māyayā sevya ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Objection: Then, like the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), wouldn't He be tainted by that [<s>Māyā</s>] and thus not be the Lord? To this he responds with 'ātmanā' (by His own self): He indeed, by His own self, by His internal function, delights with <s>Ramā</s>, His own essential power (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>) alone. The meaning is: externally He is served by <s>Māyā</s>.

children.text: eṣa prapanna-varado ramayātma-śaktyā
yad yat kariṣyati gṛhīta-guṇāvatāraḥ || [BhP 3.9.23] iti tṛtīye brahma-stavāt |
children.translated_text: whatever He will do, assuming incarnations with the <s>guṇas</s>.' [BhP 3.9.23] — from <s>Brahmā</s>'s prayer in the Third [Canto].
'This granter of boons to the surrendered, with <s>Ramā</s>, His own power (<s>ātma-śakti</s>),

children.text:
atra -māyāṃ vyudasya cic-chaktyā kaivalye sthita ātmani [BhP 1.7.23] iti
prathame śrīmad-arjuna-vacanāt | tarhi tat-preraṇaṃ vinā kathaṃ sṛṣṭis
tatrāha | sisṛkṣayā sraṣṭum icchayā tyaktaḥ sṛṣṭy-arthaṃ prahitaḥ kālaḥ
yasmāt ramaṇāt tādṛśaṃ yathā syāt tathā reme | prathamānta-pāṭhas tu
sugamaḥ | tat prabhāva-rūpeṇa tenaiva sā sidhyatīti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here — from the statement of Śrī <s>Arjuna</s> in the First [Canto]: 'Having dispelled <s>Māyā</s> by His spiritual potency (<s>cit-śakti</s>), established in the Self, in absolute oneness' [BhP 1.7.23]. Then, without His instigation, how can creation [take place]? To this he responds: 'with the desire to create (<s>sisṛkṣayā</s>)' — with the wish to create, He released, i.e., sent forth for the purpose of creation, Time (<s>kāla</s>); from which sporting, He delighted in such a way. The reading with the first-person ending is straightforward. The sense is: by His own influence, that [creation] is accomplished.

children.text: prabhāvaṃ pauruṣaṃ prāhuḥ kālam eke yato bhayam [BhP 3.26.16]
children.translated_text: 'They say that power called <s>puruṣa</s> is Time (<s>kāla</s>), from which comes fear.' [BhP 3.26.16]

children.text: kāla-vṛttyā tu māyāyāṃ guṇa-mayyām adhokṣajaḥ |
puruṣeṇātma-bhūtena vīryam ādhatta vīryavān || [BhP 3.5.26] iti ca tṛtīyāt |
children.translated_text: the powerful one, impregnated [her] with virility through the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is His own self.' [BhP 3.5.26] — from the Third [Canto].
'By the action of Time upon <s>Māyā</s>, which consists of the <s>guṇas</s>, the Transcendent Lord (<s>Adhokṣaja</s>),

children.text:
nanu ramaiva sā kā tatrāha niyatir ity ardhena | niyamyate svayaṃ
bhagavatyeva nityatā bhavatīti niyatiḥ svarūpa-bhūtā tac-chaktiḥ | devī
dyotamānā sva-prakāśa-rūpā ity arthaḥ | tad-uktaṃ dvādaśe - anapāyinī
bhagavatī śrīḥ śākṣād ātmano hareḥ [BhP 12.11.20] iti | ṭīkā ca --
anapāyinī hareḥ śaktiḥ | tatra hetuḥ sākṣād ātmana iti svarūpasya
cid-rūpatvāt tasyās tad-abhedād ity arthaḥ | ity eṣā |
children.translated_text: Objection: If <s>Ramā</s> herself is that [<s>Niyati</s>], what is she? To this he responds with the half-verse '<s>niyatiḥ</s>' (the regulating power). <s>Niyati</s> — that which is regulated by the Lord Himself and becomes eternal — [she is] the power that is part of His essential nature. '<s>Devī</s>' means shining, self-luminous in nature — this is the meaning. As stated in the Twelfth [Canto]: 'The inseparable goddess <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), directly the Self of <s>Hari</s>' [BhP 12.11.20]. And the commentary: 'The inseparable power of <s>Hari</s>; the reason — "directly of the Self," because His essential nature is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>), and because she is non-different from that' — this is the meaning.

children.text:
atra sākṣāt-śabdena vilajjamānayā yasya sthātum īkṣā-pathe'muyā ity
ā̆dy-uktyā māyā neti dhvanitam | tatrānapāyitvaṃ yathā viṣṇu-purāṇe
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'directly' (<s>sākṣāt</s>), it is implied that <s>Māyā</s> is not [so], as indicated by the earlier statement 'She whose sight-path [was avoided by] the bashful one.' The inseparability is as [stated] in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: nityaiva sā jagan-mātā viṣṇoḥ śrīr anapāyinī
yathā sarva-gato viṣṇus tathaiveyaṃ dvijottamaḥ || [ViP 1.8.17] iti |
children.translated_text: just as <s>Viṣṇu</s> is all-pervading, so is she, O best of the twice-born.' [ViP 1.8.17]
'Eternal indeed is <s>Śrī</s>, the mother of the world, the inseparable [consort] of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: evaṃ yathā jagat-svāmī deva-devo janārdanaḥ |
avatāraṃ karoty eṣā tathā śrīs tat-sahāyinī || [ViP 1.9.142] iti ca |
children.translated_text: takes incarnation, so does <s>Śrī</s>, His companion.' [ViP 1.9.142]
'Just as the lord of the universe, the God of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: devatve deva-dehā sā mānuṣatve ca mānuṣī |
harer dehānṛ-rūpāṃ vai karoty eṣātmanas tanum || [ViP 1.9.145] iti ca |
children.translated_text: She makes her own body conform to the form of <s>Hari</s>'s body.' [ViP 1.9.145]
'When He is in divine form, she assumes a divine body; when He is in human form, she becomes human.

children.text: hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātre - na viṣṇunā vinā devī na hariḥ padmajāṃ vinā iti ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>: 'The goddess is not without <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nor is <s>Hari</s> without the lotus-born one (<s>Padmajā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>).'

children.text:
tal-liṅgaṃ bhagavān śambhur jyoti-rūpaḥ sanātanaḥ |
yā yoniḥ sāparā śaktiḥ kāmo bījaṃ mahad dhareḥ ||8|| // BrS_5.12 //
children.translated_text: The mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of that [Lord] is the Lord <s>Śambhu</s>, eternal, whose form is light. That which is the womb (<s>yoni</s>) is His other power (<s>śakti</s>). Desire (<s>kāma</s>) is the great seed of <s>Hari</s>. ||8|| // BrS 5.12 //

children.text:
nanu kutrāpi śiva-śaktyoḥ kāraṇatā śrūyate, tatra virāḍ-varṇanavat
kalpanayeti tad-aṅga-viśeṣatvenāha - tal-liṅgam iti | yasyāyutāyutāṃśāṃśe
viśva-śaktir iyaṃ sthitā iti viṣṇu-purāṇānusāreṇa prapañcātmanas
tasyamahā-bhagavad-aṃśasya svāṃśa-jyotir-ācchannatvād aprakaṭa-rūpasya
puruṣasya liṅgaṃ liṅga-sthānīyaḥ yaḥ prapañcotpādako'ṃśaḥ sa eva
śambhuḥ | anyas tu tad-āvirbhāva-viśeṣatvād eva śambhur ucyate ity arthaḥ |
vakṣyate ca kṣīraṃ yathā dadhi-vikāra-viśeṣa-yogād sañjāyate na tu tataḥ
pṛthag asti hetor ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Objection: Somewhere, the causality of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> is heard [in the scriptures]. To this he responds — just as the description of the <s>Virāṭ</s> [cosmic form] is through imagination — [here too] it is stated as a specific limb of that [Lord] with 'tal-liṅgam.' According to the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>: 'In a fraction of a fraction of ten-thousands of whose [portion], this cosmic power is situated' — the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the cosmic aspect, that great portion of the Lord, whose own partial radiance is concealed, whose form is unmanifest — His mark (<s>liṅga</s>), i.e., the representative — the portion that generates the material world — is <s>Śambhu</s> himself. But the other [<s>Śambhu</s>/<s>Śiva</s>] is called <s>Śambhu</s> because he is a specific manifestation of that — this is the meaning. And it will be stated: 'Just as milk, by the special combination of transformation, becomes yogurt — but [yogurt] is not separate from the cause [i.e., milk]' and so on.

children.text:
tathā tasya vīryāvadhāna-sthāna-rūpāyā māyāyā apy aprakaṭa-rūpāyā yā
yonir yoni-sthānīyo'ṃśaḥ saivāparā pradhānākhyā śaktir iti pūrvavat | tatra
ca hares tasya puruṣākhya-hary-aṃśasya kāmo bhavati sṛṣṭy-arthaṃ
tad-didiṛkṣā jāyate ity arthaḥ | tataś ca mahad iti sa-jīva-mahat-tattva-rūpaṃ
tu māyāyām iti tṛtīyāc ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: [This is derived] from 'in <s>Māyā</s>' being in the third [case]. ||8||

Similarly, of <s>Māyā</s> — which is the form of the receptacle of His potency and is of unmanifest form — that which is the source (<s>yoni</s>), the portion serving as the womb, that itself is the other (<s>aparā</s>) power called <s>Pradhāna</s>, as stated before. And there, desire (<s>kāma</s>) arises in <s>Hari</s>'s portion called <s>Puruṣa</s> for the purpose of creation — the meaning is that the desire to see [the creation] arises. And then, [the word] '<s>mahat</s>' refers to the form of the <s>mahat-tattva</s> (great principle) together with the <s>jīvas</s> (living beings)

children.text: liṅga-yony-ātmikā jātā imā māheśvarī-prajāḥ ||9|| // BrS_5.13 //
children.translated_text: These progeny of <s>Maheśvara</s> are born, consisting of <s>liṅga</s> (the male principle) and <s>yoni</s> (the female principle). ||9|| [BrS 5.13]

children.text: vastutas tu pūrvābhiprāyatvam evety āha liṅgety ardhena | māheśvarīḥ
māheśvaryaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: means 'belonging to <s>Maheśvara</s>.' ||9||
But in reality, it is precisely the purport of what was stated before — thus he says with the half-verse beginning with '<s>liṅga</s>.' '<s>Māheśvarīḥ</s>'

children.text:
śaktimān puruṣaḥ so 'yaṃ liṅga-rūpī maheśvaraḥ |
tasminnāvirabhūlliṅge mahā-viṣṇur jagat-patiḥ ||10|| // BrS_5.14 //
children.translated_text: That powerful <s>Puruṣa</s>, who has the form of <s>liṅga</s> (the creative principle), is <s>Maheśvara</s>. In that <s>liṅga</s>, <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of the world, manifested. ||10|| [BrS 5.14]

children.text:
śaktimān ity ardhena tad evānūdya tasmin pūrvoktāprakaṭa-rūpasya
prakaṭa-rūpatayāpunar abhivyaktir ity āha tasminn ity ardhena | tasmāl
liṅga-rūpī prapañcotpādakas tad-aṃśo'pi śaktimān puruṣocyate |
maheśvaro'py ucyate tataś ca tasmin bhūta-sūkṣma-paryantatāṃ prāpte liṅge
svayaṃ tad-aṃśī mahā-viṣṇur āvirabhūt prakaṭa-rūpeṇāvirbhavati | yato
jagatāṃ sarveṣāṃ parāvareṣāṃ jīvānāṃ sa eva patir iti || 10 ||
children.translated_text: He alone is the lord of all beings, higher and lower, of all worlds. ||10||

Having restated that very [point] with the half-verse beginning with '<s>śaktimān</s>,' he declares the re-manifestation of what was previously unmanifest into manifest form with the half-verse beginning with '<s>tasmin</s>.' Therefore, even that portion which has the form of <s>liṅga</s> and is the producer of the material world is called <s>Puruṣa</s> endowed with power, and is also called <s>Maheśvara</s>. And then, in that <s>liṅga</s> which had reached the extent of the subtle elements, <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s> Himself, the source of that portion, manifested — He appears in visible form. Because

children.text:
sahasra-śīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasra-pāt |
sahasra-bāhur viśvātmā sahasrāṃśaḥ sahasra-sūḥ ||11|| // BrS_5.14 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s> of a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet, a thousand arms, the soul of the universe, of a thousand portions, generator of a thousand. ||11|| [BrS 5.14]

children.text:
tad evaṃ rūpaṃ vivṛṇoti sahasra-śīrṣeti | sahasram aṃśā avatārā yasya sa
sahasrāṃśaḥ | sahasraṃ sūte sṛjati yaḥ sa sahasra-sūḥ |
sahasra-śabda-sarvatrāsaṅkhyatā-paraḥ | dvitīye ca tasyaiva rūpam idam
uktam -- ādyo'vatāraḥ puruṣaḥ parasya [BhP 2.6.42] iti | asya ṭīkāyāṃ - yasya
sahasra-śīrṣety ukto līlā-vigrahaḥ parasya bhūmnaḥ ādyo'vatāraḥ iti ||11||
children.translated_text: playful form is described as having a thousand heads — [He is] the first incarnation of the Supreme Infinite.' ||11||

He describes that very form with '<s>sahasra-śīrṣa</s>.' One whose portions (<s>aṃśas</s>), that is, incarnations (<s>avatāras</s>), are a thousand is '<s>sahasrāṃśa</s>.' One who generates (<s>sūte</s>), that is, creates a thousand, is '<s>sahasra-sū</s>.' The word '<s>sahasra</s>' (thousand) everywhere means 'innumerable.' And in the Second [Canto], this very form is described: 'The first incarnation of the Supreme is the <s>Puruṣa</s>' [BhP 2.6.42]. In its commentary: 'He whose

children.text:
nārāyaṇaḥ sa bhagavān āpas tasmāt sanātanāt |
āvirāsīt kāraṇārṇo nidhiḥ saṅkarṣaṇātmakaḥ |
yoga-nidrāṃ gatas tasmin sahasrāṃśaḥ svayaṃ mahān ||12|| // BrS_5.16 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — from that eternal One, the waters appeared as the ocean of causes (<s>kāraṇārṇava</s>), whose nature is <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>. Having entered <s>yoga-nidrā</s> (mystic sleep) therein, He Himself, the great One of a thousand portions. ||12|| [BrS 5.16]

children.text:
ayam eva kāraṇārṇavaśāyīty āha nārāyaṇa iti sārdhena | tāḥ āpa eva
kāraṇārṇo-nidhir āvirāsīt sa tu nārāyaṇaḥ saṅkarṣaṇātmakaḥ iti | pūrvaṃ
golokāvaraṇatayā yaś caturvyūha-madhye saṅkarṣaṇaḥ sammataḥ
tasyaivāṃśo'yam ity arthaḥ | tad uktaṃ -
children.translated_text: That this very One is the recline upon the causal ocean — this he states with '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' and the following half-verse. Those very waters appeared as the ocean of causes, and He is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose nature is <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>. The meaning is: He is a portion of that very <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> who is accepted as [one of the] four <s>Vyūhas</s>, previously [described] as the covering of <s>Goloka</s>. Thus it is stated—

children.text: āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai nara-sūnavaḥ |
children.translated_text: The waters are called '<s>Nāra</s>,' for the waters are indeed the progeny of <s>Nara</s>;

children.text: tasya tā ayanaṃ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||12||
children.translated_text: since they were His abode (<s>ayana</s>) in the beginning, therefore He is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. ||12||

children.text:
tad-roma-bila jāleṣu bījaṃ saṅkarṣaṇasya ca |
haimāny aṇḍāni jātāni mahā-bhūtāvṛtāni tu ||13|| // BrS_5.17 //
children.translated_text: In the network of His body-hair pores, and from the seed of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, golden eggs were born, covered by the great elements. ||13|| [BrS 5.17]

children.text:
tasmād eva brahmāṇḍānām utpattim āha tad rometi | tad iti tasyety arthaḥ
tasya saṅkarṣaṇātmakasya yad bījaṃ yoni-śaktāvadhyas taṃ tad eva pūrvaṃ
bhūta-sūkṣma-paryantatāṃ prāptaṃ sat paścāt tasya loma-bila-jāleṣu vivareṣu
antarbhūtaṃ ca sat haimāni aṇḍāni jātāni tāni cāpañcī-kṛtāṃśaiḥ
mahābhūtair jātānīty arthaḥ | tad uktaṃ daśame brahmaṇā -
children.translated_text: From that same [source] he describes the origin of the cosmic eggs with '<s>tad roma</s>' etc. '<s>Tat</s>' means 'of Him' — of that One whose nature is <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>. That which is the seed, the potency implanted in the womb (<s>yoni</s>) — that very [seed], having first reached the extent of the subtle elements, and then having entered within the network of pores of His body-hairs, the golden eggs were born. And those [eggs] were born covered by the great elements in their undifferentiated state — this is the meaning. Thus it is stated in the Tenth [Canto], in <s>Brahmā</s>'s [prayer]:

children.text: kvedṛg-vidhāvigaṇitāṇḍa-parāṇu-caryā-
vātādhva-roma-vivarasya ca te mahitvam || [BhP 10.14.11] iti |
children.translated_text: and of the wind-paths in the pores of Your body-hair?' [BhP 10.14.11].
'Where indeed is such greatness — of the movement of innumerable atomic egg[-universes],

children.text: tṛtīye ca -
children.translated_text: And in the Third [Canto]:

children.text: vikāraiḥ sahito yuktair viśeṣādibhir āvṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Combined and joined with the transformations (<s>vikāras</s>), covered by the specifics and other [elements],

children.text: āṇḍakośo bahir ayaṃ pañcāśat-koṭi-vistṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this egg-sheath (<s>āṇḍa-kośa</s>) extends fifty billion [<s>yojanas</s>];

children.text:
daśottarādhikair yatra praviṣṭaḥ paramāṇuvat |
lakṣyate 'ntar-gatāś cānye koṭiśo hy aṇḍa-rāśayaḥ || [BhP 3.11.39-40] iti ||13||
children.translated_text: entered therein like an atom, with ten-fold increasing [coverings], and within are seen other multitudes of eggs by the millions.' [BhP 3.11.39-40] ||13||

children.text: praty-aṇḍam evam ekāṃśād ekāṃśād viśati svayam | // BrS_5.18 //
children.translated_text: Thus, into each egg, from one portion after another, He Himself enters. [BrS 5.18]

children.text: sahasra-mūrdhā viśvātmā mahā-viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ ||14|| // BrS_5.18add //
children.translated_text: The thousand-headed One, the Soul of the universe, <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>, the eternal. ||14|| [BrS 5.18 add.]

children.text:
tataś ca teṣu brahmāṇḍeṣu pṛthak pṛthak svarūpaiḥ svarūpāntaraiḥ sa eva
praviveśety āha pratyaṇḍam iti | ekāṃśād ekāṃśād ekenaikenāṃśenety
arthaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: 'by each and every portion.' ||14||
And then, in each of those cosmic eggs, He Himself entered separately through His own forms and other forms — thus he says with '<s>pratyaṇḍam</s>.' 'From one portion after another' means

children.text:
vāmāṅgād asṛjad viṣṇuṃ dakṣiṇāṅgāt prajāpatim |
jyotir-liṅga-mayaṃ śambhuṃ kūrca-deśād avāsṛjat ||15|| // BrS_5.19 //
children.translated_text: From His left limb He created <s>Viṣṇu</s>; from His right limb, <s>Prajāpati</s>; and from the space between His eyebrows, He released <s>Śambhu</s>, whose nature is the <s>jyotir-liṅga</s> (luminous creative principle). ||15|| [BrS 5.19]

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃ cakāra tatrāha - vāmāṅgād iti | viṣṇv-ādaya ime sarveṣām eva
brahmāṇḍānāṃ pālakādayaḥ prati brahmāṇḍāntaḥ sthitānāṃ viṣṇv-ādīnāṃ
svāṃśānāṃ prayoktāraḥ | yathā prati-brahmāṇḍe tathā adhi
brahmāṇḍa-maṇḍalam abhyupagantavyam iti bhāvaḥ | yeṣu prajāpatir ayaṃ
hiraṇyagarbha-rūpa eva na tu vakṣyamāṇa-caturmukha-rūpa eva, so'yaṃ
tat-tad-āvaraṇa-gata-tat-tad-devānāṃ sraṣṭeti | viṣṇu-śambhū api
tat-tat-pālana-saṃhāra-kartārau jñeyau | kūrca-deśāt bhruvor madhyāt | eṣāṃ
jalāvaraṇa eva sthānāni jñeyāni || 15 ||
children.translated_text: of these [three] should be understood to be in the water-covering itself. ||15||

What did He further do there — he says with '<s>vāmāṅgāt</s>' etc. These <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others are the protectors etc. of all cosmic eggs, and are the directors of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others situated within each cosmic egg as His own portions. Just as [they function] in each cosmic egg, so too should they be understood [to function] over the entire realm of cosmic eggs — this is the purport. Among these, this <s>Prajāpati</s> is indeed in the form of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and not in the form of the four-faced one to be described later; he is the creator of the respective deities in the respective coverings [of each egg]. <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Śambhu</s> too should be known as the respective agents of maintenance and destruction. 'From the space between the eyebrows' means from the middle of the brows. The abodes

children.text: ahaṅkārātmakaṃ viśvaṃ tasmād etad vyajāyata ||16|| // BrS_5.20 //
children.translated_text: The universe, whose nature is <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), was born from him. ||16|| [BrS 5.20]

children.text: tatra śambhoḥ kāryāntaram apy āha ahaṅkārātmakam ity ardhena | etad
viśvaṃ tasmād evāhaṅkārātmakaṃ vyajāyata babhūva |
children.translated_text: universe was born from him as having the nature of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>;

children.text: viśvasyāhaṅkārātmakatā tasmāj jātety arthaḥ sarvāhaṅkārādhiṣṭhātṛtvāt
children.translated_text: the meaning is that the universe's nature as <s>ahaṅkāra</s> was born from him, because he is

children.text: tasya || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the presiding deity of all <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. ||16||
He states another effect of <s>Śambhu</s> with the half-verse '<s>ahaṅkārātmakam</s>.' This

children.text:
atha tais tri-vidhair veśair līlām udvahataḥ kila |
yoga-nidrā bhagavatī tasya śrīr iva saṅgatā ||17|| // BrS_5.21 //
children.translated_text: Then, as He carries out pastimes through those three forms, the divine <s>Yoga-nidrā</s> (mystic sleep), like <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune), was united with Him. ||17|| [BrS 5.21]

children.text:
brahmāṇḍa-praviṣṭasya tu tat-tad-rūpasya līlām āha atha tair ity ādi | tais tat
sadṛśais trividhaiḥ prati-brahmāṇḍa-gata-viṣṇv-ādibhir veśai rūpair līlāṃ
brahmāṇḍāntargata-pālanādi-rūpām udvahato
brahmāṇḍāntargata-puruṣasyeti tām udvahati | tasminn ity arthaḥ |
yoga-nidrā - pūrvokta-mahā-yoga-nidrāṃśa-bhūtā bhagavatī
children.translated_text: '<s>Yoga-nidrā</s>' — a portion of the previously mentioned great <s>yoga-nidrā</s>, '<s>bhagavatī</s>' (divine) —

children.text: svarūpānanda-samādhimayatvād antarbhūta-sarvaiśvaryā saṅgatā śrīr iveti |
children.translated_text: because her nature is the <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) of the bliss of one's own essential nature, with all sovereignty contained within, she was 'united' — 'like <s>Śrī</s>' means:

children.text: tatra yathā śrīr apy aṃśena saṅgatā tathā sāpīty arthaḥ ||17||
children.translated_text: just as <s>Śrī</s> too is united through a portion, so too is she — this is the meaning. ||17||

He describes the pastimes of the One who entered the cosmic egg in His various forms, beginning with '<s>atha taiḥ</s>' etc. Through those three similar forms — <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others situated within each cosmic egg — as He carries out the pastimes in the form of maintenance etc. within the cosmic egg — that is, of the <s>Puruṣa</s> within the cosmic egg who carries them out. 'In Him' — this is the meaning.

children.text:
sisṛkṣāyāṃ tato nābhes tasya padmaṃ viniryayau |
tan-nālaṃ hema-nalinaṃ brahmaṇo lokam adbhutam ||18|| // BrS_5.22 //
children.translated_text: Then, when the desire to create [arose], from His navel a lotus emerged; its stalk was a golden lotus — the wondrous world of <s>Brahmā</s>. ||18|| [BrS 5.22]

children.text: tataś ca sisṛkṣāyām iti | nālaṃ nāla-yuktaṃ tad-dhema-nalinaṃ brahmaṇo
janma-śayanayoḥ sthānatvāt loka ity arthaḥ ||18||
children.translated_text: both birth and repose of <s>Brahmā</s>, is called a 'world' — this is the meaning. ||18||
And then, 'when the desire to create [arose]' — '<s>nāla</s>' means 'possessing a stalk'; that golden lotus, being the place of

children.text: tattvāni pūrva-rūḍhāni kāraṇāni parasparam |
samavāyāprayogāc ca vibhinnāni pṛthak pṛthak || // BrS_5.23 //
children.translated_text: remained distinct and separate due to the non-application of their combination. [BrS 5.23]
The principles (<s>tattvas</s>), which had previously evolved, [being] causes of one another,

children.text:
cic-chaktyā sajjamāno 'tha bhagavān ādi-pūruṣaḥ |
yojayan māyayā devo yoga-nidrām akalpayat ||19|| // BrS_5.24 //
children.translated_text: Then the divine <s>Bhagavān</s>, the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, engaging through [His] <s>cit-śakti</s> (spiritual potency), joining [the <s>tattvas</s>] through <s>Māyā</s>, fashioned <s>yoga-nidrā</s>. ||19|| [BrS 5.24]

children.text:
tathā asaṅkhya-jīvātmakasya samaṣṭi-jīvasya prabodhaṃ vaktuṃ punaḥ
kāraṇārṇonidhi-śāyinas tṛtīya-skandhoktānusāriṇīṃ sṛṣṭi-prakriyāṃ
vivṛtyāha - tattvānīti trayeṇa | tatra dvayam āha - māyayā sva-śaktyā
parasparaṃ tattvāni yojayann iti yojanānantaram eva nirīhatayā yoga-nidrām
eva svīkṛtavān ity arthaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: accepted <s>yoga-nidrā</s> through His state of non-activity — this is the meaning. ||19||

To describe the awakening of the collective <s>jīva</s> (<s>samaṣṭi-jīva</s>) consisting of innumerable individual souls, he further elaborates the process of creation following the Third Canto, [describing that which pertains to] the One who reclines on the causal ocean — with these three [verses] beginning with '<s>tattvāni</s>.' Therein, he states two [points]: joining the principles through <s>Māyā</s>, His own power, one after another — and after that joining, He simply

children.text:
yojayitvā tu tāny eva praviveśa svayaṃ guhām |
guhāṃ praviṣṭe tasmiṃs tu jīvātmā pratibudhyate ||20|| // BrS_5.25 //
children.translated_text: Having joined those very [principles], He Himself entered the cavity (<s>guhā</s>). When He entered the cavity, the <s>jīvātmā</s> (individual soul) awakens. ||20|| [BrS 5.25]

children.text:
atha tṛtīyam āha yojayitveti | yojayitvā tad yojanā-yoga-nidrayor antarāle ity
arthaḥ | guhāḥ virāḍ-vigraham | pratibudhyate pralaya-svāpāj jāgarti || 20 ||
children.translated_text: Now he states the third [point] with '<s>yojayitvā</s>.' 'Having joined' — that joining takes place in the interval between the joining and the <s>yoga-nidrā</s> — this is the meaning. '<s>Guhā</s>' (cavity) means the cosmic body (<s>virāḍ-vigraha</s>). 'Awakens' means awakes from the sleep of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>). ||20||

children.text: sa nityo nitya-sambandhaḥ prakṛtiś ca paraiva sā ||21|| // BrS_5.26 //
children.translated_text: He is eternal, with an eternal connection, and that <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) is indeed the supreme [power]. ||21|| [BrS 5.26]

children.text:
jīvasya svābhāvikī sthitim āha sa nity ity ardheneti |
nityo'nādy-ananta-kāla-bhāvī nitya-sambandho bhagavatā saha samavāyo
yasya saḥ | sūryeṇa tad-raśmi-jālasyeveti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: He describes the natural state of the <s>jīva</s> with the half-verse '<s>sa nitya</s>' etc. 'Eternal' means existing through beginningless and endless time. 'With an eternal connection' means one who has an inseparable relation (<s>samavāya</s>) with <s>Bhagavān</s>. The purport is: like the network of rays with the sun.

children.text:
yat-taṭasthaṃ tu cid-rūpaṃ sva-saṃvedyād vinirgatam |
rañjitaṃ guṇa-rāgeṇa sa jīva iti kathyate || iti nārada-pañcarātrāt |
children.translated_text: 'That marginal (<s>taṭastha</s>) consciousness-form, which has emanated from the self-cognizing [<s>Brahman</s>], colored by the attachment of the <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities) — that is called the <s>jīva</s>.' — Thus from the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>.

children.text: mamaivāṃśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ || iti śrī-gītopaniṣadbhyaś ca |
children.translated_text: 'An eternal portion of Myself has become the <s>jīva</s> (living being) in the world of the living.' — And from the Śrī <s>Gītopaniṣad</s> [BG 15.7].

children.text:
ataiva prakṛtiḥ sākṣi-rūpeṇa svarūpa-sthita eva | sva-pratibimba-rūpeṇa
pramātṛ-rūpeṇa prakṛtim iva prāptaś cety arthaḥ | prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām
jīva-bhūtām iti śrī-gītāsv eva | dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā iti śrutiś ca
nitya-svarūpaṃ darśayati || 21 ||
children.translated_text: reveals the eternal essential nature. ||21||

Therefore, <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) remains in the essential nature as a witness. In the form of His own reflection, as the knower, He has, as it were, entered <s>Prakṛti</s>—this is the meaning. 'Know My higher <s>Prakṛti</s>, which has become the living beings'—in the <s>Śrī Gītā</s> itself. And the <s>śruti</s>: 'Two birds, companions, united [perch on the same tree]'

children.text:
evaṃ sarvātma-sambandhaṃ nābhyāṃ padmaṃ harer abhūt |
tatra brahmābhavad bhūyaś catur-vedi catur-mukhaḥ ||22|| // BrS_5.27 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the lotus of <s>Hari</s>, connected with all souls, arose from His navel; thereupon <s>Brahmā</s> came into being, four-faced, knower of the four <s>Vedas</s>. ||22|| // BrS 5.27 //

children.text:
atha tasya samaṣṭi-jīvāsthānaṃ guhā-praviṣṭāt puruṣād udbhūtam ity āha
evam iti | tataḥ samaṣṭi-dehābhimāninas tasya hiraṇya-garbha-brahmaṇas
tasmāt bhoga-vigrahotpattim āha tatreti || 22 ||
children.translated_text: He states the arising of the body of enjoyment with 'thereupon.' ||22||

Now He states that the abode of the aggregate <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) arose from the <s>Puruṣa</s> who entered the cave—with 'thus.' Then, of that <s>Hiraṇyagarbha-Brahma</s>, who identifies with the aggregate body—

children.text:
sa jāto bhagavac-chaktyā tat-kālaṃ kila coditaḥ |
sisṛkṣāyāṃ matiṃ cakre pūrva-saṃskāra-saṃskṛtaḥ |
dadarśa kevalaṃ dhvāntaṃ nānyat kim api sarvataḥ ||23|| // BrS_5.28 //
children.translated_text: He, born by the Lord's energy, being impelled at that time, endowed with previous impressions, set his mind upon creation, but saw only darkness all around, nothing else. ||23|| // BrS 5.28 //

children.text: atha tasya caturmukhasya ceṣṭām āha sa jāta ity sārdhena | spaṣṭam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: Now He describes the activity of that four-faced one with 'He, born' etc. in one and a half verses. Clear. ||23||

children.text:
uvāca puratas tasmai tasya divya sarasvatī |
kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya govinda he gopī-jana ity api |
vallabhāya priyā vahner mantram te dāsyati priyam ||24|| // BrS_5.29 //
children.translated_text: The divine <s>Sarasvatī</s> spoke before him: 'The <s>kāma</s>-[mantra]—<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, he <s>gopī-jana</s> (O people of the gopīs), <s>Vallabhāya</s> (to the beloved)—dear one, the fire will give you this beloved mantra.' ||24|| // BrS 5.29 //

children.text:
atha tasmin pūrvopāsanā-bhāgya-labdhāṃ bhagavat-kṛpām āhovāceti
sārdhena | spaṣṭam || 24 ||
children.translated_text: Now He relates the grace of the Lord obtained through the fortune of previous worship—with 'spoke' etc. in one and a half verses. Clear. ||24||

children.text: tapas tvaṃ tapa etena tava siddhir bhaviṣyati ||25|| // BrS_5.30 //
children.translated_text: 'Perform <s>tapas</s> (austerity); by this your perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) will come about.' ||25|| // BrS 5.30 //

children.text:
etad eva sparśeṣu yat ṣoḍaśam ekaviṃśam iti tṛtīya-skandhānusāreṇa yojayati
tapa tvaṃ ity ardhena | spaṣṭam || 25 ||
children.translated_text: This very thing—'that which among the consonants is the sixteenth and twenty-first'—He connects according to the Third Canto with 'perform <s>tapas</s>' etc. in half a verse. Clear. ||25||

children.text: atha tepe sa suciraṃ prīṇan govindam avyayam |
śvetadvīpa-patiṃ kṛṣṇaṃ goloka-sthaṃ parāt param || // BrS_5.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lord of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, dwelling in <s>Goloka</s>, the Supreme beyond the supreme, // BrS 5.31 //
Then he performed <s>tapas</s> for a very long time, pleasing the imperishable <s>Govinda</s>,

children.text: prakṛtyā guṇa-rūpiṇyā rūpiṇyā paryupāsitam |
sahasra-dala-sampanne koṭi-kiñjalka-bṛṃhite || // BrS_5.32 //
children.translated_text: on a thousand-petalled [lotus], adorned with tens of millions of filaments, // BrS 5.32 //
worshipped all around by <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature) in her embodied form, endowed with the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),

children.text: bhūmiś cintāmaṇis tatra karṇikāre mahāsane |
samāsīnaṃ cid-ānandaṃ jyoti-rūpaṃ sanātanam || // BrS_5.33 //
children.translated_text: seated—He who is consciousness and bliss (<s>cid-ānanda</s>), of the form of light, eternal, // BrS 5.33 //
where the ground is <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), on the great throne in the whorl of the lotus,

children.text:
śabda-brahma-mayaṃ veṇuṃ vādayantaṃ mukhāmbuje |
vilāsinī-gaṇa-vṛtaṃ svaiḥ svair aṃśair abhiṣṭutam ||26|| // BrS_5.34 //
children.translated_text: playing the flute made of the sound-<s>Brahman</s> on His lotus-mouth, surrounded by a host of playful women (<s>vilāsinīs</s>), praised by His own portions. ||26|| // BrS 5.34 //

children.text:
sa tu tena mantreṇa sva-kāmanā-viśeṣānusārāt sṛṣṭikṛt-śakti-viśiṣṭatayā
vakṣyamāṇas tavānusārāt gokulākhya-pīṭha-gatatayā śrī-govindam
upāsitavān ity āha -- atha tepe ity ādi caturbhiḥ | guṇa-rūpiṇyā
sattva-rajas-tamo-guṇa-mayyā rūpiṇyā mūrtimatyā paryupāsitaṃ paritas tad
gokulād bahiḥ-sthitayopāsitam dhyānādinā arcitam | māyā parety abhimukhe
ca vilajjamānā [BhP 2.7.47] iti | balim udvahanty ajayā nimiṣā iti ca
śrī-bhāgavatāt | aṃśais tad-āvaraṇa-sthaiḥ parikaraiḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: He, by that mantra, in accordance with the specifics of his own desire, endowed with the creative energy—as will be stated—according to your instructions, worshipped <s>Śrī Govinda</s> as situated on the throne called <s>Gokula</s>—thus He says with 'then he performed <s>tapas</s>' etc. in four verses. 'Endowed with the <s>guṇas</s>': constituted of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. 'Embodied': having a form. 'Worshipped all around': situated outside that <s>Gokula</s>, worshipping through meditation and other practices. '<s>Māyā</s>, facing the Supreme, stands ashamed' [BhP 2.7.47]. 'She who brings tribute, the unborn, in a moment'—from the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>. 'By His portions': by the attendants stationed in those coverings. ||26||

children.text: atha veṇu-ninādasya trayī-mūrti-mayī gatiḥ |
sphurantī praviveśāśu mukhābjāni svayambhuvaḥ || // BrS_5.35 //
children.translated_text: shining forth, swiftly entered the lotus-mouths of <s>Svayambhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). // BrS 5.35 //
Then the melody of the flute, in the form of the threefold Vedic revelation (<s>trayī-mūrti</s>),

children.text:
gāyatrīṃ gāyatas tasmād adhigatya sarojajaḥ |
saṃskṛtaś cādi-gunuṇā dvijatām agamat tataḥ ||27|| // BrS_5.36 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained the <s>Gāyatrī</s> from that sound, the lotus-born one, singing it, consecrated by the original <s>guru</s>, thereupon attained the status of twice-born. ||27|| // BrS 5.36 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ dīkṣātaḥ parastād eva tasya dhruvasyeva dvijatva-saṃskāras
tad-ārādhitāt tan-mantrādhidevāj jātaḥ ity āha atha veṇv iti dvayena |
trayī-mūrtir gāyatrī veda-mātṛtvāt | dvitīya padye tasya eva vyaktibhāvitvāc
ca | tan-mayī gatiḥ paripāṭī | mukhābjāni praviveśety aṣṭa-karṇaiḥ
praviveśety arthaḥ | ādi-guruṇā śrī-kṛṣṇena ||27||
children.translated_text: Thus, after the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), the twice-born consecration came to him, like <s>Dhruva</s>'s, born from the presiding deity of that mantra whom he worshipped—thus He says with 'then the flute' etc. in two verses. 'The threefold form' is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, because of being the mother of the <s>Vedas</s>. In the second verse, because of its becoming manifest. 'Its melody': sequence. 'Entered the lotus-mouths': entered through eight ears—this is the meaning. 'By the original <s>guru</s>': by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||27||

children.text:
trayyā prabuddho 'tha vidhir vījñāta-tattva-sāgaraḥ |
tuṣṭāva veda-sāreṇa stotreṇānena keśavam ||28|| // BrS_5.37 //
children.translated_text: Awakened by the threefold [Vedic revelation], <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), having understood the ocean of truth, praised <s>Keśava</s> with this hymn, the essence of the <s>Vedas</s>. ||28|| // BrS 5.37 //

children.text:
tataś ca trayīm api tasmāt prāpya tam eva tuṣṭāvety āha trayyeti | keśān
aṃśūna vayati vistārayatīti keśavas tam |
children.translated_text: And then, having also obtained the threefold <s>Veda</s> from Him, he praised that very one—thus He says with 'by the threefold' etc. '<s>Keśava</s>': He who spreads out His rays (<s>keśas</s>, i.e., <s>aṃśus</s>)—Him.

children.text: aṃśavo ye prakāśante mam te keśa-saṃjñitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those portions that shine forth from Me are called My rays (<s>keśas</s>);

children.text: sarvajñāḥ keśavaṃ tasmān mām āhur muni-sattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the omniscient sages call Me <s>Keśava</s>.'

children.text: iti sahasra-nāma-bhāṣyotthāpita-keśava-niruktau bhārata-vacanāt || 28 ||
children.translated_text: From the statement of the <s>Bhārata</s>, as cited in the <s>Sahasra-nāma-bhāṣya</s> (commentary on the Thousand Names), the etymology of <s>Keśava</s>. ||28||

children.text:
cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa-
lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhir abhipālayantam |
lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||29|| // BrS_5.38 //
children.translated_text: In abodes made of clusters of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems, surrounded by millions of wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-vṛkṣas</s>), tending the <s>surabhī</s> cows, served with great reverence by hundreds of thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s>—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||29|| // BrS 5.38 //

children.text:
stutim āha cintāmaṇīty ādibhiḥ | tatra goloke'smin mantra-bhedena
tad-eka-deśeṣu bṛhad-dhyāna-mayādiṣv ekasyāpi mantrasya rāsa-mayādiṣu
ca pīṭheṣu satsv api madhyasthatvena mukhyatayā prathamaṃ
golokākhya-pīṭha-nivāsa-yogya-līlayā stauti cintāmṇīty ekena |
children.translated_text: He states the hymn with '<s>cintāmaṇi</s>' etc. There, in this <s>Goloka</s>, although through differences in mantras there are various thrones in its different regions—beginning with the <s>bṛhad-dhyāna</s> and including the <s>rāsa</s> and other thrones—yet primarily, as the central one, He first praises the pastime appropriate for the chief throne called <s>Goloka</s>, with '<s>cintāmaṇi</s>' in one verse.

children.text:
abhi sarvato-bhāvena
vana-nayana-cāraṇa-go-sthānānayana-sambhālana-prakāreṇa pālayantaṃ
sa-snehaṃ rakṣantam | kadācid rahasi tu vailakṣaṇyam ity āha lakṣmīti
lakṣmyo'tra gopa-sundarya eveti vyākhyātam eva ||29||
children.translated_text: The <s>Lakṣmīs</s> here are indeed the beautiful cowherd women (<s>gopa-sundarīs</s>)—this has already been explained. ||29||

'<s>Abhi</s>' means 'in every manner'—tending, meaning lovingly protecting, through the manner of forest-roaming, cow-herding, and caring for them. But sometimes in privacy there is a special character—thus He says '<s>Lakṣmī</s>' etc.

children.text:
veṇuṃ kvaṇantam aravinda-dalāyatākṣam-
barhāvataṃsam asitāmbuda-sundarāṅgam |
kandarpa-koṭi-kamanīya-viśeṣa-śobhaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||30|| // BrS_5.39 //
children.translated_text: Playing the flute, with eyes extended like lotus petals, wearing a peacock feather as a crest-ornament, with a beautiful form like a dark rain-cloud, with special beauty captivating tens of millions of <s>Kandarpa</s>s (gods of love)—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||30|| // BrS 5.39 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadma-mayīṃ kathā-gānaṃ nāṭyaṃ gamanam
apīti vakṣyamāṇānusāreṇa golokhākhya-vilakṣaṇa-pīṭha-gatāṃ līlām uktvā
eka-sthāna-sthitikāṃ kathā-gānādi-rahitāṃ bṛhad-dhyānādi-dṛṣṭāṃ
dvitīya-pīṭha-gatāṃ līlām āha veṇum iti dvayena | veṇum iti tatra
spaṣṭam ||30||
children.translated_text: it is clear. ||30||

Thus, having described the pastime appropriate to the distinctive throne called <s>Goloka</s>—which includes narration, song, dance, and walking, as will be stated—using abodes of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> clusters, He now describes the pastime of the second throne, which involves being in one place, without narration and song, as seen in the <s>bṛhad-dhyāna</s> etc., with 'flute' etc. in two verses. 'The flute'—therein

children.text:
ālola-candraka-lasad-vanamālya-vaṃśī-
ratnāṅgadaṃ praṇaya-keli-kalā-vilāsam |
śyāmaṃ tri-bhaṅga-lalitaṃ niyata-prakāśaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||31|| // BrS_5.40 //
children.translated_text: With a swaying moon-crescent, a shining forest garland, a flute, jeweled armlets, the art of amorous play full of love, dark-complexioned, gracefully bent in three places (<s>tri-bhaṅga</s>), of eternally manifest splendor—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||31|| // BrS 5.40 //

children.text: ālolety ādi | praṇaya-pūrvako yaḥ keli-parihāsas tatra yā vaidagdhī saiva
vilāso yasya taṃ, drava-keli-parīhāsā ity amaraḥ ||31||
children.translated_text: is the charm (<s>vilāsa</s>) of Him—'<s>drava</s>, <s>keli</s>, <s>parīhāsa</s>' are synonyms, according to the <s>Amara-koṣa</s>. ||31||
'Swaying' etc. That which is love-preceded jesting (<s>keli</s>), therein the skill (<s>vaidagdhya</s>) itself

children.text:
aṅgāni yasya sakalendriya-vṛtti-manti
paśyanti pānti kalayanti ciraṃ jaganti |
ānanda-cinmaya-sad-ujjvala-vigrahasya
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||32|| // BrS_5.41 //
children.translated_text: He whose limbs function as all the senses, who sees, protects, and regulates the worlds eternally, whose form is of bliss, consciousness, existence, and radiant splendor—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||32|| // BrS 5.41 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ līlā-dvayam uktvā paramācintya-śaktyā vaibhava-viśeṣān āha
aṅgānīti caturbhiḥ | tatra śrī-vigrahasya aṅgāni hasto'pi draṣṭuṃ śaknoti,
cakṣur api pālayituṃ pārayati, tathā anyad anyad apy aṅgam anyad anyat
kalayituṃ prabhavatīti | evam evoktaṃ - sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṃ tat
sarvato'kṣi-śiro-mukham ity ādi | jagantīti | līlā-parikareṣu tat-tad-aṅgaṃ
yathā-svam eva vyavaharatīti bhāvaḥ | tatra ca tasya vigrahasya vailakṣaṇyam
eva hetur ity āha ānandeti ||32||
children.translated_text: is the cause—thus He says 'of bliss' etc. ||32||

Thus, having described the twofold pastime, He now describes the special glories through supremely inconceivable energy with 'limbs' etc. in four verses. There, of the divine form—the limbs: even the hand can see, even the eye can protect; likewise, every other limb has the power to perform every other function. Thus indeed it is said: 'With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,' etc. 'The worlds'—among the play-companions, each limb functions in its own way—this is the purport. And therein, the uniqueness of His form itself

children.text:
advaitam acyutam anādim ananta-rūpam
ādyaṃ purāṇa-puruṣaṃ nava-yauvanaṃ ca |
vedeṣu durlabham adurlabham ātma-bhaktau
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||33|| // BrS_5.42 //
children.translated_text: Without a second (<s>advaita</s>), infallible (<s>acyuta</s>), without beginning, of infinite forms, the original, ancient Person yet ever-youthful, difficult to find through the <s>Vedas</s> but easily found through devotion to the Self—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||33|| // BrS 5.42 //

children.text:
vailakṣaṇyam eva puṣṇāti advaitam iti tribhiḥ | advaitaṃ pṛthivyā mayam
advaito rājetvad atulyam ity arthaḥ | vismāpanaṃ svasya ca
tṛtīya-sthasyoddhava-vākyāt | acyutaṃ
children.translated_text: He elaborates the uniqueness with 'without a second' etc. in three verses. '<s>Advaita</s>': pervading the earth, unequalled like a king—this is the meaning. Astonishing for Himself and for the third-person observer—from the words of <s>Uddhava</s>. '<s>Acyuta</s>' (infallible)—

children.text:
na cyavante hi yad bhaktāḥ mahatyāṃ pralayāpadi |
ato'cyuto'khile loke sa ekaḥ sarvago'vyayaḥ || iti kāśī-kāṇḍa-vacanāt |
children.translated_text: 'Since His devotees do not fall even in the great calamity of dissolution, therefore He alone, all-pervading and imperishable, is called <s>Acyuta</s> in the entire world'—from the statement of the <s>Kāśī-khaṇḍa</s>.

children.text: kaṃso batādyākṛtam ety anugrahaṃ
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṃsa</s>, alas, today obtains that grace—

children.text: drakṣye'ṅghri-padmaṃ prahito'munā hareḥ |
children.translated_text: I shall see the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s>, sent by him,

children.text: kṛtāvatārasya duratyayaṃ tamaḥ
children.translated_text: who has made His descent, whose impenetrable darkness

children.text: pūrve'taran yan nakha-maṇḍala-tviṣā ||
children.translated_text: the ancients crossed by the radiance of His toenails.'

children.text:
yad-arcitaṃ brahma-bhavādibhiḥ suraiḥ śriyā ca ity ādi
daśama-sthākrūra-vākyān |
children.translated_text: 'Which is worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and other gods, and by <s>Śrī</s>'—etc., from the words of <s>Akrūra</s> in the Tenth Canto.

children.text: yā vai śriyārcitam ajādibhir āpta-kāmair
children.translated_text: 'That which was worshipped by <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), by <s>Aja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others whose desires are fulfilled,

children.text: yogeśvarair api yad ātmani rāsa-goṣṭhyām |
children.translated_text: by the masters of <s>Yoga</s> also, within their own selves, in the <s>rāsa</s>-dance assembly—

children.text: kṛṣṇasya tad bhagavataś caraṇāravindaṃ
children.translated_text: the lotus feet of that Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>—

children.text: nyastaṃ staneṣu vijahuḥ parirabhya tāpam || [BhP 10.47.62] iti
śrīmad-uddhava-vākyam |
darśayāmāsa lokaṃ svaṃ gopānāṃ tamasaḥ param [BhP 10.28.14] ity uktvā,

nandādayas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā
paramānanda-nirvṛtāḥ |
kṛṣṇaṃ ca tatra cchandobhiḥ
stūyamānaṃ suvismitāḥ || [BhP 10.28.17] iti śrī-śuka-vākyāc ca |

anādim ity ādi-trayaṃ yathaikādaśa-sāṅkhya-kathane, kālo māyā-maye jīvaḥ
[BhP 11.24.27] ity ādau mahā-pralaye sarvāvaśiṣṭatvena brahmopadiśya tadāpi
tasya draṣṭṛtvaṃ svayaṃ bhagavān svasminn āha --
eṣa sāṅkhya-vidhiḥ proktaḥ saṃśaya-granthi-bhedanaḥ |
pratilomānulomābhyāṃ parāvara-dṛśā mayā || [BhP 11.24.29] iti |

purāṇa puruṣaḥ -- ekas tvam ātmā puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ [BhP 10.14.20] iti
brahma-vākyāt gūḍhaḥ purāṇa-puruṣo vana-citra-mālyaḥ [BhP 7.15.58] iti
māthura-vākyāc ca |

tathāpi nava-yauvanaṃ -- purāpi navaḥ purāṇa iti nirukteḥ | gopyas tapaḥ kim
acaran yad amuṣya rūpam [BhP 10.44.14] ity ādau | anusavābhinavaṃ iti
daśamāt | yasyānanaṃ makara-kuṇḍalādi nityotsavam [BhP 9.24.65] iti
navamāt | satyaṃ śaucam ity ādau saubhaga-kānty-ādīn paṭhitvā,
ete cānye ca bhagavan nityā yatra mahā-guṇāḥ |
prārthyā mahattvam icchadbhir na viyanti sma karhicit || [BhP 1.16.3] iti
prathamāt |

bṛhad-dhyānādau tathā śravaṇāt -- gopa-veśam abhrābhaṃ taruṇaṃ
kalpa-drumāśritam [GTU 1.8] iti tāpanī-śrutau | tad-dhyāne taruṇa-śabdasya
nava-yauvana eva śobhā vidhānatvena tātparyāt |

vedeṣu durlabhaṃ -- bhejur mukunda-padavīṃ śrutibhir vimṛgyām
[BhP 10.47.61] iti | adyāpi yat-pada-rajaḥ śruti-mṛgyam eva [BhP 10.14.34] iti
ca śrī-daśamāt |
adurlabham ātma-bhaktau -- bhaktyāham ekayā grāhyaḥ [BhP 11.14.11] ity
ekādaśāt | pureha bhūman [BhP 10.14.5] ity ādi śrī-daśamāc ca |

yad vā, nanu tasyātulyatve kim iti svārthaḥ | kathaṃ vātulyatvaṃ
nija-bhaktebhyaḥ ātmano dehasyāpi pradānāt | kiṃ vāvaśiṣyata ity āha
acyutam iti | nija-bhaktebhya ātma-pradānādināpi na vidyate cyutir yasya
sadaiva eka-rasam ity arthaḥ | tarhi kiṃ nārāyaṇaṃ stauṣi tasyaivācyutatvād
anādeś ca nety āha anādim iti na vidyate ādir yasya yasmād vā sarveṣāṃ
parama-kāraṇaṃ svayaṃ tu sva-prakāśaṃ kāraṇa-śūnyam ity arthaḥ | nanv
ekena kathaṃ sarveṣāṃ paripālanaṃ ghaṭate ity ata āha ananteti | anantaṃ
rūpaṃ yasya | athavā prapañca-gatatvena nāsty anto yasya | athavā anantasya
rūpaṃ svarūpaṃ yasya | yasmād evāṃśenānantādīnām utpattiḥ |

nanu nārāyaṇād evānantādi prākāṭya-prasiddhir ity āha ādyaṃ yasya
vilāsa-rūpo nārāyaṇas tam | nanu jñātaṃ tasyaiva puruṣākhyānaṃ, nety āha
purāṇeti yasya vilāsa-vapuḥ puruṣākhyas taṃ nanv āyātaṃ tasya vṛddhatvam
ity āha nava-yauvanam iti kaiśoram ity arthaḥ | ca-kārāt ya eva purātanaḥ |
sa eva kiśora-vayā ity anirvacanatvaṃ nityatvaṃ ca | nanu vedeṣu nārāyaṇa eva
gīyate ity āha | vedeṣv iti vedais tattvaṃ jñāyate cet teṣu sulabham ity arthaḥ |
bhaktiṃ vinā na jñāyate ity āha adurlabham iti || 33 ||

panthās tu koṭi-śata-vatsara-sampragamyo
vāyor athāpi manaso muni-puṅgavānām |
so 'py asti yat-prapada-sīmny avicintya-tattve
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||34|| // BrS_5.43 //
panthās tv iti prapada-sīmni caraṇāravindayor agre |
citraṃ bataid ekena vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak |
gṛheṣu dvy-aṣṭa-sāhasraṃ striya eka udāvahat || [BhP 10.69.2]
eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣṇa īḍya
eko'pi san bahudhā yo'vabhāti | [GTU 1.19] iti gopāla-tāpanyām |

tatra siddhāntam āha avicintya-tattve iti | ātmeśvaro'tarkya-sahasra-śaktiḥ iti
tṛtīyāt |
acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃs tarkena yojayet |
prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṃ yac ca tad acintyasya lakṣaṇam || [Mbh 6.6.11] iti skāndād
bhāratāc ca |
śrutes tu śabda-mūlatvāt [Vs 2.1.27] iti brahma-sūtrāt | acintyo hi
maṇi-mantra-mahauṣadhīnāṃ prabhāvaḥ iti bhāṣya-yukteś ceti bhāvaḥ || 34 ||

eko 'py asau racayituṃ jagad-aṇḍa-koṭiṃ
yac-chaktir asti jagad-aṇḍa-cayā yad-antaḥ |
aṇḍāntara-stha-paramāṇu-cayāntara-stham-
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||35|| // BrS_5.44 //
acintya-śaktim āha - eko'py asāv iti |
tāvat sarve vatsa-pālāḥ paśyato'jasya tat-kṣaṇāt |
vyadṛśyanta ghana-śyāmāḥ pīta-kauśeya-vāsasaḥ || [BhP 10.13.46]

ity ārabhya taiḥ vatsa-pālādibhir
evānanta-brahmāṇḍa-sāmagrī-yuta-tat-tadhi-puruṣāṇāṃ tenāvirbhāvanāt |
jagad-aṇḍa-cayā iti na cāntar na bahir yasya [BhP 10.9.13] ity ādeḥ | aṇor
aṇīyān mahato mahīyān [ŚvetU 3.20] ity ādi śruteḥ | yo'sau sarveṣu bhūteṣu
āviśya bhūtāni vidadhāti sa vo hi svāmī bhavati [GTU 2.22] | yo'sau
sarva-bhūtātmā gopālaḥ [GTU 2.94] | eko devaḥ sarva-bhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ [GTU
2.96] ity ādi tāpanībhyaḥ ||35||

yad-bhāva-bhāvita-dhiyo manujās tathaiva
samprāpya rūpa-mahimāsana-yāna-bhūṣāḥ |
sūktair yam eva nigama-prathitaiḥ stuvanti
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||36|| // BrS_5.45 //

atha tasya sādhaka-cayeṣv api bhakteṣu vadānyatvaṃ vadann ity eṣu
kaimutyam āha yad-bhāveti | yathā samāna-guṇa-śīla-vayo-vilāsa-veśaiś cety
āgama-rītyā nitya-tat-saṅgināṃ tat sāmyaṃ śrūyate tathaiva sambhāvyety
arthaḥ -
vaireṇa yaṃ nṛpatayaḥ śiśupāla-pauṇḍra-
śālvādayo gati-vilāsa-vilokanādyaiḥ |
dhyāyanta ākṛta-dhiyaḥ śayanāsanādau
tat-sāmyam āpur anurakta-dhiyāṃ punaḥ kim || [BhP 11.5.48] ity ekādaśāt ||

ānanda-cinmaya-rasa-pratibhāvitābhis
tābhir ya eva nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ |
goloka eva nivasaty akhilātma-bhūto
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||37|| // BrS_5.46 //

tat-preyasīnāṃ tu kiṃ vaktavyam, yataḥ parama-śrīṇāṃ tāsāṃ sāhityenaiva
tasya tal-loke vāsa ity āha ānandeti | akhilānāṃ goloka-vāsināṃ anyeṣām api
priya-vargānāṃ ātma-bhūtaḥ parama-preṣṭhatayātmavad avyabhicāry api
tābhir eva saha nivasatīti tāsām atiśayitvaṃ darśitam | atra hetuḥ - kalābhiḥ
hlādinī-śakti-vṛtti-rūpābhiḥ | atrāpi vaiśiṣṭyam āha - ānanda-cinmayo yo
rasaḥ, parama-prema-maya ujvvala-nāmā, tena prati bhāvitābhiḥ | pūrvaṃ
tāvat tāsāṃ tan-nāmnā rasena so'yaṃ bhāvito vāsito jātaḥ | tataś ca tena yāḥ
pratibhāvitā jātāḥ, tābhiḥ saha ity arthaḥ | pratiśabdāl labhyate | yathā
praty-upakṛtaḥ sa ity ukteḥ | tasya prāg-upakāritvam āyāti tadvat tatrāpi
nija-rūpatayā sva-dāratvenaiva na tu prakaṭa-līlāvat
para-dāratva-vyavahāreṇety arthaḥ | parama-lakṣmīṇāṃ tāsāṃ
tat-para-dāratvāsambhavād asya sva-dāratva-maya-rasasya
kautukāvaguṇṭhitatayā saumutkaṇṭhā poṣaṇārthaṃ prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ
māyayaiva tādṛśatvaṃ vyañjitam iti bhāvaḥ | ya eva ity eva-kāreṇa yat
prāpañcika-prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ tāsu para-dāratā-vyavahāreṇa nivasati so'yaṃ ya
eva tad-aprakaṭa-līlāyāṃ tāsu para-dāratā vyavahāreṇa nivasati so'yaṃ ya eva
tad-aprakaṭa-līlāspade goloke nija-rūpatā-vyavahāreṇa nivasatīti vyajyate |
tathā ca vyākhyātaṃ gautamīya-tantre
tad-aprakaṭa-nitya-līlā-śīlana-daśārṇa-vyākhyāne - aneka-janma-siddhānām
ity ādau darśitam eva | goloka evety eva-kāreṇa seyaṃ līlā tu kvāpi nānyatra
vidyate iti prakāśyate || 37 ||
children.translated_text: this is revealed. ||37||

As for His beloveds, what more need be said? Since those possessing supreme <s>Śrī</s> (fortune) — it is only in their company that He resides in that world — this he states with 'ānanda.' He who is the very self (<s>ātma-bhūta</s>) of all the residents of <s>Goloka</s> and other groups of dear ones — as their supreme beloved, inseparable like their own self — yet He dwells with them alone, showing their superiority. The reason: 'with <s>kalās</s> (portions)' — [meaning] with the functions of the <s>hlādinī-śakti</s> (pleasure potency). Even here a distinction is made: the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic relish) that is made of bliss and consciousness (<s>ānanda-cinmaya</s>), the one called <s>ujjvala</s> (brilliant), made of supreme love (<s>parama-prema</s>) — 'with those who are imbued (bhāvita) by that.' First, He was imbued — made fragrant — by that <s>rasa</s> named after them; and then those who were reciprocally imbued by Him — with them — this is the meaning. This is derived from the prefix 'prati' (in return); just as when it is said 'he was reciprocally helped,' it implies His prior beneficence — similarly here too, in His own original form, as His own consorts (<s>sva-dāra</s>) only, not with the conduct of being others' wives (<s>para-dāra</s>) as in the manifest pastimes — this is the meaning. Since the notion of being others' wives is impossible for those who are the supreme goddesses of fortune, and since the <s>rasa</s> consisting of His own conjugal love is veiled by sportive curiosity to nourish mutual longing — in the manifest pastimes, such an appearance is suggested by <s>māyā</s> (grace) alone — this is the purport. By the emphatic particle 'eva' in 'ya eva' — He who in the manifest worldly pastimes dwells among them with the conduct of [others'] wives — this very same one, in the unmanifest pastimes at <s>Goloka</s>, dwells with the conduct of His own original relationship — this is implied. And so it is explained in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>, in the commentary on the ten syllables of the unmanifest eternal pastimes — as shown in the passage beginning 'of those perfected through many births.' By the emphatic 'eva' in '<s>Goloka</s> eva' — this pastime indeed exists nowhere else —

children.text:
premāñjana-cchurita-bhakti-vilocanena
santaḥ sadaiva hṛdayeṣu vilokayanti |
yaṃ śyāmasundaram acintya-guṇa-svarūpaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||38|| // BrS_5.47 //
children.translated_text: With eyes anointed with the salve of love, the saints always behold Him in their hearts — Him, the beautiful dark one (<s>Śyāmasundara</s>), whose nature is inconceivable qualities. I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the original Person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). ||38|| // BrS 5.47 //

children.text:
yadyapi goloka eva nivasati tathāpi premāñjaneti | acintya-guṇa-svarūpam api
premākhyaṃ yad añjana-cchuritavad uccaiḥ prakāśamānaṃ
bhakti-rūpa-vilocanaṃ tenety arthaḥ | tena pratibimbavad dūrād apy uditaṃ
hṛdaye manasy api paśyantīty arthaḥ | bhaktir atra samādhiḥ | tad uktaṃ
śrī-gītāsu - ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham [Gītā 9.29]
children.translated_text: Although He resides in <s>Goloka</s> alone, yet [He is perceived] — thus '<s>premāñjana</s>' (with the ointment of love). Although His nature is of inconceivable qualities, the devotional eye (<s>bhakti-rūpa-vilocana</s>), which shines forth brilliantly like [being anointed with] the ointment called <s>prema</s> (love) — by that [eye] — this is the meaning. By that, even from afar, like a reflection, [He] arises in the heart and mind — they see [Him] — this is the meaning. <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) here means <s>samādhi</s> (deep absorption). As stated in the Śrī <s>Gītā</s>: 'Those who worship Me with devotion — I am in them, and they are in Me.' [<s>Gītā</s> 9.29]

children.text:
rāmādi-mūrtiṣu kalā-niyamena tiṣṭhan
nānāvatāram akarod bhuvaneṣu kintu |
kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ samabhavat paramaḥ pumān yo
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||39|| // BrS_5.48 //
children.translated_text: Abiding in the forms of <s>Rāma</s> and others by a regulated distribution of powers (<s>kalā-niyamena</s>), He made various incarnations in the worlds; but <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself manifested as the supreme Person. I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the original Person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). ||39|| // BrS 5.48 //

children.text:
sa eva kadācit prapañce nijāṃśena svayam avataratīty āha rāmādīnti yaḥ
kṛṣṇākhyaḥ paramaḥ pumān kalā-niyamena tatra tatra niyatānām eva
śaktīnāṃ prakāśena rāmādi-mūrtiṣu tiṣṭhan tat-tan-mūrtīḥ prakāśayan
nānāvatāram akarot | ya eva svayaṃ samabhavad avatatāra | taṃ līlā-viśeṣeṇa
govindaṃ santam ahaṃ bhajāmīty arthaḥ | tad uktaṃ śrī-daśame devaiḥ --
children.translated_text: That very same one sometimes descends into the material world by His own portion — this he states with '<s>rāmādi</s>' (beginning with <s>Rāma</s>). He who is the supreme Person named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by a regulated distribution of powers — manifesting only the specific powers appropriate to each — abiding in the forms of <s>Rāma</s> and others, manifesting those various forms, He made various incarnations. He who Himself descended — that [<s>Govinda</s>], who through His specific pastimes is <s>Govinda</s>, I worship — this is the meaning. As stated in the Śrī Tenth [Canto] by the gods:

children.text:
matsyāśva-kacchapa-nṛsiṃha-varāha-haṃsa-
rājanya-vipra-vibudheṣu kṛtāvatāraḥ |
tvaṃ pāsi nas tri-bhuvanaṃ ca yathādhuneśa
bhāraṃ bhuvo hara yadūttama vandanaṃ te || [BhP 10.2.40] iti || 39 ||
children.translated_text: 'Having incarnated as fish, horse[-headed], tortoise, man-lion, boar, swan, king, sage, and god — You protect us and the three worlds, just as now, O Lord. Remove the burden of the earth, O best of the <s>Yadus</s>! Salutations to You!' [BhP 10.2.40] ||39||

children.text:
yasya prabhā prabhavato jagad-aṇḍa-koṭi-
koṭiṣv aśeṣa-vasudhādi vibhūti-bhinnam |
tad brahma niṣkalam anantam aśeṣa-bhūtaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||40|| // BrS_5.49 //
children.translated_text: The radiance of Him from whom millions upon millions of universe-eggs, each with its complete variety of earths and other opulences, [emanate] — that is the undivided, infinite, all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>. I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the original Person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). ||40|| // BrS 5.49 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ tasya sarvāvatāritvena pūrṇatvam uktvā svarūpeṇāpy āha yasyeti |
dvayor eka-rūpatve'pi viśiṣṭatayāvirbhāvāt śrī-govindasya dharmi-rūpatvam
aviśiṣṭatayāvirbhāvāt brahmaṇo dharma-rūpatvaṃ tataḥ pūrvasya
maṇḍala-snānīyatvam iti bhāvaḥ | tatra viṣṇu-purāṇam api sampravadate
śubhāśrayaḥ sa-cittasya sarvagasya tathātmanaḥ [ViP 6.7.76] iti | vyākhyātaṃ
ca śrīdhara-svāmibhiḥ - sarvagasyātmanaḥ ppara-brahmaṇo apy āśrayaḥ
pratiṣṭhā | tad uktaṃ bhagavatā brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham [Gītā 14.27] iti |
children.translated_text: 'As stated by the Lord: "I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>" [<s>Gītā</s> 14.27].'

Thus, having stated His completeness as the source of all incarnations, he now speaks of His essential nature with 'yasya' (whose). Although the two [<s>Govinda</s> and <s>Brahman</s>] are of one nature, since <s>Śrī Govinda</s> manifests with distinction, He has the nature of the qualified substance (<s>dharmin</s>); since <s>Brahman</s> manifests without distinction, it has the nature of the attribute (<s>dharma</s>). Therefore, the former has the primacy of the orb over its effulgence — this is the purport. Here the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> also concurs: 'The auspicious abode of the conscious, all-pervading Self' [ViP 6.7.76]. And it is explained by <s>Śrīdhara Svāmī</s>: 'The abode, the foundation, even of the all-pervading Self, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: ataivaikādaśe sva-vibhūti-gaṇanāyāṃ tad api svayaṃ gaṇitam --
children.translated_text: For this very reason, in the Eleventh [Canto], in the enumeration of His own opulences, He Himself counted that [<s>Brahman</s>] too:

children.text: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśa āpo jyotir ahaṃ mahān |
vikāraḥ puruṣo 'vyaktaṃ rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaḥ param || [BhP 11.16.37] iti |
children.translated_text: the transformations, <s>Puruṣa</s>, the unmanifest, <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, <s>tamas</s>, and the Supreme (<s>param</s>).' [BhP 11.16.37]
'Earth, air, ether, water, light, the ego, the <s>mahat</s> (cosmic intelligence),

children.text:
ṭīkā cātra - paraṃ brahma ca ity eṣā | śrī-matsya-devenāpy aṣṭame
tathoktam - madīyaṃ mahimānaṃ ca paraṃ brahmeti śabditam [BhP 8.24.38] |
ataiva śrī-yāmunācārya-caraṇair api -
children.translated_text: And the commentary here: 'And the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — this is the meaning. By Śrī <s>Matsya-deva</s> too, in the Eighth [Canto], it is similarly stated: 'My greatness, which is called the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' [BhP 8.24.38]. For this very reason, by the venerable <s>Yāmunācārya</s> also:

children.text:
yad-aṇḍāntara-gocaraṃ ca yad
daśottarāṇy āvaraṇāni yāni ca |
guṇāḥ pradhānaṃ puruṣaḥ paraṃ padaṃ
parātparaṃ brahma ca te vibhūtayaḥ || [Stotra-ratnam 14] iti |
children.translated_text: the <s>guṇas</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme abode, and the <s>Brahman</s> beyond the beyond — these are Your opulences.' [<s>Stotra-ratnam</s> 14]
'That which is within the universe-egg, and the ten coverings surrounding it,

children.text: ataivāha dhruvaś caturthe -
children.translated_text: For this very reason, <s>Dhruva</s> says in the Fourth [Canto]:

children.text: yā nirvṛtis tanu-bhṛtāṃ tava pāda-padma-
children.translated_text: 'The bliss that comes to embodied beings from meditation on Your lotus feet,

children.text: dhyānād bhavaj-jana-kathā-śravaṇena vā syāt |
children.translated_text: or from hearing the narratives of Your devotees —

children.text: sā brahmaṇi sva-mahimany api nātha mā bhūt
children.translated_text: may that [bliss] not exist in <s>Brahman</s>, in its own glory, O Lord —

children.text: kiṃ tv antakāsi-lulitāt patatāṃ vimānāt || [BhP 4.9.10]
children.translated_text: much less from the celestial chariot falling, struck by the sword of death!' [BhP 4.9.10]

children.text: ataivātmārāmāṇām api tad guṇenākarṣaḥ śrūyate |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, even the attraction of the self-delighting ones (<s>ātmārāmas</s>) by His qualities is heard [in scripture]:

children.text: ātmārāmāś ca munayo nirgranthā apy urukrame |
kurvanty ahaitukīṃ bhaktim itthambhūto guṇo hariḥ || [BhP 1.7.11] iti |
children.translated_text: such is the quality of <s>Hari</s>!' [BhP 1.7.11]
'Even the self-delighting sages, free from all bonds, perform causeless devotion to <s>Urukrama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) —

children.text: atra viśeṣa-jijñāsā cet śrī-bhāgavata-sandarbho dṛśyatām ity alam
ativistareṇa || 40 ||
children.translated_text: of excessive elaboration. ||40||
If one desires specific details here, one should consult the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata-sandarbha</s>. Enough

children.text:
māyā hi yasya jagad-aṇḍa-śatāni sūte
traiguṇya-tad-viṣaya-veda-vitāyamānā |
sattvāvalambi-para-sattvaṃ viśuddha-sattvam-
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||41|| // BrS_5.50 //
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, who gives birth to hundreds of universe-eggs, expanding into the threefold <s>guṇas</s> and the <s>Vedas</s> that deal with them — [He whose <s>sattva</s> is] supported by <s>sattva</s>, yet is beyond <s>sattva</s>, the pure <s>sattva</s> (<s>viśuddha-sattva</s>).
