I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the original Person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). ||41|| // BrS 5.50 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ tasya svarūpa-gata-māhātmyaṃ darśayitvā jagad-gata-māhātmyaṃ
darśayati dvābhyām | tatra bahiraṅga-śakti-māyācintya-kārya-gatam āha
māyā hīti | māyayā hi tasya sparśo nāstīty āha sattveti | sattvasya
rajas-tamo-miśrasyāśrayi yat paraṃ tad amiśraṃ śuddhaṃ sattvaṃ tasmād api
viśuddhaṃ cic-chakti-vṛtti-rūpaṃ sattvaṃ yasya tam | tathoktaṃ
śrī-viṣṇu-purāṇe -
children.translated_text: Thus, having shown His greatness pertaining to His essential nature, he shows His greatness pertaining to the world in two [verses]. Of these, the greatness pertaining to the inconceivable works of the external potency (<s>Māyā</s>) is stated with '<s>māyā</s> hi.' And that He has no contact with <s>Māyā</s>, he states with '<s>sattva</s>.' That which is <s>sattva</s> mixed with <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — its support is the transcendent, unmixed, pure <s>sattva</s>; and even beyond that is the thoroughly pure <s>sattva</s>, which is of the nature of the function of the spiritual potency (<s>cit-śakti</s>) — [He] whose [nature] is that. As stated in the Śrī <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: sattvādayo na santīśe yatra ca prākṛtā guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s> and the other material <s>guṇas</s> do not exist in the Lord;

children.text: sa śuddhaḥ sarva-śuddhebhyaḥ pumān ādyaḥ prasīdatu ||
children.translated_text: may that pure one, purer than all pure things, the original Person, be pleased!'

children.text: hlādinī sandhinī saṃvit tvayy ekā guṇa-saṃśraye |
hlāda-tāpa-karī miśrā tvayi no guṇa-varjite || [ViP 1.9.44-45] iti |
children.translated_text: the mixed [power], causing pleasure and pain — [that is] not in You, who are free from [material] qualities.' [ViP 1.9.44-45]
'<s>Hlādinī</s> (bliss), <s>sandhinī</s> (existence), and <s>saṃvit</s> (knowledge) — in You, the abode of qualities, these are one [power];

children.text: viśeṣataḥ śrī-bhāgavata-sandarbhe tad idam api vivṛtam asti || 41 ||
children.translated_text: In the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata-sandarbha</s>, this too is elaborated in detail. ||41||

children.text:
ānanda-cinmaya-rasātmatayā manaḥsu
yaḥ prāṇināṃ pratiphalan smaratām upetya |
līlāyitena bhuvanāni jayaty ajasram-
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||42|| // BrS_5.51 //
children.translated_text: He who, through His nature as the essence of bliss and consciousness (<s>ānanda-cinmaya-rasa</s>), reflected in the minds of living beings, approaching those who remember Him, eternally conquers all the worlds through His playfulness (<s>līlā</s>) — I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the original Person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). ||42|| // BrS 5.51 //

children.text:
atha tan-maya-mohanatvam āha ānandeti | ānanda-cin-mayasya ujjvalākhyaḥ
prema-rasaḥ | tad-ātmatayā tad-āliṅgitatayā prāṇināṃ manaḥsu
pratiphalan-sarva-mohana-svāṃśa-cchurita-paramāṇu-pratibimbatayākiñcid
udayann api smaratām upetyety ādi yojyam | yad uktaṃ rāsa-pañcādhyāyyāṃ
- sākṣān manmatha-manmathaḥ [BhP 10.32.2] iti, cakṣuṣaś cakṣuḥ [KenaU
1.2] itivat | tad evaṃ tat-kāraṇatve'pi smarāveśasya duṣṭatvaṃ
jagad-āveśavat ||42||
children.translated_text: is like the possession by the world [of it]. ||42||

Now he states His enchanting power that pervades everything — with 'ānanda.' The <s>prema-rasa</s> (love-relish), called <s>ujjvala</s> (brilliant), which is of the nature of bliss and consciousness (<s>ānanda-cinmaya</s>) — by being embraced by that nature, reflected in the minds of living beings — even slightly arising as a reflection of the all-enchanting atomic particles of His own portion — approaching those who remember [Him] — this and what follows should be connected. As stated in the five chapters on the <s>rāsa</s> [dance]: 'He is directly the enchanter of <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid) himself' [BhP 10.32.2] — like 'the eye of the eye' [<s>Kena Upaniṣad</s> 1.2]. Thus, even though He is the cause of the amorous impulse, its contamination [in the world]

children.text:
goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya
devi maheśa-hari-dhāmasu teṣu teṣu |
te te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||43|| // BrS_5.52 //
children.translated_text: In the abode called <s>Goloka</s>, His own domain, and below that, in the realms of <s>Devī</s>, <s>Maheśa</s>, and <s>Hari</s>, in each and every one of those — the respective powers were established by Him. I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the original Person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). ||43|| // BrS 5.52 //

children.text:
tad idaṃ prapañca-gataṃ māhātmyam uktvā nija-dhāma-gata-māhātmyam
āha goloketi | devī-maheśety-ādi-gaṇanaṃ vyutkrameṇa jñeyam |
devy-ādīnāṃ yathottara-mūrdhārdha-prabhavatvāt tal-lokānām
ūrdhvordhva-bhāvitvam iti | golokasya sarvordhva-gāmitvaṃ vyāpakatvaṃ ca
vyavasthāpitam asti | bhuvi prakāśamānasya vṛndāvanasya tu tenābhedaḥ
pūrvatra darśitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having stated this glory pertaining to the material world, he now states the glory pertaining to His own abode with the word '<s>Goloka</s>.' The enumeration beginning with '<s>Devī</s>, <s>Maheśa</s>...' should be understood in reverse order. Since <s>Devī</s> and the others successively emanate from the upper half of the head, their respective worlds are progressively higher. <s>Goloka</s>'s position as the highest of all and its all-pervading nature have been established. And the non-difference of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> manifesting on earth with that [<s>Goloka</s>] has been shown earlier.

children.text: sa tu lokas tvayā kṛṣṇa sīdamānaḥ kṛtātmanā |
dhṛto dhṛtimatā vīra nighantopdadravān gavām || [HV 62.33] iti |
children.translated_text: O steadfast hero, destroying the calamities of the cows.' [HV 62.33]
'That world, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, when it was sinking, was upheld by you, the self-controlled one,

children.text:
ity anenābhedenaiva hi goloka eva nivasatīty eva-kāraḥ saṃghaṭate | yato
bhuvi prakāśamāne'smin vṛndāvane'pi tasya nitya-vihāritvaṃ śrūyate | yathā
ādi-vārāhe -
children.translated_text: Thus, by this very non-difference, the emphatic particle 'eva' (only) is consistent [with the statement that] he dwells in <s>Goloka</s> alone. Since even in this <s>Vṛndāvana</s> manifesting on earth, his eternal sporting is heard of. As in the <s>Ādi-Vārāha</s> [Purāṇa]:

children.text: vṛndāvanaṃ dvādaśamaṃ vṛndayā parirakṣitam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the twelfth [forest], protected by <s>Vṛndā</s>,

children.text: hariṇādhiṣṭhitaṃ tac ca brahma-rudrādi-sevitam ||
children.translated_text: presided over by <s>Hari</s>, and served by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others.'

children.text: tatra ca viśeṣataḥ -
children.translated_text: And there, specifically:

children.text: kṛṣṇa-krīḍā-setu-bandhaṃ mahāpātaka-nāśanam |
children.translated_text: 'The dam of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s play, the destroyer of great sins;

children.text: valabhīṃ tatra krīḍārthaṃ kṛtvā devo gadādharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made a pavilion there for the purpose of play, the Lord <s>Gadādhara</s>,

children.text:
gopakaiḥ sahitas tatra kṣaṇam ekaṃ dine dine |
tatraiva ramaṇārthaṃ hi nitya-kālaṃ sa gacchati || iti |
children.translated_text: together with the cowherds, [spends] a single moment there each day. Indeed, for the purpose of sporting, he goes there eternally.'

children.text: ataiva gautamīye śrī-nārada uvāca --
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Gautamīya</s> [Tantra], <s>Śrī Nārada</s> said:

children.text: kim idaṃ dvādaśābhikhyaṃ vṛndāraṇyaṃ viśāmpate |
children.translated_text: 'What is this [forest] called the twelfth, the <s>Vṛndā</s> forest, O ruler of the people?

children.text: śrotum icchāmi bhagavan yadi yogo'smi me vada ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear, O Blessed One; if I am worthy, tell me.'

children.text: śrī-kṛṣṇa uvāca --
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> said:

children.text: idaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ mama dhāmaiva kevalam |
children.translated_text: 'This beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is my abode alone.

children.text: atra ye paśavaḥ pakṣi-vṛkṣā kīṭā narāmarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, whatever animals, birds, trees, insects, humans, and gods

children.text: ye vasanti mamādhiṣṇye mṛtā yānti mamālayam ||
children.translated_text: dwell in my realm, upon dying, go to my abode.

children.text: atra yā gopa-kanyāś ca nivasanti mamālaye |
children.translated_text: Here, the cowherd maidens who dwell in my realm

children.text: yoginyas tā mayā nityaṃ mama sevā-parāyaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are <s>yoginīs</s>, eternal with me, devoted to my service.

children.text: pañca-yojanam evāsti vanaṃ me deha-rūpakam |
children.translated_text: The forest, extending five <s>yojanas</s>, is the form of my body;

children.text: kālindīyaṃ suṣumnākhyā paramāmṛta-vāhinī ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) is called <s>suṣumnā</s>, the carrier of supreme nectar.

children.text: atra devāś ca bhūtāni vartante sūkṣma-rūpataḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, gods and beings exist in subtle form;

children.text: sarva-deva-mayaś cāhaṃ na tyajāmi vanaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: and I, who embody all gods, never abandon this forest.

children.text: āvirbhāvas tirobhāvo bhaven me 'tra yuge yuge |
children.translated_text: My appearance and disappearance occur here age after age.

children.text: tejo-mayam idaṃ ramyam adṛśyaṃ carma-cakṣuṣā || iti
children.translated_text: This beautiful [abode] is made of light, invisible to the physical eye.'

children.text:
etad-rūpam evāśritya vārāhādau te nitya-kadambādayo varṇitāḥ | tasmād
adṛśyamānasyaiva vṛndāvanasya asmad-adṛśya tādṛśa-prakāśa-viśeṣa eva
goloka iti labdham | yadā cāsmad-dṛśyamāne prakāśe sa-parikaraḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa
āvirbhavati tadaiva tasyāvatāra ucyate | tadaiva ca rasa-viśeṣa-poṣāya
saṃyoga-virahaḥ, punaḥ saṃyogādimaya-vicitra-līlā-pāradāryādi-vyavahāraś
ca gamyate | yadā tu yathātra yathā vānyatra
tantra-yāmala-saṃhitā-pañcarātrādiṣu tathā dig-darśanena viśeṣā jñeyāḥ |
tathā ca daśame jayati jananivāso devakī janma-vādaḥ [BhP 10.90.48] ity ādi |
tathā ca pādme nirvāṇa-khaṇḍe śrī-bhagavad-vyāsa-vākye -
children.translated_text: Relying on this very form, the eternal <s>kadamba</s> trees and others are described in the <s>Vārāha</s> [Purāṇa] etc. Therefore, it is established that <s>Goloka</s> is nothing but that special manifestation of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> which, though invisible to us, is [always present]. When <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with his associates, appears in the manifestation visible to us, then alone is his descent (<s>avatāra</s>) spoken of. And it is then that, for the nourishment of special <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments), union and separation occur, and diverse pastimes consisting of reunion, and activities like the breaking of doors, etc., are understood. The specifics should be known by way of indication, as here and elsewhere in the <s>Tantras</s>, <s>Yāmalas</s>, <s>Saṃhitās</s>, <s>Pañcarātras</s>, etc. Similarly in the Tenth [Canto]: 'Glory to Him who is the abode of mothers, called the birth of <s>Devakī</s>' [BhP 10.90.48] and so on. And similarly in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Nirvāṇa-khaṇḍa</s>, in the words of <s>Śrī Bhagavān Vyāsa</s>:

children.text: paśya tvaṃ darśayiṣyāmi svarūpaṃ veda-gopitam |
children.translated_text: 'Behold, I shall show you the essential form concealed by the <s>Vedas</s>.'

children.text: tato'paśyam ahaṃ bhūpa bālaṃ kālāmbuda-prabham ||
children.translated_text: 'Then I beheld, O King, a boy with the radiance of a dark rain cloud,

children.text: gopa-kanyāvṛtaṃ gopaṃ hasantaṃ gopa-bālakaiḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: a cowherd surrounded by cowherd maidens, laughing with cowherd boys.'

children.text:
anena atra yā gopa-kanyāś ceti pūrvoktena ca
anālabdha-strī-dharma-vayaskatādi-bodhakena kanyā-padena tāsām
anyādṛśatvaṃ nirākriyate | tathā ca gautamīye caturthādhyāye - atha
vṛndāvanaṃ dhyāyet ity ārabhya tad-dhyānaṃ -
children.translated_text: By this, and by the word 'maidens' (<s>kanyā</s>) in the earlier statement 'the cowherd maidens who are here,' which indicates those who have not attained the age of womanly duties etc., the notion that they are of an ordinary nature is refuted. And similarly in the fourth chapter of the <s>Gautamīya</s> [Tantra], beginning with 'Now one should meditate on <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,' the meditation on it [is described]:

children.text: svargād iva paribhraṣṭa kanyakā-śata-maṇḍitam |
children.translated_text: 'Adorned with hundreds of maidens as if fallen from heaven,

children.text: gopa-vatsa-gaṇākīrṇaṃ vṛkṣa-ṣaṇḍaiś ca maṇḍitam ||
children.translated_text: filled with groups of cowherd calves and adorned with groves of trees,

children.text:
gopa-kanyā-sahasrais tu padma-patrāyatekṣaṇaiḥ |
arcitaṃ bhāva-kusumais trailokyaika-guruṃ param || ity ādi |
children.translated_text: worshipped with flowers of devotion by thousands of cowherd maidens with eyes wide as lotus petals — the supreme, the sole guru of the three worlds.' And so on.

children.text: tad-darśanādikārī ca darśitas tatraiva sad-ācāra-prasaṅge -
children.translated_text: And one who is qualified for that vision is also shown there, in the context of righteous conduct:

children.text:
ahar-niśaṃ japen mantraṃ mantrī niyata-mānasaḥ |
sa paśyati na sandeho gopa-veśa-dharaṃ harim || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Day and night, the practitioner with controlled mind should chant the <s>mantra</s>; he will see <s>Hari</s> in the garb of a cowherd — there is no doubt.'

children.text:
ataiva tāpanyāṃ brahma-vākyam - tad u hovāca brahmaṇo'sāv anavarataṃ me
dhyātaḥ stutaḥ | parārdhānte so'budhyata | gopaveśo me puruṣaḥ purastād
āvirbabhūva || iti tasmāt kṣīroda-śāyy ādy-avatāratayā tasya yat kathanaṃ tat
tu tad-aṃśānāṃ tatra praveśāpekṣayā alam ativistareṇa śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe
darśita-careṇa || 43 ||
children.translated_text: as demonstrated therein. ||43||

Therefore, the statement of <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Tāpanīya</s> [Upaniṣad]: 'That one whom I have ceaselessly meditated upon and praised — after half of <s>Brahmā</s>'s lifespan (<s>parārdha</s>), he was realized. The <s>Puruṣa</s> in the garb of a cowherd appeared before me.' Therefore, the description of him as an <s>avatāra</s> of <s>Kṣīrodakaśāyī</s> and others is in reference to the entry of his portions therein. Enough of excessive elaboration; [the details are] in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s>,

children.text:
sṛṣṭi-sthiti-pralaya-sādhana-śaktir ekā
chāyeva yasya bhuvanāni bibharti durgā |
icchānurūpam api yasya ca ceṣṭate sā
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||44|| // BrS_5.53 //
children.translated_text: I worship <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord, whose shadow-like energy <s>Durgā</s>, the single power that accomplishes creation, maintenance, and dissolution, sustains the worlds and acts in accordance with His will. ||44||

children.text:
atha prastutam anusarāmaḥ | pūrvaṃ devī-maheśa-hari-dhāmnām
uparicara-dhāmatvaṃ tasya caritaṃ, samprati tu tat-tad-āśrayatvād eva yogyam
iti darśayati sṛṣṭīti pañcabhiḥ | yathoktaṃ śrutibhiḥ | tvam akaraṇaḥ svarāḍ
akhila-kāraka-śakti-dharas tava balim udvahanti samadantyajayā nimiṣā iti ||
children.translated_text: Now we follow the main topic. Previously, the fact that [<s>Goloka</s>] is the abode that moves above the abodes of <s>Devī</s>, <s>Maheśa</s>, and <s>Hari</s> has been narrated. Now, he shows that this is fitting precisely because [<s>Govinda</s>] is the support of each of those, with five [verses beginning] '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' (creation). As stated by the <s>Śrutis</s>: 'You are without instruments, self-ruling, the bearer of all causal power; [all beings] offer tribute to you, consumed by the unconquerable [<s>Māyā</s>] in the blink of an eye.'

children.text:
kṣīraṃ yathā dadhi vikāra-viśeṣa-yogāt
sañjāyate na hi tataḥ pṛthag asti hetoḥ |
yaḥ śambhutām api tathā samupaiti kāryād
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||45|| // BrS_5.54 //
children.translated_text: I worship <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord, from whom <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) arises for the purpose of creation, just as yogurt is produced from milk by a special transformation, yet is not separate from its cause. ||45||

children.text:
atha krama-prāptaṃ maheśaṃ nirūpayati kṣīram iti |
kārya-kāraṇa-bhāva-mātrāṃśe dṛṣṭānto'yaṃ dārṣṭāntika-kāraṇasya
nirvikāratvāt cintāmaṇy-ādivat acintya-śaktyaiva tad-ādi-kāryatayāpi
sthitatvāt | śrutiś ca eko nārāyaṇa evāgra āsīt, na brahmā na ca śaṅkaraḥ,
sa munir bhūtvā samacintayat | tata evaite vyajāyanta viśvo hiraṇyagarbho'gnir
varuṇa-rudrendrāḥ iti tathā sa brahmaṇā sṛjati rudreṇa nāśayati |
so'nutpatti-laya eva hariḥ | kāraṇa-rūpaḥ paraḥ paramānandaḥ | iti |
śambhor api kāryatvaṃ guṇa-saṃvalanāt | yathoktaṃ śrī-daśame -
children.translated_text: Now he describes <s>Maheśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose turn has come, with 'milk.' This analogy applies only to the aspect of the cause-effect relationship, since the analogized cause is unchanging — like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), existing as the cause of effects by inconceivable power alone. And the <s>śruti</s>: 'Only <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> existed in the beginning — not <s>Brahmā</s>, not <s>Śaṅkara</s>; he, becoming a sage, reflected; from that alone these were born: <s>Viśva</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>.' Similarly: 'He creates through <s>Brahmā</s>, destroys through <s>Rudra</s>. He, <s>Hari</s>, is indeed without origin or dissolution — the causal form, the supreme, the supreme bliss.' <s>Śambhu</s>'s status as an effect is due to his association with the <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities). As stated in the Tenth [Canto]:

children.text: harir hi nirguṇaḥ sākṣāt puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ
sa sarva-dṛg upadraṣṭā taṃ bhajan nirguṇo bhavet || [BhP 10.88.5] iti |
children.translated_text: he is the all-seeing witness. By worshipping him, one becomes free from the <s>guṇas</s>.' [BhP 10.88.5]
'<s>Hari</s> is indeed directly without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), the <s>Puruṣa</s> beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>;

children.text:
etad evoktaṃ - vikāra-viśeṣa-yogād iti | kutracid abhedoktir yā dṛśyate tām
api samādadhāti tato hetoḥ pṛthaktvaṃ nāstīti | yathoktam ṛg-veda-śirasi -
atha nityo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ | brahmā nārāyaṇaḥ | śivaś ca nārāyaṇaḥ |
śakraś ca nārāyaṇaḥ | dvādaśādityāś ca nārāyaṇaḥ | vāsavo nārāyaṇaḥ |
aśvinī nārāyaṇaḥ | sarve ṛṣayo nārāyaṇaḥ | kālaś ca nārāyaṇaḥ | diśaś ca
nārāyaṇaḥ | adhaś ca nārāyaṇaḥ | ūrdhvaś ca nārāyaṇaḥ | antar bahiś ca
nārāyaṇaḥ | nārāyaṇa evedaṃ sarvaṃ jātaṃ jagatyāṃ jagad ity ādi | dvitīye
brahmaṇā tv evam uktaṃ -
children.translated_text: This alone is stated by 'through the special combination of transformation.' And the statements of non-difference seen somewhere are also reconciled by 'there is no separateness from that cause.' As stated in the <s>Ṛg-veda-śiras</s> (<s>Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad</s>): 'The eternal God is one, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. <s>Brahmā</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. <s>Śiva</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. <s>Śakra</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. The twelve <s>Ādityas</s> are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. The <s>Vasus</s> are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. The <s>Aśvins</s> are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. All the <s>Ṛṣis</s> are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Time is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. The directions are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Below is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Above is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. Within and without is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is all this that has been born in the world.' And so on. In the Second [Canto], it is said by <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text:
sṛjāmi tan-niyukto 'haṃ haro harati tad-vaśaḥ |
viśvaṃ puruṣa-rūpeṇa paripāti tri-śakti-dhṛk || [BhP 2.6.33] iti ||45||
children.translated_text: 'Appointed by Him, I create; <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), subject to Him, destroys; the holder of three powers [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] protects the universe in the form of the <s>Puruṣa</s>.' [BhP 2.6.33] ||45||

children.text:
dīpārcir eva hi daśāntaram abhyupetya
dīpāyate vivṛta-hetu-samāna-dharmā |
yas tādṛg eva hi ca viṣṇutayā vibhāti
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||46|| // BrS_5.55 //
children.translated_text: I worship <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord, who indeed manifests as <s>Viṣṇu</s> in just such a way — as the flame of a lamp, having reached another lamp, illuminates with qualities equal to its manifest source. ||46||

children.text:
atha krama-prāptaṃ hari-svarūpam ekaṃ nirūpayan
guṇāvatāra-maheśa-prasaṅgād guṇāvatāraṃ viṣṇuṃ nirūpayati dīpārcir iti |
tādṛktve hetuḥ | vivṛta-heta-samāna-dharmeti | yadyaḸ śrī-govindāṃśāṃśaḥ
kāraṇārṇava-śāyī tasya garbhodaka-śāyī, tasya cāvatāro'yaṃ viṣṇur iti
labhyate tathāpi mahā-dīpāt
krama-paramparayātisūkṣma-nirmala-dīpasyoditasya | jyoti-rūpatvāṃśe yathā
tena saha sāmyam | tathā govindena viṣṇur gamyate | śambhos tu
tamo'dhiṣṭhānatvāt kajjvala-maya-sūkṣma-dīpa-śikhā-sthānīyasya na tathā
sāmyam iti bodhanāya tad ittham ucyate | mahā-viṣṇor api kalā-viśeṣatvena
darśayiṣyamāṇatvāt ||46||
children.translated_text: as will be shown [later]. ||46||

Now, establishing the one true nature of <s>Hari</s> whose turn has come, in connection with <s>Maheśa</s> who is a <s>guṇāvatāra</s> (incarnation of a quality), he describes <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is also a <s>guṇāvatāra</s>, with 'the flame of a lamp.' The reason for the similarity: 'having qualities equal to its manifest source.' Although it is understood that <s>Kāraṇārṇavaśāyī</s> (Viṣṇu lying on the Causal Ocean) is a portion of a portion of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, <s>Garbhodakaśāyī</s> is a portion of Him, and this <s>Viṣṇu</s> is an <s>avatāra</s> of that one — nevertheless, of a lamp that has arisen in gradual succession from the great lamp, being an exceedingly subtle and pure lamp, insofar as the aspect of being of the nature of light, there is equality with the original. Similarly, <s>Viṣṇu</s> is understood through <s>Govinda</s>. But <s>Śambhu</s>, because he presides over darkness (<s>tamas</s>), being in the position of a subtle lamp-flame made of soot, does not have such equality. To convey this understanding, it is thus stated. Even regarding <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>, by way of being a specific <s>kalā</s> (portion),

children.text:
yaḥ kāraṇārṇava-jale bhajati sma yoga-
nidrām ananta-jagad-aṇḍa-sa-roma-kūpaḥ |
ādhāra-śaktim avalambya parāṃ sva-mūrtiṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||47|| // BrS_5.56 //
children.translated_text: He who reclines on the waters of the Causal Ocean in <s>yoga-nidrā</s> (mystic slumber), in whose hair-pores reside innumerable cosmic eggs (<s>jagad-aṇḍas</s>), supporting His own supreme form through the sustaining energy (<s>ādhāra-śakti</s>)—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||47|| // BrS 5.56 //

children.text:
atha kāraṇārṇava-śāyinaṃ nirūpayati | ananta-jagad-aṇḍaiḥ saha roma-kūpā
yasya saḥ | saha-śabdasya pūrva-nipātābhāvaḥ, ārṣaḥ | ādhāra-śakti-mayīṃ
parāṃ sva-mūrtiṃ, śeṣākhyām ||47||
children.translated_text: is an archaic usage. 'His own supreme form, consisting of the sustaining energy'—called <s>Śeṣa</s>. ||47||
Now He describes the one who reclines on the Causal Ocean. 'Whose hair-pores contain innumerable cosmic eggs'—that is He. The non-prior placement of the word 'saha' (with)

children.text:
yasyaika-niśvasita-kālam athāvalambya
jīvanti loma-vilajā jagad-aṇḍa-nāthāḥ |
viṣṇur mahān sa iha yasya kalā-viśeṣo
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||48|| // BrS_5.57 //
children.translated_text: The lords of the cosmic eggs survive only for the duration of one exhalation of His, relying upon Him; that <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s> is but a particular <s>kalā</s> (portion) of Him—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||48|| // BrS 5.57 //

children.text:
tatra sarva-brahmāṇḍa-pālako yas tavāvatāratayā
mahā-brahmādi-sahacaratvena tad-atibhinnatvena ca mahā-viṣṇur darśitaḥ |
atra ca tam apy evaṃ tat-salakṣaṇatayā varṇayati | tat-taj-jagad-aṇḍa-nāthā
viṣṇv-ādayaḥ jīvanti tat-tad-adhikāritayā jagati prakaṭaṃ tiṣṭhanti ||48||
children.translated_text: namely <s>Viṣṇu</s> and others, 'survive'—that is, they remain manifestly present in the world through their respective authority. ||48||

There, He who protects all the cosmic eggs, who was shown as <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>—distinct from the <s>Mahā-Brahmā</s> and others who accompany Him as His avatāras and yet supremely distinct from them—here He describes that one too as having the same characteristics. 'The lords of the respective cosmic eggs,'

children.text:
bhāsvān yathāśma-śakaleṣu nijeṣu tejaḥ
svīyam kiyat prakaṭayaty api tadvad atra |
brahmā ya eṣa jagad-aṇḍa-vidhāna-kartā
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||49|| // BrS_5.58 //
children.translated_text: Just as the sun reveals its own light to a certain degree in its own sun-stones, so too <s>Brahmā</s>, who is the creator of the arrangement of this cosmic egg—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||49|| // BrS 5.58 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ devy-ādīnāṃ tad-āśrayakatvaṃ darśayitvā prasaṅga-saṅgatyā
brahmaṇaś ca darśayan atīva-bhinnatayā jīvatvam eva spaṣṭayati bhāsvān
iti | bhāsvān sūryo, yathā nijeṣu nitya-svīyatvena vikhyāteṣu aśma-sakaleṣu
sūrya-kāntākhyeṣu svīyaṃ kiñcit tejaḥ prakaṭayati | api-śabdāt tena
tad-upādhikāṃśena dāhādi-kāryaṃ svayam eva karoti | tathā ya eva
jīva-viśeṣa-kiñcit-tejaḥ prakaṭayati | tena tad-upādhikāṃśena svayam eva
brahmā san jagad-aṇḍe brahmāṇḍe vidhāna-kartā vyaṣṭi-sṛṣṭi-kartā
bhavatīty arthaḥ | yad vā mahā-brahmaivāyaṃ varṇyate | tad-upalakṣito
mahā-śivaś ca jñeyaḥ | tataś ca jagad-aṇḍānāṃ vidhāna-kartṛtvaṃ ca yuktam
eva | yadyapi durgākhyā māyā kāraṇārṇava-śāyina eva karmakarī | yadyapi
ca brahma-viṣṇv-ādyā garbhodaka-śāyina evāvatārās tathāpi tasya
sarvāśrayatayā te'pi tad-āśritatayā gaṇitāḥ | evam uttaratrāpi ||49||
children.translated_text: Thus, having shown the dependence of <s>Devī</s> and others upon Him, and in the course of showing that of <s>Brahmā</s> as well, He makes clear that [Brahmā's] nature as a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) is [maintained] through supreme distinction—with 'the sun' etc. 'The sun': just as the sun reveals some of its own light in its own sun-stones, which are well-known as eternally belonging to it. By the word 'api' (also/even), through the instrumental portion conditioned by that, it itself performs actions such as burning. Similarly, He reveals a certain amount of light in a particular <s>jīva</s>; through the instrumental portion conditioned by that, he himself, being <s>Brahmā</s>, becomes the creator of the arrangement in the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), that is, the creator of the individual creation—this is the meaning. Or else, it is <s>Mahā-Brahmā</s> himself who is being described. <s>Mahā-Śiva</s>, who is implied by him, should also be understood. Thus, his creatorship of the cosmic eggs is indeed fitting. Although the <s>Māyā</s> called <s>Durgā</s> is the agent of the one who reclines on the Causal Ocean, and although <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and others are avatāras of the one who reclines on the waters within the cosmic egg, nevertheless, because of His being the ultimate shelter of all, they too are counted as dependent on Him. The same applies further. ||49||

children.text:
yat-pāda-pallava-yugaṃ vinidhāya kumbha-
dvandve praṇāma-samaye sa gaṇādhirājaḥ |
vighnān vihantum alam asya jagat-trayasya
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||50|| // BrS_5.59 //
children.translated_text: He who, placing the pair of His tender lotus feet upon the pair of pots [the trunks of His own arms at the time of obeisance], the chief of the <s>Gaṇas</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), is fully capable of destroying all obstacles of the three worlds—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||50|| // BrS 5.59 //

children.text:
atha sarve sarva-vighna-nivāraṇārthaṃ prathamaṃ gaṇapatiṃ stuvantīti tasyaiva
stuti-yogyatety āśaṅkayā pratyācaṣṭe yat-pādeti | kaimutyena tad evaṃ
dṛḍhīkṛtaṃ śrī-kapila-devena -- yat-pāda-niḥsṛta-sarit-pravarodakena tīrthena
mūrdhny adhikṛtena śivaḥ śivo 'bhūt [BhP 3.28.22] iti || 50 ||
children.translated_text: Now, with the apprehension that 'everyone first praises <s>Gaṇapati</s> for the removal of all obstacles, and therefore he alone is worthy of praise,' He refutes this with 'whose feet' etc. This is further confirmed by reasoning from the greater—as stated by <s>Śrī Kapila-deva</s>: 'By the supreme sanctifying water of the river flowing from His feet, placed upon his head, <s>Śiva</s> became auspicious' [BhP 3.28.22]. ||50||

children.text:
agnir mahi gaganam ambu marud diśaś ca
kālas tathātma-manasīti jagat-trayāṇi |
yasmād bhavanti vibhavanti viśanti yaṃ ca
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||51|| // BrS_5.60 //
children.translated_text: Fire, earth, sky, water, air, the directions, time, the soul, and mind—the three worlds—from whom they arise, by whom they flourish, and into whom they enter—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||51|| // BrS 5.60 //

children.text: tac ca yuktam ity āha agnir mahīti | sarvaṃ spaṣṭam ||51||
children.translated_text: And that is fitting—thus He says with 'fire, earth' etc. Everything is clear. ||51||

children.text:
yac-cakṣur eṣa savitā sakala-grahāṇāṃ
rājā samasta-sura-mūrtir aśeṣa-tejāḥ |
yasyājñayā bhramati sambhṛta-kāla-cakro
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||52|| // BrS_5.61 //
children.translated_text: The sun, which is His eye, the king of all planets, the embodiment of all the gods, of unlimited radiance, who by His command revolves, carrying the wheel of time—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||52|| // BrS 5.61 //

children.text:
kecit sa-vitāraṃ sarveśvaraṃ vadanti yathāha yac-cakṣur iti ya eva cakṣuḥ
prakāśako yasya saḥ |
children.translated_text: Some declare the sun as the lord of all—thus He says with 'whose eye' etc. 'He who is the eye'—that is, the illuminator of whose [vision], He is that.

children.text:
yad āditya-gataṃ tejo jagad bhāsayate'khilam |
yac candramasi yac cāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam || iti gītābhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That light which, dwelling in the sun, illumines the entire world, which is in the moon and which is in fire—know that light to be Mine'—from the <s>Śrī Gītā</s> [14.12].

children.text: bhīṣāsmād vātaḥ pavate bhīṣodeti sūryaḥ || ity ādi śruteḥ | virāḍ-rūpasyaiva
savitṛ-cakṣuṣṭvāc ca || 52 ||
children.translated_text: has the sun as its eye. ||52||
'From fear of Him the wind blows; from fear of Him the sun rises'—from the <s>śruti</s> [Taittirīya Upaniṣad]. Also because the <s>virāṭ</s> (cosmic) form itself

children.text:
dharmo 'tha pāpa-nicayaḥ śrutayas tapāṃsi
brahmādi-kīṭa-patagāvadhayaś ca jīvāḥ |
yad-datta-mātra-vibhava-prakaṭa-prabhāvā
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||53|| // BrS_5.62 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), and also the accumulation of sin, the sacred scriptures (<s>śrutis</s>), austerities, and all <s>jīvas</s> (living beings) from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the smallest insect and worm—their powers are manifest only through the glory bestowed by Him—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||53|| // BrS 5.62 //

children.text:
kiṃ bahunā, dharma iti | ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate
[Gītā 10.8] iti śrī-gītābhyaḥ || 53 ||
children.translated_text: What more need be said?—with '<s>dharma</s>' etc. 'I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds' [Gītā 10.8]—from the <s>Śrī Gītā</s>. ||53||

children.text:
yas tv indragopam athavendram aho sva-karma-
bandhānurūpa-phala-bhājanam ātanoti |
karmāṇi nirdahati kintu ca bhakti-bhājāṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||54|| // BrS_5.63 //
children.translated_text: He who extends [the fruits] from the <s>indragopa</s> insect to <s>Indra</s> himself—making each the recipient of fruits befitting their own <s>karma</s> (actions)—yet burns away the <s>karma</s> of those devoted to Him—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||54|| // BrS 5.63 //

children.text:
ataiva sarveśvaras tu parjanyavad draṣṭavyaḥ iti nyāyena
karmānurūpa-phala-dātṛtvena sāmye'pi bhakte tu pakṣapāta-viśeṣaṃ karotīty
āha yas tv indreti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, although the supreme Lord should be viewed like rain [which falls equally on all], as the giver of fruits befitting <s>karma</s> in equal measure, yet He shows special partiality toward the devotee—thus He says with 'He who, from the <s>indragopa</s>' etc.

children.text: samo'haṃ sarva-bhūteṣu na me dveṣo'sti na priyaḥ |
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham || [Gītā 9.29] iti |
children.translated_text: but those who worship Me with devotion—they are in Me, and I am also in them.' [Gītā 9.29]
'I am equal to all beings; there is none hateful to Me nor dear;

children.text: ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: 'Those persons who, with undivided mind, worship Me,

children.text: teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yoga-kṣemaṃ vahāmy aham || [Gītā 9.22] iti ca
children.translated_text: who are constantly devoted—I carry their <s>yoga-kṣema</s> (security and sustenance).' [Gītā 9.22]—

children.text: śrī-gītābhyaḥ || 54 ||
children.translated_text: from the <s>Śrī Gītā</s>. ||54||

children.text:
yaṃ krodha-kāma-sahaja-praṇayādi-bhīti-
vātsalya-moha-guru-gaurava-sevya-bhāvaiḥ |
sañcintya tasya sadṛśīṃ tanum āpur ete
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi ||55|| // BrS_5.64 //
children.translated_text: Him whom [beings] contemplate through anger, desire, natural affection, fear, parental love, delusion, reverence for a superior, or the attitude of servitude—they attain a form resembling His—I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Lord. ||55|| // BrS 5.64 //

children.text:
ya eva ca vairbhyo'py anya-durlabha-phalaṃ dadāti kim uta
sva-viṣayaka-kāmādinā niṣkāma-śreṣṭhebhyaḥ | tataḥ ko vānyo bhajanīya
iti bhajāmīty anta-prakaraṇam upasaṃharati yaṃ krodheti | sahaja-praṇayaṃ
sakhyam | vātsalya-pitrādy-ucita-bhāvaḥ | mohaḥ
sarva-vismaraṇa-maya-bhāvaḥ | para-brahmatayāsphūrtiḥ | guru-gauravaṃ
svasmin pitṛtvādi-bhāvanāmayam | sevyo'yaṃ memeti bhāvanā dāsyam ity
arthaḥ | tasya sadṛśīṃ krodhāveśino'prākṛta-mātrāṃśena, tu tat tad bhāvanā
yogya-rūpa-guṇāṃśa-lābha-tāratamyena tulyam ity arthaḥ | adṛṣṭānyatamaṃ
loke śīlaudārya-guṇaiḥ samam iti śrī-vāsudeva-vākyasya |
jagad-vyāpāra-varjam [Vs. 4.4.17] iti brahma-sūtrasya, prayojyamāne mayi tāṃ
śuddhāṃ bhāgavatīṃ tanum iti śrī-nārada-vākyasya ca dṛṣṭyā sarvathā
tat-sadṛśatve virodhāt | vaireṇa yaṃ nṛpatayaḥ ity ādau anurakta-dhiyām
punaḥ kim ity anurakta-dhīṣu suṣṭhv iti | anena
goloka-stha-prapañcāvatīrṇayor ekatvam eva darśitam | tad uktaṃ -
nandādayas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā ity ādi || 55 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s> and the others, having seen that'—etc. ||55||

He who grants even to His enemies fruits difficult for others to obtain—how much more then to those who are the best among the desireless, through desire and other sentiments directed at Him! Therefore, who else is worthy of worship?—thus He concludes the hymn section with 'Him whom, through anger' etc. 'Natural affection' means friendship (<s>sakhya</s>). 'Parental love' is the attitude befitting a parent etc. 'Delusion' is the state of total forgetfulness—that is, non-apprehension of [Him as] the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. 'Reverence for a superior' consists of attitudes such as parenthood toward oneself. 'Attitude of servitude' means the conviction 'He is to be served by me'—this is <s>dāsya</s> (servanthood). 'Resembling His'—for those overwhelmed by anger, through the non-material partial aspect; but equality is in the sense of gradations in obtaining portions of forms and qualities suited to their respective contemplations. From the statement of <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s>: 'one whose character and generosity are unseen elsewhere in the world'; from the <s>Brahma-sūtra</s>: 'except for the governance of the universe' [Vs. 4.4.17]; and from the statement of <s>Śrī Nārada</s>: 'when I am employed, that pure divine form'—in view of these, complete similarity in every respect would be contradictory. In the verse 'through enmity, kings [attained Him],' the phrase 'what then for those with devoted minds' means 'how excellent it is for the devoted.' By this, the oneness of the one dwelling in <s>Goloka</s> and the one descended into the world is shown. As stated—

children.text:
śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ kalpa-taravo
drumā bhūmiś cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-mayi toyam amṛtam |
kathā gānaṃ nāṭyaṃ gamanam api vaṃśī priya-sakhi
cid-ānandaṃ jyotiḥ param api tad āsvādyam api ca || // BrS_5.65 //
children.translated_text: the light is consciousness and bliss, supreme, yet also relishable.

The <s>Śrīs</s> (goddesses of fortune) are His beloveds, He is the supreme lover, the Supreme Person; the trees are wish-fulfilling trees, the ground is made of multitudes of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems, the water is nectar, conversation is song, walking is dance, the flute is the dear companion,

children.text:
sa yatra kṣīrābdhiḥ sravati surabhībhyaś ca su-mahān
nimeṣārdhākhyo vā vrajati na hi yatrāpi samayaḥ |
bhaje śvetadvīpaṃ tam aham iha golokam iti yaṃ
vidantas te santaḥ kṣiti-virala-cārāḥ katipaye ||56|| // BrS_5.66 //
children.translated_text: Where the great ocean of milk flows from the <s>surabhī</s> cows, and where even a half-moment of time does not pass—I worship that <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, which those few saintly persons who rarely walk upon the earth know as <s>Goloka</s>. ||56|| // BrS 5.66 //

children.text:
tad evaṃ nijeṣṭa-devaṃ bhajanīyatvena stutvā tena viśiṣṭaṃ tal lokaṃ tathā
stauti śriyaḥ kāntā iti yugmakena | śriyaḥ śrī-vraja-sundarī rūpās tāsām eva
mantre dhyāne ca sarvatra prasiddheḥ | tāsām anantānām apy eka eva kāntaḥ
iti parama-nārāyaṇādibhyo'pi tasya tat-tal-lokebhyo'pi tadīya-lokasya cāsya
māhātmyaṃ darśitam | kalpa-taravo drumāḥ iti teṣāṃ sarveṣām eva
sarva-pradatvāt tvāt tathaiva prathitam |
children.translated_text: Thus, having praised His own chosen deity as worthy of worship, He now praises that world distinguished by Him with 'the <s>Śrīs</s> are His beloveds' etc. in a pair of verses. 'The <s>Śrīs</s>': those in the form of the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>, since they are well-known everywhere in the mantra and meditation. 'Their one beloved alone'—by this, the greatness of Him over <s>Parama-Nārāyaṇa</s> and others, and of His world over their respective worlds, is shown. 'The trees are wish-fulfilling trees'—this is well-established because all of them grant everything.

children.text:
bhūmir ity ādikaṃ ca tadvad bhūmir api sarva-spṛhāṃ dadāti kim uta
kaustubhādi | toyam apy amṛtam iva svādu kim utāmṛtam ity ādi | vaṃśī
priya-sakhīva sarvataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya sukha-sthiti-śrāvakatvena jñeyam |
cid-ānanda-lakṣaṇaṃ vastv eva jyotiś candra-sūryādi-rūpam |
samānodita-candrārkam iti vṛndāvana-viśeṣaṇaṃ gautamīya-tantra-dvaye | tac
ca nitya-pūrṇa-candratvāt tathā tad eva param api tat tat prakāśyam apīty
arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The verse beginning with "the ground" (<s>bhūmi</s>) is likewise — the ground itself fulfills all desires, how much more then <s>Kaustubha</s> gems and the like. The water too is sweet like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), how much more then actual <s>amṛta</s>, and so on. The flute (<s>vaṃśī</s>), like a dear companion (<s>priya-sakhī</s>), should be understood as that which everywhere broadcasts the blissful state of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. The substance characterized by spiritual bliss (<s>cid-ānanda</s>) alone is the luminance in the form of the moon, sun, and so forth. The phrase "where the moon and sun rise simultaneously" (<s>samānodita-candrārkam</s>) is a qualifier of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> found in two passages of the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>. And because the moon there is eternally full, it is also the supreme illuminator of all that is to be illuminated — this is the meaning.

children.text:
tathā tad eva teṣām āsvādyaṃ bhogyam api ca cic-chaktimayatvād iti bhāvaḥ |
darśayāmāsa lokaṃ svaṃ gopānāṃ tamasaḥ param [BhP 10.28.14] iti
śrī-daśamāt | hayaśīrṣa-pañcarātre ca vaikuṇṭhastha-tattva-nirūpaṇe --
children.translated_text: Likewise, that very substance is also their object of relish and enjoyment, because it is constituted of <s>cit-śakti</s> (spiritual potency) — this is the purport. As stated in the Tenth Canto [of the <s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s>]: "He showed them His own abode, beyond darkness" [<s>BhP</s> 10.28.14]. And in the <s>Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>, in the section determining the nature of the reality situated in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> —

children.text: dravya-tattvaṃ śṛṇu brahman pravakṣyāmi samāsataḥ |
children.translated_text: "Hear, O <s>Brahman</s>, I shall explain to you briefly the nature of substance (<s>dravya-tattva</s>).

children.text: sarva-bhoga-pradā yatra pādapāḥ kalpa-pādapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the trees are wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-pādapa</s>), granting all enjoyments.

children.text: gandha-rūpaṃ svādu-rūpaṃ dravyaṃ puṣpādikaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever substance such as flowers and the like possesses the quality of fragrance and the quality of sweetness,

children.text: heyāṃśānām abhāvāc ca rasa-rūpaṃ bhavec ca tat ||
children.translated_text: due to the absence of objectionable parts, that substance becomes the very essence of <s>rasa</s> (flavor).

children.text:
tvag-bījaṃ caiva heyāṃśaṃ kaṭhināṃśaṃ ca yad bhavet |
sarvaṃ tad bhautikaṃ viddhi nahi bhūtamayaṃ hi tat |
rasavad bhautikaṃ dravyam atra syād rasa-rūpakam || iti |
children.translated_text: Whatever objectionable part there may be — skin, seeds, and hardness — know all that to be material (<s>bhautika</s>); indeed, that [transcendent substance] is not composed of material elements. The material substance that possesses flavor becomes there the very form of <s>rasa</s> (pure essence)." Thus [ends the quotation].

children.text:
surabhībhyaś ca saratīti tvadīya-vaṃśī-dhvany-ādy-āveśād iti bhāvaḥ |
vrajati nahīti tad-āveśena te tad-vāsinaḥ kālam api na jānantīti bhāvaḥ |
kāla-doṣās tatra na santīti vā | na ca kālaḥ vikramaḥ [BhP 2.9.10] iti dvitīyāt |
children.translated_text: Or, the faults of time do not exist there. As stated in the Second Canto [of <s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s>]: "Nor does time hold sway there" [<s>BhP</s> 2.9.10].

children.text:
ataiva śvetaṃ śuddhaṃ dvīpaṃ anyāsaṅga-rahitam | yathā -- sarasi padmaṃ
tiṣṭhati tathā-bhūmyāṃ hi tiṣṭhati [GTU 2.27] iti tāpanībhyaḥ | kṣitīti | tad
uktaṃ yaṃ na vidmo vayaṃ sarve pṛcchanto'pi pitāmaham [HV 62.29] iti || 56 ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, <s>Śveta-dvīpa</s> (the White Island) means the pure realm, free from all extraneous attachment. As stated: "Just as a lotus stands upon a lake, so does it stand upon the earth" [<s>Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad</s> 2.27] — from the <s>Tāpanī</s> [Upaniṣads]. Regarding "the earth" (<s>kṣiti</s>) — as it is said: "We all, even when asking <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Grandfather Brahmā), do not know Him" [<s>Harivaṃśa</s> 62.29]. ‖ 56 ‖

"From the <s>Surabhī</s> cows it flows" — this means due to being absorbed in the sound of Your flute and so on. "It does not move away" — the purport is that due to absorption in that [divine sound], the residents there do not even perceive the passage of time.

children.text:
athovāca mahā-viṣṇur bhagavantaṃ prajāpatim |
brahman mahattva-vijñāne prajā-sarge ca cen matiḥ |
pañca-ślokīm imāṃ vidyāṃ vatsa dattāṃ nibodha me ||57|| // BrS_5.67 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s> spoke to the blessed <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of creatures): "O <s>Brahman</s>, if your mind is set upon understanding [My] greatness and upon the creation of progeny, then, dear child, learn this knowledge of the five verses (<s>pañca-ślokī</s>) that I bestow upon you." ‖ 57 ‖ // <s>BrS</s> 5.67 //

children.text: tad evaṃ tasya stutim uktvā śrī-bhagavat-prasāda-lābham āha atheti | sarvaṃ
spaṣṭam || 57 ||
children.translated_text: is clear. ‖ 57 ‖
Having thus described His praise, [the author] now speaks of the attainment of the grace of the Blessed Lord with the word "then" (<s>atha</s>). Everything

children.text:
prabuddhe jñāna-bhaktibhyām ātmany ānanda-cin-mayī |
udety anuttamā bhaktir bhagavat-prema-lakṣaṇā ||58|| // BrS_5.68 //
children.translated_text: When the self is awakened through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), there arises in the <s>ātman</s> the supreme devotion (<s>anuttamā bhakti</s>), which is of the nature of bliss and consciousness (<s>ānanda-cin-mayī</s>), and which is characterized by love for the Lord (<s>bhagavat-prema</s>). ‖ 58 ‖ // <s>BrS</s> 5.68 //

children.text: tatra prasāda-rūpāṃ pañca-ślokīm āha prabuddha iti |
children.translated_text: Now he states the <s>pañca-ślokī</s> in the form of [the Lord's] grace, beginning with "when awakened" (<s>prabuddhe</s>).

children.text: jñāna-vijñāna-sampanno bhaja māṃ bhakti-bhāvitaḥ || [BhP 11.19.5] ity
children.translated_text: "Endowed with <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>vijñāna</s> (realized knowledge), worship Me with a disposition of devotion" [<s>BhP</s> 11.19.5] —

children.text: ekādaśāt || 58 ||
children.translated_text: from the Eleventh Canto. ‖ 58 ‖

children.text:
pramāṇais tat-sad-ācārais tad-abhyāsair nirantaram |
bodhayan ātmanātmānaṃ bhaktim apy uttamāṃ labhet ||59|| // BrS_5.69 //
children.translated_text: Through scriptural authorities (<s>pramāṇa</s>), through the righteous conduct of the saints (<s>sat-ācāra</s>), and through constant practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of these, enlightening the self by the self, one may attain even the highest devotion (<s>uttamā bhakti</s>). ‖ 59 ‖ // <s>BrS</s> 5.69 //

children.text:
prema-lakṣaṇa-bhakteḥ sādhana-jñāna-rūpayoḥ bhaktyoḥ prāpty-upāyam āha
pramāṇair iti | pramāṇair bhagavac-chāstrais tat-sadācārais tadīyā ye santas
teṣām ācārair anusṭānais tad-abhyāsais teṣām eva paunaḥpuṇyena bāhulyena
ātmanā ātmānaṃ bodhayati svayam eva svaṃ bhagavad-āśritaḥ
śuddha-jīva-rūpam anubhavati, tato'py uttamāṃ śuddhāṃ bhaktiṃ labhata iti |
tathā ca śruti-stave -
children.translated_text: He now states the means of attaining the two forms of <s>bhakti</s> — that characterized by <s>sādhana</s> (practice) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) — which lead to devotion characterized by <s>prema</s> (divine love), beginning with "through authorities" (<s>pramāṇai</s>). "Through authorities" means through the scriptures of the Lord; "through the righteous conduct of the saints" means through the practices and observances of those saintly persons who belong to Him; "through practice of these" means through repeated and abundant [engagement with them]. "Enlightening the self by the self" means that one, being sheltered by the Lord, personally realizes one's own nature as a pure soul (<s>śuddha-jīva</s>); and from that, one attains the highest, pure devotion (<s>śuddhā bhakti</s>). And thus in the <s>Śruti-stava</s> —

children.text:
sva-kṛta-pureṣv amīṣv abahir-antara-saṃvaraṇaṃ
tava puruṣaṃ vadanty akhila-śakti-dhṛto 'ṃśa-kṛtam |
iti nṛ-gatiṃ vivicya kavayo nigamāvapanaṃ
bhavata upāsate 'ṅghrim abhavaṃ bhuvi viśvasitāḥ || [BhP 10.87.20] iti || 59 ||
children.translated_text: "In these bodies created by Yourself, which are covered neither externally nor internally, the wise declare <s>Puruṣa</s>, the bearer of all potencies, to be a partial manifestation. Having thus discerned the course of human life, the sages, trusting in You, worship Your lotus feet — the source of the <s>Vedas</s> and the destroyer of material existence — upon this earth" [<s>BhP</s> 10.87.20]. ‖ 59 ‖

children.text:
yasyāḥ śreyas-karaṃ nāsti yayā nirvṛtim āpnuyāt |
yā sādhayati mām eva bhaktiṃ tām eva sādhayet ||60|| // BrS_5.70 //
children.translated_text: "There is nothing more auspicious than that [devotion]; through it one attains supreme satisfaction (<s>nirvṛti</s>). That devotion which accomplishes Me alone — one should practice that very devotion." ‖ 60 ‖ // <s>BrS</s> 5.70 //

children.text: dharmān anyān parityajya mām ekaṃ bhaja viśvasan |
yādṛśī yādṛśī śraddhā siddhir bhavati tādṛśī || // BrS_5.71 //
children.translated_text: Whatever the nature of one's faith, such will be the nature of one's perfection (<s>siddhi</s>)." // <s>BrS</s> 5.71 //
"Abandoning all other <s>dharmas</s> (duties), worship Me alone with faith.

children.text:
kurvan nirantaraṃ karma loko 'yam anuvartate |
tenaiva karmaṇā dhyāyan māṃ parāṃ bhaktim icchati ||61|| // BrS_5.72 //
children.translated_text: "This world continues by performing action (<s>karma</s>) unceasingly. By that very action, meditating upon Me, one desires the supreme devotion (<s>parā bhakti</s>)." ‖ 61 ‖ // <s>BrS</s> 5.72 //

children.text:
punaḥ śuddhām eva sādhana-bhaktiṃ draḍhayann akāmair api tām eva
kuryād ity āha - dharmān anyān iti | tad uktaṃ -
children.translated_text: Further strengthening pure <s>sādhana-bhakti</s> (devotional practice), he says that even those who are free from desires (<s>akāma</s>) should perform that very [devotion] — beginning with "abandoning other duties" (<s>dharmān anyān</s>). As it is stated —

children.text:
akāmaḥ sarva-kāmo vā mokṣa-kāma udāra-dhīḥ |
tīvreṇa bhakti-yogena yajeta puruṣaṃ param || [BhP 2.3.10] iti || 61 ||
children.translated_text: "Whether one is free from desires (<s>akāma</s>), full of all desires (<s>sarva-kāma</s>), or desirous of liberation (<s>mokṣa-kāma</s>), if one is of noble intelligence, one should worship the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>) through intense <s>bhakti-yoga</s>" [<s>BhP</s> 2.3.10]. ‖ 61 ‖

children.text:
ahaṃ hi viśvasya carācarasya
bījaṃ pradhānaṃ prakṛtiḥ pumāṃś ca |
mayāhitaṃ teja idaṃ bibharṣi
vidhe vidhehi tvam atho jaganti ||62|| // BrS_5.73 //
children.translated_text: "I am indeed the seed, the foremost cause, the material nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>), and the person (<s>Pumān</s>) of this universe of moving and non-moving beings. O <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), the effulgence (<s>tejas</s>) that you bear has been placed in you by Me. Therefore, create the worlds!" ‖ 62 ‖ // <s>BrS</s> 5.73 //

children.text: tasmāt tava sisṛkṣāpi phaliṣyatīti sa-yuktikam āha - ahaṃ hīti | pradhānaṃ
śreṣṭhaṃ bījaṃ, pūrṇa-bhagavad-rūpaṃ prakṛtir avyaktaṃ, pumān tad-draṣṭā,
children.translated_text: the best seed, the form of the complete Lord (<s>pūrṇa-bhagavad-rūpa</s>); "<s>Prakṛti</s>" means the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>); "<s>Pumān</s>" is the seer of that [<s>Prakṛti</s>];

children.text: kiṃ bahunā tavam api mayā āhitaṃ arpitaṃ teja idaṃ bibharṣi, tasmāt tena
children.translated_text: what more need be said — you bear even this effulgence (<s>tejas</s>) that has been placed, bestowed by Me; therefore, by that

children.text: mat-tejasā jaganti sarvāṇi sthāvara-jaṅgamāni he vidhe hi kurv iti ||62||
children.translated_text: effulgence of Mine (<s>mat-tejas</s>), O <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), create all the worlds — both stationary and moving beings — thus is the meaning. ‖ 62 ‖
Therefore, He says with reasoning that "your desire to create will also bear fruit" — beginning with "I indeed" (<s>ahaṃ hi</s>). "The foremost" (<s>pradhāna</s>) means

children.text:
iti śrī-brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ mūla-sūtrākhyasya pañcamādhyāyasya
śrīla-śrīpāda-śrī-jīva-gosvāmi-kṛtā dig-darśanī nāmnī ṭīkā samāptā ||
children.translated_text: Thus concludes the commentary named <s>Dig-darśanī</s>, composed by the revered <s>Śrīla Śrīpāda Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī</s>, on the Fifth Chapter of the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>, known as the <s>Mūla-sūtra</s>.
